section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Drive more slowly.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Drive through deeper water.,d:Turn off traction control.
note: Hydroplaning is more likely at higher speeds on wet roads; slowing down helps tires channel water and maintain contact with the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far ahead should you look while driving to maintain safe awareness?
options: a:About 10 to 15 seconds ahead.,b:Only 100 to 150 yards ahead.,c:One to two blocks only.,d:Directly in front of the hood at all times.
note: Scanning 10–15 seconds down the road helps you anticipate hazards and avoid last-second maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle begins to skid, how should you steer?
options: a:Turn the wheel in the direction you want the vehicle to go.,b:Turn the wheel to keep the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the wheel opposite the direction of the skid.
note: If you skid, steer toward where you want the vehicle to go. When the car begins to straighten, correct steering to keep control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a tire suddenly blows out, what should you do with the steering and brakes?
options: a:Apply the brake and hold it.,b:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: Hold the steering wheel firmly to keep the vehicle straight, slow gradually by easing off the gas, and apply brakes lightly once the vehicle is under control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Your vehicle's blind spot is the area:
options: a:You cannot see without turning your head.,b:Directly behind your vehicle only.,c:Visible in your rearview mirror.,d:Inside the car behind the passenger seat.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; check them by turning your head to look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you stop along the road at night, what lighting should you use?
options: a:Keep your low-beam headlights on and turn on emergency flashers.,b:Turn off all lights to conserve battery.,c:Use parking lights only.
note: If you stop at night, turn on your emergency flashers and keep your low-beam headlights on so other road users can see your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What helps you avoid needing to make emergency stops in traffic?
options: a:Drive only in the right lane.,b:Look ahead and maintain a safe following distance.,c:Honk to make others aware of you.
note: Maintaining a safe following distance and scanning ahead allows you to react and avoid sudden emergency stops.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing from the right lane into the left on a multi-lane highway, what checks should you make?
options: a:Look over your left shoulder for traffic in your blind spot and check mirrors, then signal.,b:Look only in your side mirror and then change lanes.,c:Signal and look in your rearview mirror only.
note: Check mirrors and look over your left shoulder for vehicles in the blind spot; always signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Anything that requires you to which of the following could cause a crash?
options: a:Take your attention away from the task of driving.,b:Take your hands off the wheel only briefly.,c:Use your mirrors occasionally.
note: Any activity that diverts attention from driving, takes your eyes off the road, or your hands off the wheel is a dangerous distraction that can cause a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing on the left, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:When you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After roughly three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: You may return to the right lane when the passed vehicle's front is visible in your rearview mirror; always signal before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which type of roadway area tends to freeze first in cold weather?
options: a:Areas shaded by trees or buildings.,b:Flat open areas.,c:Roads in direct sunlight.
note: Shaded sections freeze sooner and stay icy longer because they get less sun and dry more slowly than exposed areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Faced with an oncoming car on your left and a bicyclist on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Pull onto the shoulder.,b:Split the difference.,c:Let the car pass and then pass the bike.
note: When multiple hazards exist, handle one at a time: allow the oncoming vehicle to pass before safely passing the bicyclist.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you want to turn left but oncoming traffic is heavy and the light is green, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Use the next intersection.,b:Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.,c:Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
note: If the light is green and it is safe, you may enter the intersection to wait for a gap in oncoming traffic to complete your left turn; do not block the crosswalk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When it starts to rain while you are driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive at the posted maximum speed.,c:Drive faster than surrounding traffic to get through the rain quickly.
note: Reduce speed when rain begins, turn on headlights for visibility, and pull over if visibility becomes too poor to continue safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a multilane, one-way street onto another one-way or multilane roadway, from which lane should you begin the turn?
options: a:The left lane.,b:The middle of the intersection.,c:The right lane.
note: When turning left from multilane or one-way streets, begin the turn from the leftmost lane designated for left turns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever legal to block an intersection?
options: a:If you entered the intersection on the green light.,b:During rush hour traffic.,c:Under no circumstances.
note: You may not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking an intersection is unlawful even if the light is green when you enter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your wheels go off the pavement, what should you do?
options: a:Ease off the accelerator, keep steering straight, slow down gradually, and return to the pavement when safe.,b:Grip the wheel and sharply steer back onto the pavement.,c:Brake hard immediately to bring the vehicle to a stop.
note: If your vehicle leaves the pavement, reduce speed gently by easing off the accelerator while staying straight; when safe, steer back onto the road. Do not make sudden, sharp turns to force the vehicle back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Pass with caution.,c:Do not pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to your lane means passing from your direction is prohibited; wait for a legal passing zone.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the roadway from a driveway, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop and proceed only when there are no pedestrians or vehicles approaching.,b:Must drive slowly so approaching vehicles can get out of your way.,c:Must honk your horn to alert pedestrians and drivers.
note: Stop before entering the roadway from a driveway, yield to approaching vehicles and pedestrians, and proceed only when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you be cautious when passing a bicycle?
options: a:Oncoming traffic may not see you pull out to pass the bike.,b:The bicycle always has the right-of-way.,c:You are moving slower than the bicycle.
note: Bicyclists may swerve to avoid hazards and oncoming traffic may not see you moving into its lane; give bicycles extra room.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On long highway trips, what helps prevent drowsiness?
options: a:Stopping at regular intervals to rest.,b:Turning up the radio.,c:Slowing down.
note: Schedule regular stops to rest and stretch to reduce drowsiness while driving long distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must a driver respond to a flashing red traffic signal?
options: a:Stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and proceed when safe.,b:Slow down and proceed without stopping.,c:Merge to the right and continue.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop; yield to other road users and go only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped at a railroad crossing with more than one track, when is it safe to proceed?
options: a:When you have a clear view of all tracks and there are no trains approaching.,b:As soon as one train passes on one track.,c:When the crossing lights stop flashing even if you cannot see down all tracks.
note: Wait until you can see clearly down all tracks before proceeding; another train may be approaching on a different track.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a single dashed yellow line between opposing lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may pass if it is safe to do so.,b:Both lanes travel in the same direction.,c:Drivers may not pass.
note: A single dashed yellow centerline indicates passing is allowed for vehicles in both directions when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does alcohol affect driving skills and judgment?
options: a:It harms both driving skills and judgment.,b:It helps driving skills but harms judgment.,c:It has no effect on either.
note: Alcohol impairs reaction time, vision, coordination, and judgment, making driving dangerous at any level of consumption.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is 'highway hypnosis' most likely caused by?
options: a:Staring at the roadway for long periods of time.,b:Frequent rest stops.,c:Too much sleep the night before your trip.
note: Highway hypnosis occurs when you stare ahead for long periods and stop actively scanning; take breaks and stay mentally alert to avoid zoning out.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Two solid white lines across a lane mark what?
options: a:The boundaries of a crosswalk where pedestrians should be given the right-of-way.,b:That motor vehicles have priority over pedestrians.,c:That no one has the right-of-way.
note: Two solid white lines across a lane typically mark a crosswalk; drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the effect of driving while distracted by activities such as phone use?
options: a:It usually causes the driver to react more slowly to hazards.,b:It typically improves driver awareness.,c:It causes drivers to drive faster intentionally.
note: Distracted driving slows reaction time and reduces the ability to perceive and respond to road hazards, increasing crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A vehicle is hydroplaning when what occurs?
options: a:Its tires lose contact with the road surface and the vehicle rides on water.,b:The windshield wipers cannot keep the windshield clear.,c:Spray from a large truck reduces visibility.
note: Hydroplaning happens when tires ride on a layer of water, causing loss of steering and braking control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On slippery roads, how should you adjust your following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance (stay farther back).,b:Keep the same distance as normal.,c:Follow closer to the car ahead.
note: Slippery surfaces require longer stopping distances; maintain extra space between you and the vehicle ahead.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your view to the side at an intersection is blocked, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways without stopping.,c:Maintain speed and look both ways.
note: When sight lines are obstructed, stop and inch forward until you have a clear view before entering the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factor commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit and driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Careful scanning of the environment.
note: Driving too fast for posted speeds or conditions is a frequent cause of crashes; maintain appropriate speed for conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving on major highways, what should you remember?
options: a:Stay alert and ready to react to hazards.,b:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead to maintain concentration.,c:Avoid checking mirrors to reduce distraction.
note: Highway driving requires alertness and scanning to avoid highway hypnosis and to respond to unexpected hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a driver's left arm and hand are extended downward, what does that signal mean?
options: a:Turn left.,b:Stop.,c:Turn right.
note: A downward left-arm signal indicates the driver intends to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you begin to slow down for a highway exit?
options: a:After you have moved into the exit lane.,b:On the main road just before the exit lane.,c:Only when you see a toll booth.
note: Get into the exit lane well in advance and begin to slow down after you are fully in the exit lane, following any posted advisory speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which behavior describes a good defensive driver?
options: a:Drives slowly at all times.,b:Looks out for the actions of other drivers.,c:Travels at a constant speed.
note: A defensive driver anticipates other drivers' actions, scans the road for hazards, and plans safe reactions rather than relying solely on their own speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times when necessary to prevent hitting them, even if they ignore traffic laws.,b:Only in a marked crosswalk.,c:Only when traffic signals favor the pedestrian.,d:Only when a police officer is present.
note: Always do everything possible to avoid striking a pedestrian, regardless of whether they are obeying traffic laws.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until you can pass through completely.,b:Get as close as possible to the vehicle ahead so you can go next.,c:Enter the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.,d:Honk to move traffic along.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can clear it without blocking cross traffic; wait until traffic ahead moves.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement accurately describes alcohol's effect on driving?
options: a:Alcohol impairs judgment, which is essential for safe driving.,b:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,c:Being under the legal BAC limit guarantees unimpaired driving.
note: Alcohol reduces judgment, which is needed to perceive and react to road hazards. Even small amounts can affect driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on an interstate expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Stop and make a U-turn.,b:Get off at the next exit and come back to the exit you missed.,c:Roll down your window and ask the driver next to you for help.
note: Do not back up or make a U-turn on the highway. Continue to the next exit and safely return to the missed exit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a transit vehicle is signaling to reenter the main roadway after a stop, you must:
options: a:Hon k to let them reenter.,b:Move to the left lane immediately.,c:Yield and allow it to merge safely.
note: Yield to transit vehicles re-entering traffic after a stop by changing lanes or slowing as necessary to let them merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does it mean when lanes are separated by double solid yellow lines?
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is allowed from either direction when safe.,c:You may pass from the left only.,d:You may cross the lines to make a U-turn anywhere.
note: Double solid yellow lines mark opposing traffic lanes; passing is prohibited for traffic in both directions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see an approaching emergency vehicle using flashing lights, what must you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane until the vehicle has passed.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until the vehicle has passed.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed.
note: Pull over to the right edge of the road, stop, and remain stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed; on one-way streets move to the nearest edge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When stopped on an uphill slope, why should you allow a larger space cushion in front of you?
options: a:At an intersection.,b:On an incline, to allow for a vehicle ahead that may roll back.,c:At a stop sign.
note: Allow more space when stopped on an uphill grade because the vehicle ahead may roll backward when traffic starts moving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do two solid yellow lines in the center of the road mean?
options: a:Passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction.,b:Passing is allowed for drivers in both directions.,c:Passing is allowed only when going downhill.
note: Two solid yellow centerlines indicate opposite-direction traffic and prohibit passing from either side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless otherwise posted, what is the maximum speed limit in a school zone where children or crossing guards are present?
options: a:10 mph,b:15 mph,c:20 mph
note: Unless signs indicate otherwise, the maximum speed limit in a school zone with children or crossing guards present is 15 mph.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the only effective method to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Exercise.,c:Allow your body time to get rid of the alcohol.
note: Only time allows your body to metabolize alcohol; coffee, exercise, and other remedies do not reduce BAC.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, what should you check?
options: a:Rearview mirror and side mirror, then glance quickly over your shoulder for blind spots.,b:Only the side view mirror.,c:Only the inside mirror.,d:Nothing; trust other drivers to avoid you.
note: Check mirrors for approaching traffic, then look over your shoulder just before changing lanes to ensure it is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: While driving in fog or other low-visibility conditions, what should you do about headlights?
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your high beams to see further.,c:Increase speed to clear the area quickly.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams will reflect off moisture and reduce visibility. If visibility is too poor, pull off the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles enter an intersection from different highways at the same time, which vehicle must yield?
options: a:The vehicle on the left.,b:Either one.,c:The vehicle on the right.
note: When two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and remain in your vehicle if possible.,b:Get out of the vehicle and stand near the rear to warn approaching cars.,c:Flag down the first vehicle that passes for assistance.
note: If you must stop on an interstate, move completely off the travel lanes onto the shoulder if possible, turn on your hazard flashers so others can see you, and stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt on. Walking or standing near high‑speed traffic is extremely dangerous and should be avoided unless you must exit for immediate safety (such as fire or smoke).

question: When must you stop for a school bus on a two-lane highway?
options: a:Only if it is stopped in your lane and you are traveling in the same direction.,b:When the bus is parked on the shoulder and has no students.,c:If you and the bus are on a two-lane highway and its red lights are flashing.
note: On a two‑lane road with no physical divider, traffic in both directions must stop when a school bus has its red lights flashing and/or stop arm extended. You must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus moves or the driver signals you to proceed.

question: On wet pavement, which should you keep in mind?
options: a:Wet roads increase the chance of hydroplaning.,b:Road surfaces are most slippery just after rain begins.,c:Give extra stopping distance than usual.,d:All of the above.
note: On wet pavement you should remember all of the following: wet roads increase the risk of hydroplaning, roads are often most slippery just after rain begins because oil and dirt rise to the surface, and you must allow extra following and stopping distance. Slow down and increase your space cushion to maintain control.

question: What can happen to bicyclists who disobey traffic laws?
options: a:They can be ticketed.,b:They are exempt from traffic laws.,c:They always get a warning instead of a ticket.
note: Bicyclists using the roadway generally have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers of motor vehicles. They must obey traffic signals, signs, and lane markings, and they can be stopped and ticketed for violations such as running red lights or stop signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive faster than other vehicles on a two-lane road and keep passing, what is likely to happen?
options: a:Help prevent traffic congestion.,b:Increase your chances of a collision.,c:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.
note: Frequently driving faster than surrounding traffic and repeatedly passing on a two‑lane road greatly increases your risk of a head‑on or side‑swipe collision. Each pass exposes you to oncoming traffic and limited visibility. Safe drivers adjust their speed to the flow of traffic within the speed limit and avoid unnecessary passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway, what should you generally do?
options: a:Check for cars and adjust your speed to merge smoothly using the acceleration lane.,b:Check for cars and reduce speed to 25 mph before entering.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a large gap.
note: When entering an interstate, you should use the entrance/acceleration lane to check for traffic, signal, and adjust your speed to match the flow of vehicles on the highway. Do not stop in the acceleration lane unless absolutely necessary, and do not slow to very low speeds before merging, because that makes it harder and more dangerous to enter traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may proceed through an intersection with a yellow light under which circumstance?
options: a:There are pedestrians crossing.,b:You are turning right.,c:There is an emergency vehicle crossing your lane.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should stop if you can do so safely. You may proceed only if you are so close to the intersection when it turns yellow that stopping suddenly would be unsafe. You must not enter or continue just because there are pedestrians, you are turning right, or an emergency vehicle is crossing; in those cases you still follow the normal rule: stop on yellow if it is safe, or clear the intersection if you are already in it.

question: What color are construction and maintenance temporary signs and markings?
options: a:Yellow background with blue writing.,b:Blue background with white writing.,c:Orange background with black writing.,d:Red background with green writing.
note: Construction and maintenance work-zone signs are typically orange with black letters or symbols. This color combination alerts drivers that they are entering a temporary work area and should slow down, be prepared for lane shifts, and watch for workers and equipment.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic light mean?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and wait for a green light.,c:Stop and look for other vehicles, then go if there is no traffic.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you should be prepared to yield and watch carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or other hazards in or approaching the intersection.

question: If pedestrians cross illegally in the middle of the street, what must you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and continue.,b:Do not stop for them.,c:Yield and stop for them.
note: Even if pedestrians are crossing illegally (jaywalking), you must yield and be prepared to stop to avoid hitting them. Drivers are always responsible for using due care to prevent collisions with pedestrians, regardless of who has the right-of-way.

question: On a road without sidewalks, where should pedestrians walk?
options: a:Side of the road facing oncoming traffic.,b:Same side of the road on which traffic is moving.,c:Side of the road which has the lightest traffic.
note: On roads without sidewalks, pedestrians should walk on the side facing oncoming traffic. This lets them see approaching vehicles and react quickly if a driver drifts toward the edge of the road, which improves their safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should not:
options: a:Continue on the freeway and find an alternate route to your destination.,b:Proceed to the next exit,c:Back up on the road or shoulder.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, never back up on the travel lane or shoulder. Instead, continue to the next exit, leave the freeway safely, and then find an alternate route to your destination.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Having many passengers.,b:Erratic and improper lane changes.,c:Using cruise control.,d:Driving consistently under the speed limit.
note: Erratic and improper lane changes are a common sign of aggressive driving. Drivers who weave through traffic, cut others off, or change lanes without signaling create unsafe conditions and should be given extra space.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what is the best initial action?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and move out of the traffic lane.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge of the roadway.
note: When a tire blows out, keep a firm grip on the steering wheel, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Once you have control and your speed has dropped, carefully move out of the traffic lane to a safe place. Avoid hard braking or sudden steering, which can cause loss of control.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what should you do first?
options: a:Shift into park immediately.,b:Shift into neutral and apply steady pressure on the brake.,c:Reach down and attempt to lift the accelerator with your hand.
note: If the accelerator sticks, keep looking at the road, shift the transmission into neutral, and apply steady pressure on the brake. Steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place, then turn off the engine. Do not turn off the ignition or shift into park while moving, as this can cause loss of control.

question: What does a diamond-shaped traffic sign indicate?
options: a:Warns of existing or possible hazards.,b:Alerts drivers to school zones.,c:Alerts drivers to public recreation areas.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are general warning signs. They are usually yellow or orange and alert drivers to existing or possible hazards or special conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, or road work. School zones and recreation areas have their own specific sign shapes and symbols.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you?
options: a:Every two to four seconds.,b:Every six to eight seconds.,c:Every four to six seconds.
note: Good defensive driving includes checking your mirrors regularly so you know what is happening behind you. Many state manuals recommend glancing at your rearview mirror about every six to eight seconds, and more often in heavy traffic. This helps you react early to vehicles approaching quickly or changing lanes.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, where should you look?
options: a:Look straight ahead.,b:Look toward the right side of the road.,c:Look toward the center of the roadway.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim their high beams, avoid looking directly at the bright lights. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road. This reduces glare, helps you maintain your lane position, and lets your eyes adjust so you can still see the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach an intersection and the light turns from green to yellow, what is the best action?
options: a:Come to a stop in the center of the intersection.,b:Speed up to beat the red.,c:Be prepared to stop; stop if you can do so safely.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and be prepared to stop. If you can stop safely before entering the intersection, you must do so; if you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through with caution.

question: In which situations should you reduce your speed?
options: a:On narrow or winding roads.,b:At intersections or railroad crossings.,c:When the road is wet or slippery.,d:All of the above
note: You must reduce speed whenever conditions make normal speeds unsafe. This includes narrow or winding roads, intersections and railroad crossings where cross traffic may appear, and any time the road is wet, icy, or otherwise slippery. Slowing down gives you more time and distance to react.

question: A blood alcohol concentration increase of 0.02 percent results in what change to crash risk?
options: a:It makes driving safer.,b:It halves the crash risk.,c:It nearly doubles a driver's chance of being in a fatal crash.,d:It has no measurable effect.
note: Even a small increase in blood alcohol concentration (BAC) greatly raises crash risk. Research shows that for drivers around age 21–34, each 0.02% increase in BAC can nearly double the risk of being involved in a fatal crash. This is why it is unsafe to drive after drinking at any level, not just at or above the legal limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it permissible to cross solid yellow centerlines?
options: a:During daylight hours only.,b:Any time you want to pass.,c:Only when you are making a turn or entering/exiting a driveway where it is legal and safe.
note: A solid yellow centerline means you should not cross it to pass other vehicles. However, you may cross a solid yellow line when you are making a lawful turn (such as turning left into a driveway or side road), as long as it is safe and not otherwise prohibited by signs or markings.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking between two vehicles, what should you do first?
options: a:Pull up even with the car in front of the parking space, then begin backing in.,b:Turn your wheels to the left immediately.,c:Turn your wheels to the right immediately.
note: For standard parallel parking, after you signal and check traffic, you pull up alongside and even with the vehicle in front of the space, leaving a safe gap. From that position you begin backing slowly while turning the wheel as needed to angle into the space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who moves first?
options: a:The driver on your right,b:The drivers who arrived before you, in order of arrival; if you arrive at the same time as another driver, the one on the right goes first.,c:The driver on your left
note: At a four‑way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive: the first vehicle to stop goes first. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right‑of‑way. If drivers arrive exactly together facing each other and one is turning left, the driver going straight has the right‑of‑way.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the default maximum speed limit in outlying parts of cities and villages when no speed is posted?
options: a:45 mph.,b:25 mph.,c:35 mph.
note: In many states, including Wisconsin and several others, when no speed limit is posted in outlying parts of cities and villages, the default maximum speed limit is 35 mph. Drivers must still adjust speed for conditions, but may not exceed this statutory limit unless signs indicate otherwise.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do about following distance?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Speed up to get off the road sooner.,c:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.
note: When visibility is reduced by rain, fog, snow, or darkness, you need more time and space to see hazards and react safely. Increasing your following distance gives you a larger safety cushion so you can brake or steer smoothly if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

question: When must drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.,b:At all times.,c:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks, regardless of whether the pedestrian is distracted or signals to the driver. You must slow or stop as needed so pedestrians can cross safely and may proceed only when the crosswalk is clear.

question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?
options: a:Brake abruptly to get attention.,b:Check mirrors only after stopping.,c:Avoid sudden stops by releasing the gas early and braking smoothly.
note: Rear-end collisions are often caused by sudden, hard braking. By easing off the accelerator early and then braking smoothly, you give drivers behind you more time to see your brake lights and slow down, which helps prevent them from crashing into the back of your vehicle.

question: A solid white edge line that slants toward the left indicates what about the road ahead?
options: a:There is an intersection just ahead.,b:You will be required to turn left ahead.,c:The road becomes narrower ahead.
note: A solid white edge line marks the outer edge of the roadway. When this line angles toward the center of the road, it warns that the usable roadway is narrowing ahead. You should reduce speed and be prepared for less space to maneuver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to change lanes, which actions are important?
options: a:Change lanes quickly without checking mirrors.,b:Only signal at the last second.,c:Signal in advance, check mirrors and blind spots, and ensure the lane is clear before changing.
note: Before changing lanes, signal well in advance to alert other drivers, then check your mirrors and blind spots and make sure there is enough space in the lane you want to enter. Move over smoothly and avoid sudden or last-second lane changes.

question: When are streets and highways most slippery?
options: a:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,b:When they are clean and dry.,c:Just after it starts to rain.
note: Streets and highways are usually most slippery just after it starts to rain. Oil and other residues build up on the road during dry periods; when the first rain falls, this mixture rises to the surface and reduces traction until it is washed away by continued rainfall.

question: When driving at night, what is a key safety action?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
note: At night your visibility and depth perception are reduced, so you should increase your following distance to give yourself more time to react. Use high beams only when appropriate and switch to low beams when you are following another vehicle or when there is oncoming traffic to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while you're driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Hold the steering wheel firmly and slow to a stop.,c:Keep driving normally.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease off the accelerator to slow down gradually, then when the vehicle is under control and speed has dropped, apply the brakes gently and steer to a safe place off the road.

question: What do crossbuck signs indicate?
options: a:Railroad crossings.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A crossbuck sign marks a railroad crossing. It means you are approaching train tracks and must look and listen for trains, be prepared to stop, and yield the right-of-way to any approaching train.

question: What usually causes hydroplaning?
options: a:Sudden stops.,b:Driving too fast on a wet road so tires cannot clear water.,c:Excessive stops.
note: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on a wet road and your tires ride up on a layer of water instead of gripping the pavement. Because the tires cannot push the water aside, you lose traction and can lose steering and braking control.

question: When following another vehicle, you should allow extra space behind which type of vehicle?
options: a:Passenger vehicle.,b:Motorcycle.,c:Station wagon.
note: You should allow extra following distance behind motorcycles. Motorcycles can stop and maneuver more quickly than larger vehicles, and they are less visible and more vulnerable in a collision. Leaving more space gives you more time to react if the rider slows or stops suddenly.

question: When preparing to exit an interstate, when is the proper time to begin slowing down?
options: a:As you approach the deceleration lane.,b:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,c:About halfway through the deceleration lane.
note: On an interstate, maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane. Once you are in the deceleration lane, begin slowing to the advisory or posted speed for the exit ramp. Do not slow significantly on the main travel lanes, because that can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: What does a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line mean for drivers?
options: a:Drivers next to the broken line may pass; drivers next to the solid line may not.,b:Driving in both directions may pass.,c:Drivers next to the solid line may pass.
note: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means that passing is allowed only for drivers on the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid line must not pass. This marking is used where passing is safe in one direction but not the other.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and a driver on your left reach a four-way stop at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.,b:Whoever is signaling to make a turn has the right-of-way.,c:The vehicle to your right has the right-of-way (you go before the driver on your left).
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the right has the right-of-way. If the other vehicle is on your left, you are on the right, so you may proceed first after stopping and making sure it is safe.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Releasing your seat belt.,b:Bracing yourself and pressing your head against the head restraint.,c:Keeping a firm grip on the steering wheel.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep your seat belt fastened. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and keep a firm grip on the steering wheel. The seat belt and head restraint help reduce the risk of whiplash and other injuries in a rear-end collision.

question: Which category of drug best describes alcohol?
options: a:An antihistamine.,b:A stimulant.,c:A depressant.
note: Alcohol is classified as a depressant because it slows down the central nervous system. This slowing affects reaction time, coordination, and judgment, all of which are critical for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you legally pass another vehicle on the right?
options: a:On a narrow bridge.,b:If the vehicle is waiting to turn left and there is an available lane to pass on the right.,c:Even if it means driving off the pavement.
note: You may pass on the right only when the vehicle ahead is making or about to make a left turn and there is a clearly marked lane or enough paved roadway to do so safely without leaving the pavement. You must never drive off the roadway or onto the shoulder to pass.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing that has no flashing lights or gates, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Cross immediately and quickly.,b:Yield to a train and only proceed when the entire vehicle can clear the tracks.,c:Always stop before crossing.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop. You must yield to any approaching train and only proceed when you are sure it is safe and your entire vehicle can clear all tracks without stopping on them.

question: What best ensures safety when you intend to back up a vehicle?
options: a:Honk your horn right before shifting into reverse.,b:Check behind the vehicle before you get into the driver's seat.,c:Check your rearview mirrors to see what is behind you.
note: Before backing, walk behind your vehicle to check for children, pets, or objects that may be hidden from your mirrors. Then back up slowly while looking over your shoulder and using your mirrors. Mirrors alone do not show all blind spots behind the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, what should you do?
options: a:Blow your horn to warn oncoming traffic.,b:Enter quickly to merge smoothly.,c:Pull partially onto the roadway to check for traffic.,d:Yield to pedestrians and traffic already on the roadway.
note: When entering a roadway from a private road or driveway, you must stop if necessary and yield to all pedestrians and vehicles already on the roadway. Do not pull out until you can enter safely without forcing others to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: What does a single broken white line between lanes indicate?
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.,b:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,c:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may change lanes or pass across this line when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

question: What is the safest way to prevent hydroplaning in wet weather?
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Put on cruise control.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a thin layer of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to prevent this is to slow down in wet conditions and avoid sudden steering or braking. Do not use cruise control on wet roads, because you need full control of your speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it appropriate to drive at the posted maximum speed limit?
options: a:Only at night.,b:During the day.,c:Only under ideal driving conditions.
note: The posted maximum speed is the fastest you may legally drive only when conditions are ideal—good visibility, dry pavement, light traffic, and a safe vehicle. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or other hazards, you must drive slower than the posted maximum.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane of an expressway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Move to the lane on your left.,b:Move to the lane on your right.,c:Stay in the center lane.
note: On multi-lane highways, the right lane is generally for slower traffic, and the left lane is for passing. If vehicles are passing you on both sides while you are in the center lane, you are likely going slower than the flow of traffic and should move safely to the right lane when possible.

question: When should you increase your following distance?
options: a:When exiting an expressway.,b:When following a motorcycle closely in good conditions.,c:When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your vision.
note: You should increase your following distance whenever your view is blocked, conditions are poor, or you are behind more vulnerable road users. Large vehicles can block your view of the road ahead, so leaving extra space gives you more time to react to hazards.

question: Collisions are more likely to occur under which condition?
options: a:One lane of traffic is traveling faster than the other lanes.,b:All vehicles are traveling at about the same speed.,c:One vehicle is traveling faster or slower than the flow of traffic.
note: Collisions are more likely when one vehicle is moving much faster or much slower than the surrounding traffic. Large speed differences increase lane changes, sudden braking, and closing speeds, which all raise crash risk. When safe and legal, you should travel at about the same speed as the flow of traffic, within the speed limit.

question: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights of an emergency vehicle, you must:
options: a:Speed up and clear the area.,b:Signal the emergency vehicle to pass.,c:Drive to the right side of the road and stop.,d:Slow down but remain in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using a siren and/or flashing lights, you must yield the right-of-way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop until the vehicle has passed, unless directed otherwise by a police officer. Do not speed up, stop in the middle of your lane, or block intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you hear or see an approaching emergency vehicle, what is the proper response?
options: a:Drive as far to the right as safely possible and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the lane you are in.,c:Proceed slowly and allow it to pass without pulling over.
note: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or siren on, you must pull as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stop until it passes. Do not stop in an intersection; if you are in one, clear the intersection first, then pull over and stop.

question: What is a “No zone” around large vehicles?
options: a:A one-way traffic area.,b:A designated no-passing zone.,c:The blind spot of a large vehicle.
note: A "No Zone" is the large blind spot area around trucks and other large vehicles where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. If you drive in these areas, the truck driver may not know you are there, increasing the risk of a collision. Avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a red light, when may you turn right?
options: a:When the cross traffic has cleared.,b:After you stop.,c:Both of the above.
note: Unless a sign forbids it, you may turn right on red after coming to a complete stop and yielding to traffic, pedestrians, and bicyclists.

question: There is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead. What must you do?
options: a:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.,b:Make eye contact with and then pass the pedestrian.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.
note: Even when there is no marked crosswalk you must yield to pedestrians crossing your lane and allow them to finish crossing safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection at the posted speed and the signal turns yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Stop before entering if you can do so safely; otherwise proceed through carefully.,b:Speed up to cross before red.,c:Cross the intersection without caution.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when it turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution.

question: When checking the blind spot to change lanes left, you should glance:
options: a:Over your right shoulder.,b:Only at your side mirror.,c:Over your left shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes to the left, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your left shoulder. This head check lets you see the blind spot that mirrors cannot show, helping you avoid vehicles beside you.

question: If an oncoming car's headlights are very bright at night, what should you do?
options: a:Stop until the car passes.,b:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look directly below their headlights.
note: Bright oncoming headlights can temporarily blind you if you look directly at them. Instead, glance toward the right edge of your lane or the right side of the road to guide your path until the vehicle passes, while still keeping track of your lane position.

question: Does drinking coffee after consuming alcohol lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:No — it has no effect on BAC.,b:Yes — it decreases BAC.,c:Yes — it cancels alcohol's effects.
note: Coffee may make you feel more awake but does not reduce the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream or your impairment.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When a traffic light turns green, what must you still yield to?
options: a:Pedestrians and any traffic already in the intersection.,b:No one; you have the right-of-way.,c:Other vehicles only.
note: A green light means you are permitted to go, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and any vehicles already in the intersection. Traffic that entered on a previous signal or is still clearing the intersection has the right-of-way, and you must wait until it is safe before proceeding.

question: If you are about to be struck from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.,b:Applying your brakes.,c:Letting go of the steering wheel.
note: If you are about to be hit from the rear, keep both hands on the steering wheel so you can maintain control of the vehicle. Press your head firmly against the head restraint and be ready to apply the brakes after impact if needed. Letting go of the steering wheel can cause you to lose control and increase the risk of injury or a secondary crash.

question: When should you allow extra following distance behind a vehicle?
options: a:Your car is cold.,b:There are no vehicles behind you.,c:You are following a motorcycle.
note: You should allow extra following distance when driving behind a motorcycle. Motorcycles are smaller, can stop more quickly, and are more vulnerable to road hazards. Leaving more space gives you extra time to react if the rider slows, stops suddenly, or loses control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Whose instructions must drivers obey at a construction site?
options: a:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,b:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.,c:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.
note: At construction and road work zones, you must obey the instructions of flaggers and other authorized traffic control workers. Their directions can temporarily override signs or signals to keep traffic moving safely around workers, equipment, and lane closures.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an emergency vehicle stopped with flashing lights on the roadside, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and, if possible, change lanes to avoid driving next to the stopped vehicle.,b:Drive to the right side of the road and stop immediately.,c:Continue at the same speed in your lane.
note: When an emergency, tow, or roadside assistance vehicle is stopped with flashing lights, move over a lane if safe; if you cannot change lanes, slow to a safe speed below the limit.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes or passing, you should:
options: a:Change lanes without checking mirrors if you can see enough.,b:Signal only after you begin the lane change.,c:Signal your intention and check mirrors and blind spots.
note: Before changing lanes or passing, always signal first, then check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Never change lanes without checking, and always signal before you start moving into another lane.

question: How can you ensure your physical condition won't make driving unsafe?
options: a:Know the effects of any medicine on your driving ability and drive within your limitations.,b:Always drive faster to stay alert.,c:Skip regular health checks.,d:Drive only at night.
note: You are responsible for making sure your health and any medications you take do not make driving unsafe. Know how medicines affect you, avoid driving when you are ill, tired, or impaired, and always drive within your physical limitations.

question: Which of the following will lower blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat,b:Drinking caffeine,c:Time
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol; food, coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not speed this up. If you have been drinking, the only way to become sober enough to drive is to wait until your BAC has gone down over time.

question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas you cannot see using a vehicle’s mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices that block your view.
note: Blind spots are areas around your vehicle that you cannot see in your mirrors. They are usually along the sides and slightly to the rear. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly turn your head to check these areas in addition to using your mirrors.

question: To be able to turn quickly and safely, how should you position your hands on the steering wheel?
options: a:Next to each other on the top of the wheel.,b:On opposite sides of the wheel (such as the 9 and 3 o’clock positions).,c:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.
note: For good control and the ability to turn quickly and safely, place your hands on opposite sides of the steering wheel, typically around the 9 and 3 o’clock positions. This gives you better leverage and stability than holding the top or top-and-bottom of the wheel.

question: If a driver behind you wants to pass, how should you respond?
options: a:Maintain the same speed.,b:Speed up to prevent the pass.,c:Slow down to allow room for the passing maneuver.
note: If a driver behind you wants to pass, you should help them do it safely. Slightly reduce your speed to create more space in front of your vehicle so the passing driver has room to move back into the lane. Never speed up to block a pass, as that increases risk and can be illegal.

question: When approaching a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Proceed normally because the pedestrian will hear you.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop; yield the right-of-way.,c:Sound your horn to alert them.,d:Take the right-of-way so you don't block traffic.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the right-of-way. You must slow down, be prepared to stop, and yield so they can cross safely. Do not honk or try to force your way through; sudden sounds can be confusing and dangerous for someone relying on hearing and their guide dog.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parallel parking facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn your wheels away from the curb.,b:Turn your wheels sharply toward the side of the road.,c:Keep your wheels straight.
note: When parking facing downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road. If the vehicle rolls, it will move toward the curb instead of into traffic. On an uphill with a curb, you turn the wheels away from the curb; on a hill with no curb, you generally turn the wheels toward the edge of the road.

question: Coming to a complete stop and yielding to cross traffic and pedestrians corresponds with which type of signal?
options: a:A solid red light.,b:A flashing yellow light.,c:A flashing red light.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe. A flashing yellow means proceed with caution without stopping if the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady green traffic light allow you to do?
options: a:Always yield to all traffic even if the light is green.,b:Stop and check for cross traffic before moving.,c:Proceed through the intersection if the way is clear.
note: A steady green light means you may go straight or turn, if not prohibited, but only if the intersection is clear. You must still yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and to oncoming traffic when turning left. Green never means go without checking; it means you have the right to proceed when it is safe.

question: Which statement about using feet to operate pedals is correct?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,c:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and the brake. This helps you avoid accidentally pressing both pedals at once and gives you better control for smooth, safe stops and starts.

question: What is important to know about large trucks?
options: a:They need less room to maneuver than passenger vehicles.,b:They have large blind spots and need more room to maneuver and stop.,c:They can stop more quickly than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots on all sides and need more space to turn, change lanes, and stop. Because of their size and weight, they cannot maneuver or stop as quickly as smaller passenger vehicles, so you should give them extra room.

question: A pentagon-shaped traffic sign indicates:
options: a:A regulatory speed sign.,b:A stop requirement.,c:A school zone or school crossing.,d:A yield ahead warning.
note: Pentagon-shaped (five-sided) signs are used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, be prepared to slow down and watch carefully for children and crossing guards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Large trucks tend to slow down under which condition?
options: a:When descending long or steep hills.,b:When driving through long tunnels.,c:When climbing long or steep hills.
note: Large, heavy trucks usually lose speed when climbing long or steep hills because their weight makes it harder to accelerate uphill. When following a truck on an upgrade, expect it to slow down and allow extra space so you can react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When traffic is moving at 50–55 mph, when are you least likely to have an accident?
options: a:If you drive much slower than other traffic.,b:If you drive a few miles per hour faster than others.,c:If you stay within the same speed range as most other vehicles.,d:If you drive in the leftmost lane only.
note: You are least likely to be in a collision when you travel at about the same speed as surrounding traffic, as long as you stay within the posted speed limit. Large speed differences—either much faster or much slower than other vehicles—increase the chance of conflicts and crashes.

question: If other drivers around you are acting angrily, what should you do?
options: a:Confront them to resolve the issue.,b:React with similar gestures to defend yourself.,c:Distance yourself from them and avoid eye contact or gestures.
note: When other drivers act aggressively, the safest response is to avoid any interaction. Do not make eye contact, respond with gestures, or try to confront them. Instead, create space by slowing slightly or changing lanes when safe, and focus on your own driving so the situation does not escalate.

question: What does a diamond-shaped sign indicate?
options: a:Stop.,b:Warning.,c:Yield.
note: Diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to hazards or changes in road conditions ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or work zones. They are usually yellow for general warnings or orange in construction and maintenance areas.

question: How can you keep track of traffic behind you?
options: a:Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots at all times.,b:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,c:Turn and look out your back window for long periods.
note: To stay aware of traffic behind you, check your mirrors regularly—about every few seconds and before changing lanes, slowing, or stopping. This helps you notice fast-approaching vehicles, tailgaters, or emergency vehicles so you can adjust safely. Do not stare backward for long periods, as this takes your attention off the road ahead.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases, how are you affected?
options: a:You become more coordinated.,b:You become more sober.,c:You become more intoxicated and impaired.
note: As your BAC increases, alcohol slows your brain and body. Your judgment, coordination, vision, and reaction time all get worse, even at relatively low BAC levels. The higher the BAC, the more impaired you become and the more dangerous it is to drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic in opposite directions, when should you return to your lane?
options: a:Remain in the left lane if you intend to turn left.,b:Return to the driving lane when there's enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.,c:Return to the right side of the roadway immediately.
note: When passing on a two-lane road, move back into your lane only when you are safely ahead of the vehicle you passed. A good rule is to wait until you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle (including its front bumper) in your rearview mirror and there is plenty of space before returning to your lane.

question: If you are under 18, which is required to get a probationary license?
options: a:Hold an instruction permit for at least six months.,b:Be free of moving violations for the prior six months.,c:Complete an approved driver education course.,d:All of the above.
note: For drivers under 18, a probationary license typically requires completing an approved driver education course, holding an instruction permit for a minimum period (often six months), having no moving violations for a set period before applying, completing required supervised driving hours, passing the driving test, and paying the required fees. All listed options are part of the usual requirements, so the correct choice should be that all of them are required.

question: What does a 'No passing zone' sign tell drivers?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign means you must not pass other vehicles in that area. Passing is illegal and unsafe there, usually because of limited sight distance, hills, curves, or other hazards. You must stay in your lane and wait until you are past the no-passing zone before attempting to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you face a green light but pedestrians are in the intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Proceed because you have the right-of-way.,b:Yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,c:Sound your horn to make pedestrians move.
note: When you have a green light, you may go only if the intersection is clear. Pedestrians already in the crosswalk have the right-of-way, and you must wait until they have safely crossed before proceeding, even if your light is green.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is a U-turn prohibited?
options: a:On a straight roadway with clear view for 500 feet both directions.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On or near any curve or hill where you cannot be seen by oncoming traffic.
note: U-turns are generally prohibited on or near curves or hills where other drivers cannot see you in time. Limited visibility makes it dangerous for oncoming traffic, so you must wait until you are in a place with a clear view and where U-turns are allowed by law and signs.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a steady yellow traffic light indicate?
options: a:Go immediately.,b:Slow down and prepare to stop because the light will soon turn red.,c:Yield to other cars only.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop before entering the intersection, unless you are so close that stopping suddenly would be unsafe. It is not a signal to speed up.

question: At dawn, dusk, or in precipitation, what should you do to be more visible to others?
options: a:Use parking lights.,b:Turn up the instrument panel lights.,c:Turn on your headlights (low beams).
note: Use low-beam headlights at dawn, dusk, and in rain, snow, or fog so other drivers can see you more easily. Parking lights or bright instrument panel lights do not improve your visibility to others and can even make it harder for you to see outside.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Wait for a green light before going.,b:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. Treat it as a warning that other traffic may be entering the intersection.

question: When is it legal to drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:When the warning lights are not flashing.,b:When you can clearly see both directions.,c:Never.
note: You must never drive around or under a lowered railroad gate. Trains cannot stop quickly, and signals may activate before you can see the train. Always wait until the lights stop flashing, the gates are fully raised, and you are sure the tracks are clear.

question: On roadways, bicycles are legally considered what?
options: a:Vehicles subject to the same rules as motor vehicles.,b:Hazards that must yield to cars.,c:Objects that are not covered by traffic laws.
note: Bicycles on the roadway are treated as vehicles. Bicyclists generally must obey the same traffic signals, signs, and right‑of‑way rules as drivers, and drivers must treat bicycles as legitimate traffic, giving them space and yielding when required.

question: Guide signs that provide directions and mileage are normally what color?
options: a:Yellow.,b:Green.,c:Red.
note: Guide and destination signs that show directions, routes, and distances are typically green with white lettering. These signs help you navigate to cities, exits, and points of interest along the highway.

question: What is the only medically proven method of removing alcohol or drug effects from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Give your body time.,c:Breathe in some fresh air.
note: The only proven way to reduce alcohol or many drug effects in your body is to allow time for metabolism and elimination.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles,b:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing,c:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles
note: You may only pass where signs and pavement markings allow it and where you have enough clear distance ahead to pass safely. Passing is prohibited at intersections and is unsafe on curves or hills where your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

question: Approximately how far might it take a fully loaded tractor-trailer traveling 55 mph to stop?
options: a:Up to 400 feet.,b:About 50 feet.,c:About 125 feet.
note: Large trucks need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. A fully loaded tractor‑trailer traveling about 55 mph can require roughly the length of a football field or more—up to around 400 feet—to come to a complete stop.

question: A single broken yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicates what?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,b:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is not allowed.,c:Drivers are not permitted to pass in either direction.
note: A single broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions. When the line is broken on your side, you may pass another vehicle if it is safe and legal, with enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic.

question: What action must you take when you approach an octagonal traffic sign?
options: a:Turn immediately.,b:Stop.,c:Slow down but keep moving.
note: An octagonal (eight‑sided) red sign is always a STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop at the stop line, crosswalk, or before entering the intersection, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: How can you prevent becoming an aggressive driver?
options: a:Relax, focus on driving, and be realistic about travel time.,b:Tailgate slower drivers to pressure them.,c:Drive above the posted speed limit to get ahead.
note: Staying calm, allowing extra travel time, and focusing on safe driving helps prevent frustration from turning into aggressive behavior. Avoid tailgating, speeding, or trying to “punish” other drivers, as these are examples of aggressive driving.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim high beams, where should you look to avoid glare?
options: a:Directly at the headlights.,b:Toward the left edge of your lane.,c:Toward the right edge of your lane.
note: When an oncoming driver does not dim high beams, look toward the right edge of your lane and use your peripheral vision to track the road. This reduces glare and helps you stay in your lane more safely than looking directly at the bright lights.

question: Which behavior describes defensive driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,b:Look only at the car directly in front of you.,c:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road ahead, to the sides, and behind to spot hazards early and give themselves time to react. Staring only at the car in front or relying on a fixed distance without scanning reduces your ability to respond to changing conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle, when is it safe to return to the right lane?
options: a:Whenever you feel comfortable.,b:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.,c:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:About three seconds after passing.
note: After passing, it is safe to return to the right lane only when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror and have checked your blind spot. This ensures you have enough space and do not cut off the other driver.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Right,c:Left
note: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the right, toward the edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic instead of into the lane, reducing the risk of a collision.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no warning signals, you should:
options: a:Always come to a complete stop whether a train is visible or not.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Assume a crossing will have signals.
note: At a railroad crossing without lights or gates, you are not required to stop every time, but you must slow down, look, and listen carefully for trains. Be prepared to stop if you see or hear a train, or if your view is blocked. Never assume the tracks are clear just because there are no signals.

question: How does the type of alcoholic beverage affect impairment?
options: a:The type of alcohol (beer vs. wine) does not change impairment; the amount consumed does.,b:Beer impairs less than wine.,c:Hard ciders and mixed drinks always cause the most impairment.
note: Impairment is determined by how much alcohol enters your bloodstream (BAC), not by whether it comes from beer, wine, or liquor. A standard serving of each can contain about the same amount of alcohol, and all types can equally impair judgment, reaction time, and coordination if you drink enough.

question: If pedestrians are in a crosswalk ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and wait for them to finish crossing.,b:Proceed; drivers have the right-of-way.,c:Drive around them on the right if safe.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk. You must stop and allow them to cross safely, and remain stopped until they are safely out of your path and it is clearly safe to proceed. Never drive around or pressure pedestrians who are lawfully crossing.

question: What best describes distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,b:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from the driving task. This includes taking your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Even if it does not force you into an evasive maneuver, distraction greatly increases your risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a pedestrian is in the middle of the street when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.,b:Wait until the pedestrian has finished crossing before proceeding.,c:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,d:Honk to hurry the pedestrian along.
note: Even with a green light, you must yield to pedestrians already in the crosswalk and allow them to finish crossing safely.

question: Before switching on the ignition, what safety checks should you make?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt.
note: Before starting the engine, you should always buckle your own safety belt and make sure all passengers are properly buckled. As the driver, you are responsible for checking that everyone is restrained before you turn the ignition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an emergency vehicle using flashing lights approaches while you are on a one-way street, you must:
options: a:Drive toward the nearest roadside and stop.,b:Drive with your flashers turned on.,c:Speed up to reach the nearest exit.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches on a one‑way street, you must pull toward the nearest edge or curb—right or left—and stop until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: When you take any medication, what should you do regarding driving?
options: a:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.,b:Drive the same as always because medications usually have no effect.,c:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about effects before driving.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can make you drowsy, dizzy, or slow your reactions. Always check with your doctor or pharmacist, or read the label, to see if it is safe to drive before you get behind the wheel.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing warning sign, what should you be ready to do?
options: a:Drive faster than the train to clear the crossing.,b:Be prepared to stop if a train is nearby.,c:Look for a way around any lowered gates.
note: A railroad crossing warning sign means you are approaching train tracks. Slow down, look and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop if a train is approaching or if warning devices such as lights or gates are activated. Never drive around lowered gates.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.,b:Steer to the left.,c:Steer to the right.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids to the left, you should steer gently in the same direction—toward the left. Steering in the direction of the skid helps you regain control and straighten the vehicle. Avoid hard braking or jerky steering, which can make the skid worse.

question: A steady yellow traffic signal warns that which light will soon appear?
options: a:Steady green.,b:Flashing yellow.,c:Steady red.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and prepare to stop, unless you are so close to the intersection that stopping suddenly would be unsafe.

question: If a flagger is directing traffic in a construction zone, you must:
options: a:Copy what surrounding traffic is doing despite the flagger's instructions.,b:Assume the flagger is not supposed to be directing traffic.,c:Follow the flagger's directions.
note: In construction zones, flaggers are authorized to direct traffic and their instructions have the same legal force as traffic signals or signs. You must follow the flagger’s directions, even if they differ from normal traffic controls.

question: Why should drivers give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:They can stop more quickly than adults.,b:They always follow traffic laws.,c:They have less developed reflexes and are smaller and harder to see.,d:They always use bike lanes.
