note: Children on bicycles are smaller, harder to see, and less predictable because their judgment and reflexes are not fully developed. Always give them extra space and be prepared for sudden or unexpected movements, especially near schools and parks.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,c:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks are much heavier than passenger vehicles and need more time and distance to stop, especially when fully loaded. Never cut closely in front of a truck, and allow extra following distance when driving behind one.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers on a freeway make space for vehicles entering from an on-ramp?
options: a:Slow to a stop on the freeway.,b:Merge into an adjacent lane when possible or adjust speed to create a gap.,c:Maintain speed and position.
note: On a freeway, help entering traffic merge safely by creating space. When it is safe, change to an adjacent lane to give them room. If you cannot change lanes, adjust your speed slightly so a clear gap opens for the merging vehicle. Do not stop on the freeway unless absolutely necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What do speed limit signs indicate?
options: a:The speed drivers should drive in heavy traffic.,b:The maximum or minimum speed that is legally allowed.,c:Potential driving speeds for the area.
note: Speed limit signs show the maximum (and sometimes minimum) speed allowed under ideal conditions. You must still slow down below the posted limit when weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: What is the 'No zone' in relation to large trucks and buses?
options: a:A road area where loud music is restricted.,b:A special reduced speed zone near large vehicles.,c:The blind spots around a truck or bus where smaller vehicles cannot be seen.
note: The 'No Zone' is the large blind-spot area around trucks and buses where the driver cannot see you in their mirrors. These areas are along both sides, directly behind, and sometimes directly in front of the vehicle. Staying out of these zones helps prevent collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to turn left at a corner, to whom must you yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard, and pedestrians and bicyclists in or entering the crosswalk.,b:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a “Walk” signal.,c:Oncoming vehicles turning left with you.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is close enough to be a hazard, as well as to pedestrians and bicyclists in or entering the crosswalk. You do not have to yield to every approaching vehicle far away, but you must wait for any oncoming traffic that has the right-of-way and could collide with you if you turn.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline mean?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic on either side may pass on the left when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic. You must not pass if your view is blocked, if it is not safe, or if there is also a solid yellow line on your side of the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change with vehicle speed?
options: a:They increase as speed increases.,b:They decrease as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect.
note: As speed increases, your vehicle needs more distance to stop because both reaction distance and braking distance grow. Crashes at higher speeds involve more force, so injuries and damage are usually more severe. Leave more following distance as your speed goes up.

question: Which action helps prevent crashes by communicating with other road users?
options: a:Drive only on side streets.,b:Signal when slowing,c:Ignore other drivers.
note: Using your turn signals, brake lights, horn, and emergency flashers lets other road users know what you plan to do. Signaling when you slow, stop, or turn reduces surprises and helps prevent crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at the same time to a four-way intersection controlled by stop signs, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:One driver may continue driving without stopping.
note: At a four-way stop where vehicles arrive at the same time, each driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. This rule helps decide who goes first and prevents confusion and collisions.

question: What can happen when you drink alcohol and take drugs together?
options: a:The effects of both can be increased, greatly impairing driving.,b:They will cancel each other out.,c:They will help cure your illness.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both slow your reactions and judgment. When taken together, their effects often multiply, making you far more impaired and unsafe to drive than with either substance alone.

question: What do downward-facing triangular traffic signs typically indicate?
options: a:Indicate construction zones.,b:Tell drivers to yield.,c:Indicate school zones.
note: A downward-pointing triangle is the standard shape for yield signs. When you see this sign, slow down, be prepared to stop, and give the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians if they are close enough to be a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to turn left, what should drivers do?
options: a:Speed up and complete the turn quickly to avoid delays.,b:Signal,c:Move into the left lane at the last second.
note: Before turning left, signal well in advance, move into the correct lane in plenty of time, slow down smoothly, and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. Only complete the turn when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter a flashing red traffic light, what must you do?
options: a:Continue through if no other vehicles are present.,b:Wait until it changes to green before proceeding.,c:Treat the intersection as if controlled by a stop sign (come to a full stop).
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield as needed, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: An octagonal eight-sided traffic sign always indicates:
options: a:A speed limit sign.,b:A stop sign.,c:A hospital sign.
note: An eight-sided (octagonal) sign is used only for STOP signs. When you see this shape, you must come to a complete stop and proceed only when it is safe.

question: If you have a probationary license or instructional permit, when may you use your cell phone while driving?
options: a:As long as you don't text.,b:When you are reporting an emergency.,c:If you are just answering a call.
note: Drivers with probationary licenses or instructional permits are generally not allowed to use a cell phone while driving, even hands‑free, except to report an emergency such as a crash, crime, or hazard to 911 or appropriate authorities.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement onto the shoulder, you should:
options: a:Slow down and carefully steer back onto the pavement once it is safe.,b:Brake hard and turn sharply back onto the pavement.,c:Stop immediately on the shoulder and wait.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm, ease off the accelerator, and avoid hard braking or jerking the wheel. When your speed is under control and it is safe, gently steer back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is true about emergency vehicles using sirens and flashing lights?
options: a:They have the right-of-way and you must yield.,b:They always must pull over to the right before you do.,c:You should follow them closely so traffic clears.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using sirens and flashing lights, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling to the right side of the road and stopping, if possible, and then proceed only after it has passed and the way is clear.

question: When driving on slippery surfaces such as ice or snow, what should you do before going down steep hills?
options: a:Pump your brakes continuously to keep them from freezing.,b:Shift to a low gear.,c:Follow other vehicles closely.
note: On steep, slippery hills, shifting to a low gear before you start downhill lets the engine help slow the vehicle so you rely less on the brakes. This improves traction and control and reduces the chance of skidding. You should also leave extra following distance and avoid sudden braking or steering.

question: When you see a steady yellow arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?
options: a:Should slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Merge into a lane in the arrow's direction without stopping.,c:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic.
note: A steady yellow arrow means the protected movement (such as a protected left turn) is ending and a red arrow is about to appear. You should slow and prepare to stop if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light changes, continue through and clear the intersection carefully; do not speed up to beat the red.

question: Why is night driving more hazardous?
options: a:Speed limits are higher at night.,b:There are always fewer vehicles at night.,c:Distance and speed of other vehicles are harder to judge in the dark.
note: At night, your visibility is limited to the area lit by your headlights, and glare from other vehicles can further reduce what you see. Because you cannot see as far or as clearly, it is harder to judge how far away other vehicles are and how fast they are moving, which makes night driving more hazardous.

question: At a light rail intersection you should always:
options: a:Share the road only with pedestrians and bicycles.,b:Pay attention to signals and signs and look both ways before crossing tracks.,c:Ignore traffic signals if no train is visible.
note: At light rail crossings, always obey all signals, signs, and pavement markings, and look carefully in both directions before crossing the tracks. Trains can be quiet and may approach from either direction on any track. Never drive around lowered gates or ignore warning devices, even if you do not immediately see a train.

question: Before turning on the ignition, what safety check should you do?
options: a:Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers are buckled.,b:Buckle only child passengers.,c:Buckle only adult passengers.
note: Before starting the vehicle, always buckle your own seat belt and make sure every passenger, adults and children, is properly restrained. This habit ensures everyone is protected from the moment the vehicle begins moving, which greatly reduces the risk of injury in a crash.

question: What is true about drivers who travel much slower than the speed limit?
options: a:Driving excessively slowly can be hazardous and you may be required to pull off to let traffic pass.,b:They always have the right-of-way.,c:They are always very safe drivers.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly. If you are moving so slowly that you are blocking traffic, many states require you to pull over where it is safe and let faster vehicles pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which traffic?
options: a:No one—they have the right-of-way.,b:Oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right.,c:Only vehicles that are overtaking them.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, because they have the right-of-way. You may only complete your left turn when there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic, even if you are in an intersection.

question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning on wet pavement?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Put your cruise control on to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a layer of water and lose contact with the road, usually at higher speeds. The best way to reduce the risk is to slow down in wet conditions and make smooth, gentle steering and braking inputs so your tires can maintain grip.

question: What is the purpose of regulatory signs?
options: a:To mark danger areas only.,b:To tell drivers what they must or must not do.,c:To always be diamond-shaped and yellow or green.
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must do (such as obeying a speed limit) or must not do (such as no U-turns or no parking). They communicate traffic laws and rules that you are legally required to follow.

question: If an oncoming driver uses high beams, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the center of the road.,b:Toward the right side of the road.,c:Toward either side of the road.
note: Bright high beams from oncoming traffic can temporarily blind you. To protect your vision and still stay in your lane, briefly glance toward the right edge of the road and use the lane markings or road edge as a guide until the vehicle passes.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Drink caffeinated beverages and continue driving.,b:Open a window to stay awake.,c:Stop and rest or switch drivers.
note: Stop for a rest or change drivers; caffeine and windows are not reliable substitutes for sleep.

question: What steps should you take when changing lanes?
options: a:Begin signaling as you move into the next lane.,b:Signal at least 100 feet before your lane change in lower-speed areas.,c:Check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder for blind spots before changing lanes.
note: Before changing lanes, check mirrors, signal, and glance over your shoulder to clear your blind spot; signal in advance (about 100 feet in residential areas).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:They are eliminated by having one outside mirror on each side.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked only with rearview mirrors.
note: All vehicles have blind spots that mirrors cannot fully eliminate. Large trucks and buses have much larger blind spots than passenger cars, especially directly behind and along the sides. Because of this, you should avoid lingering next to or close behind large trucks where the driver may not see you.

question: A flashing red traffic light has the same meaning as which sign?
options: a:Yield sign.,b:Stop sign.,c:Solid red light.
note: A flashing red light means you must stop completely, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, then proceed only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: What is the shape of a stop sign?
options: a:Square.,b:Octagon.,c:Rectangle.
note: A stop sign is an octagon, which means it has eight sides. This unique shape helps drivers recognize it quickly from a distance and even when visibility is poor, so they know they must come to a complete stop.

question: Combining a prescription drug with alcohol can cause what effect?
options: a:It can make you unfit to drive and increase impairment.,b:It will make you more alert.,c:There will likely be no effect.
note: Many prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines can interact with alcohol and greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and slowed reaction time. When combined, these effects can make you unfit to drive and much more likely to be involved in a crash.

question: If you are under 21, what blood alcohol level can result in license suspension?
options: a:0.15 percent or more.,b:Any detectable amount.,c:0.08 percent or more.
note: For drivers under 21, Wisconsin uses a zero‑tolerance standard. Any detectable amount of alcohol in the system can lead to license suspension and other penalties, even if the level is below the adult legal limit of 0.08%. Young drivers must not drive after consuming any alcohol.

question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Check for vehicles moving into the same lane.,c:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.
note: Safe lane changes are planned and gradual. You should always check mirrors, look over your shoulder to clear blind spots, and signal before moving. Abrupt or spontaneous lane changes surprise other drivers and greatly increase the risk of a collision.

question: Which road surface tends to freeze first?
options: a:An intersection,b:A tunnel,c:A bridge
note: Bridges and overpasses usually freeze before the rest of the road because cold air circulates above and below the surface, causing ice to form sooner even when nearby pavement may still be just wet. Approach bridges with extra caution in cold or freezing conditions.

question: Approaching a heavy truck from behind on a hill, what should you expect?
options: a:You will always be able to safely pass the truck.,b:The truck may be traveling slower than the posted speed limit.,c:You may not be able to legally pass the truck.
note: Heavy trucks often slow down on upgrades because of their weight and limited power, so they may travel below the posted speed limit on hills. When approaching from behind, be prepared for a slower speed and only pass if it is legal, safe, and you have enough clear distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
note: After passing, do not move back into your lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have left enough space and reduces the risk of cutting the other driver off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: What attitude should a driver adopt about other drivers' compliance with right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way rules help organize traffic, but you must never assume others will follow them. Always be prepared to yield, even when you are legally entitled to go first, to avoid crashes caused by impatient, distracted, or confused drivers.

question: Where is the safest place for children age 12 and under to ride in a vehicle equipped with airbags?
options: a:The bed of a pick-up truck.,b:The back seat.,c:The front seat.
note: Children age 12 and under are safest riding in the back seat, away from front airbags. Airbags deploy with great force and are designed for adults; a deploying airbag can seriously injure or kill a child in the front seat, especially if they are unrestrained or in a child seat.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a two-way road with no curb, which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Straight ahead,b:Toward the right/side of the road so the vehicle will roll away from the center.,c:Toward the left/center of the road.
note: On an uphill road with no curb, turn your front wheels toward the right edge of the road. If your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll off the roadway rather than into traffic, reducing the chance of a collision.

question: If a vehicle equipped with ABS starts to lose traction on a slippery road, what should you do?
options: a:Press and hold the gas pedal.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: With antilock brakes (ABS), you should press and hold the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go. The ABS system automatically pumps the brakes to help prevent wheel lockup, allowing you to maintain steering control on slippery surfaces. Do not pump the brakes in a vehicle equipped with ABS.

question: When encountering a flashing yellow light at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for other traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when the intersection is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you proceed through an intersection that has a stop sign but no stop line or crosswalk?
options: a:After coming to a complete stop and verifying that it is safe to proceed,b:After you have stopped at least 20 feet prior to the intersection,c:After slowing down to verify that there is no cross traffic
note: At a stop sign, you must always come to a complete stop. If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection, check for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: When a school bus is stopped to pick up or drop off passengers, what must drivers do?
options: a:Stop only if you are traveling in the same direction on any type of road.,b:Slow down and pass carefully.,c:Stop as required by law when the bus has flashing red lights and/or an extended stop arm.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and/or stop arm extended, drivers must stop and remain stopped until the signals are turned off. In many states this applies to traffic in both directions unless the roadway is divided by a physical median or barrier.

question: When should you allow an extra cushion of space behind or around your vehicle?
options: a:When following a driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle (such as a truck, bus, or vehicle towing a trailer).,b:When following a station wagon.,c:When following a small passenger car.
note: You should allow extra following distance behind large vehicles or those that block their rear view, such as trucks, buses, and vehicles towing trailers. These drivers may not see you as easily, and the extra space gives you more time to react and a better view of the road ahead.

question: Because motorcycles and mopeds are harder to see, what should car drivers do?
options: a:Share a lane with a motorcycle to keep it visible.,b:Slow down whenever one is nearby but not check mirrors.,c:Make constant visual checks for motorcycles.
note: Because motorcycles and mopeds are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots, drivers should make frequent visual checks of mirrors and blind spots, especially before changing lanes or turning.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you be prepared to do?
options: a:Speed up to cross before a train arrives.,b:Ignore it if no train is visible.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.
note: At any railroad crossing you should slow down, look and listen for trains, and be ready to stop. If warning lights are flashing or gates are lowering or down, you must stop between 15 and 50 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until it is safe and legal to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Another driver is passing you. How should you respond?
options: a:Maintain your lane and speed, slowing slightly if needed to allow safe passing and reentry.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Signal them when it's safe for them to pass.
note: When another driver is passing you, stay in your lane and keep a steady speed, or slightly reduce speed if needed so they can pass safely. Do not speed up or signal them when to pass; they are responsible for judging when it is safe. Your job is to make their pass as predictable and safe as possible.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow signal, what should you do?
options: a:Make a U-turn because the intersection is closed.,b:Drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Stop and wait for the light to change.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. Scan for cross traffic, pedestrians, and other hazards, and be prepared to yield if another road user does not obey their signal.

question: Which centerline marking prohibits passing from either direction?
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Single broken yellow,c:Combination solid and broken yellow
note: A double solid yellow centerline means vehicles traveling in either direction are not allowed to cross the lines to pass. You may cross only when making a permitted left turn or entering/exiting a driveway or side road, when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When should you increase the distance between your vehicle and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:Are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.,b:Are being tailgated by another driver.,c:Are following a small passenger vehicle.
note: If you are being tailgated, you should increase the space in front of your vehicle. By slowing gradually or changing lanes when safe, you create a larger following distance ahead, which gives you more time to brake smoothly and reduces the chance of a rear‑end collision from the driver following too closely.

question: A leaking exhaust system can cause what while driving?
options: a:Make you drowsy or cause dangerous fumes.,b:Increase oil consumption.,c:Require an early tune-up.
note: A leaking exhaust can let carbon monoxide and other toxic fumes enter the passenger compartment. These gases can make you drowsy, dizzy, or confused and can lead to carbon monoxide poisoning, which can be fatal. Any suspected exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: What dangers do worn or bald tires present?
options: a:They always reduce fuel consumption.,b:They decrease stopping distances.,c:They increase stopping distances,d:They improve ride comfort.
note: Tires with worn or bald tread cannot grip the road properly, especially in wet conditions. This reduces traction, increases stopping distance, and raises the risk of skidding or hydroplaning. Keeping good tread depth is essential for safe braking and handling.

question: Which statement is true about driving and medications?
options: a:Medications are safe to take at any time.,b:Most cold medications can make a person drowsy.,c:Over-the-counter medications cannot impair driving ability if taken in the recommended dosages.
note: Many cold medications, including some that are available without a prescription, can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction time, and reduced coordination. Both prescription and over‑the‑counter drugs can impair driving, so always read labels and follow your doctor’s or pharmacist’s advice before driving.

question: To check your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulder toward the direction you plan to move.,b:Look only at your side mirror.,c:Look only at your rearview mirror.
note: Mirrors do not show the areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, known as blind spots. Before changing lanes, you must briefly look over your shoulder in the direction you intend to move to be sure no vehicle, motorcycle, or bicycle is in your blind spot.

question: What does a pentagonal (five-sided) traffic sign warn you about?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:School zones.,c:No passing zones.
note: A five‑sided (pentagon‑shaped) sign is used for school zones and school crossings. When you see this shape, be prepared to slow down, watch carefully for children, and obey any posted school‑zone speed limits.

question: When stopped in line on a railroad crossing with no gates, what must you ensure?
options: a:You may pass slower drivers while on the tracks.,b:You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.,c:That there is room ahead so your vehicle can clear the tracks without stopping.
note: Before you drive onto railroad tracks, you must be sure there is enough space on the far side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks without stopping. Never stop on the tracks, and never pass other vehicles while you are on the crossing.

question: A broken yellow centerline between two lanes means what?
options: a:Both lanes go in the same direction.,b:Traffic flows in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.,c:Passing is not permitted.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed in either direction when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. You must still check carefully for oncoming traffic and only pass when you have enough time and space.

question: Where is it best to keep a space cushion while driving?
options: a:Only in front of the vehicle.,b:Only on the left and right sides of your vehicle.,c:On all sides of your vehicle.
note: A space cushion is the open space around your vehicle that gives you time to react. The safest practice is to keep space on all sides—front, rear, and both sides—so you have room to maneuver or stop if another driver makes a mistake or a hazard appears.

question: If your vehicle is blocking traffic after a minor accident, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle off the traveled portion of the roadway.,b:Leave your vehicle where it is until police arrive.,c:Drive away immediately and report the crash later.
note: After a minor crash, if no one is seriously injured and the vehicles can be moved, you should move them off the traveled portion of the road to reduce the risk of another collision. You must stay at the scene, exchange information, and provide help as required by law.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Left-turning drivers must yield to which vehicles?
options: a:No one at all.,b:Oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and any pedestrians in the crosswalk.,c:Passing cars only.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming traffic that is going straight or turning right, and you must also yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: What instruction is given by a red octagon-shaped sign?
options: a:No parking.,b:Do not enter.,c:Yield.,d:Stop.
note: A red octagon is the universal STOP sign. You must come to a complete stop before the crosswalk, stop line, or entering the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What does a steady red arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:Drivers may turn after a complete stop.,b:Drivers may proceed in any direction.,c:Traffic in the indicated lane must stop and may not proceed in that direction.
note: A steady red arrow means traffic in the lane controlled by that arrow must stop and may not proceed in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until a green arrow or green light allows movement in that direction.

question: At about what speed can tires begin to hydroplane on water?
options: a:Around 35 miles per hour.,b:Around 45 miles per hour.,c:Around 55 miles per hour.,d:At any speed below 20 mph.
note: Tires can begin to hydroplane at about 35 mph on standing water. As speed increases, the tires ride up on the water and lose contact with the road, greatly reducing steering and braking control.

question: When must you report a crash to law enforcement in Wisconsin?
options: a:Only if your vehicle is severely damaged.,b:When someone is hurt or when property damage meets or exceeds the legal reporting threshold.,c:Only when someone is killed.
note: In Wisconsin, you must report a crash to law enforcement when there is injury or death, or when there is $1,000 or more in damage to any one person’s property, or $200 or more damage to government-owned property. Reporting ensures proper documentation and that emergency help can be provided if needed.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Turn the wheel into oncoming traffic.,b:Steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go (generally the direction of the skid).,c:Overcorrect in the opposite direction.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the vehicle to go, which is generally the same direction the rear of the vehicle is skidding. This helps you straighten the vehicle and regain control without overcorrecting.

question: If your wheels drop off the pavement edge, what is the correct way to return to the roadway?
options: a:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately.,b:Stop where you are and remain off the pavement.,c:Wait until it is safe and gently steer back onto the pavement.
note: If your wheels drop off the pavement, stay calm and do not jerk the steering wheel back onto the road. Ease off the accelerator, keep a firm grip on the wheel, slow down gradually, check traffic, and when the car is under control and there is a safe gap, gently steer back onto the pavement.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed most commonly does what?
options: a:Decreases your ability to react to hazards but reduces crash severity.,b:Often leads to high-risk decision-making and increases crash severity.,c:Has no effect on crash risk.
note: Excessive speed reduces the time you have to see and react to hazards, makes it harder to control your vehicle, and greatly increases the force of any collision. Crashes at higher speeds are more likely to cause serious injury or death, and speeding drivers often make more risky decisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What determines how much space you need to cross traffic?
options: a:Use of your turn signals.,b:Presence of a stop sign.,c:Road and weather conditions, and the speed and distance of oncoming traffic.
note: The space you need to cross traffic depends on how quickly you and other vehicles can stop or change speed. Road and weather conditions affect traction and acceleration, and you must also judge the speed and distance of oncoming traffic to be sure you have enough time to cross safely.

question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, you should:
options: a:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,b:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots on both sides, especially on the right. You should avoid driving alongside them for long periods so the driver can see you and has room to maneuver. Pass safely and promptly, and do not linger next to a large vehicle.

question: In which situation should your wheels not be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.,b:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,c:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.
note: When parked on a hill or sloping driveway, you should turn your wheels so that if your brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic. On level roads without a curb, wheels are normally left straight, and when waiting to turn left at a light, wheels should stay straight so a rear-end collision does not push you into oncoming traffic.

question: What may happen if alcohol is combined with another drug?
options: a:The effects of both the alcohol and the drug may be increased.,b:Nothing will happen.,c:The effects of both will always be reduced.
note: Combining alcohol with other drugs often makes each substance’s effects stronger and more unpredictable. This can greatly increase drowsiness, slow reaction time, and impair judgment, making driving extremely dangerous.

question: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a slash through it means:
options: a:That drivers should come to a complete stop.,b:That an action is forbidden.,c:That some drivers should yield to other drivers.
note: A regulatory sign with a red circle and a diagonal slash over a symbol means that the action shown inside the circle is prohibited. For example, a right-turn arrow with a red circle and slash means “No Right Turn.” Drivers must not perform the indicated maneuver.

question: Which of the following commonly causes traffic accidents?
options: a:Excessive speed under the driving conditions,b:Inattentive driving,c:Following other vehicles too closely,d:All of the above
note: Many crashes are caused by drivers going too fast for conditions, not paying attention, or following too closely. Any of these behaviors can reduce your time and space to react. Safe drivers control their speed, stay alert, and leave enough following distance to avoid sudden collisions.

question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to freeway traffic?
options: a:Be 5–10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,b:Be at or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,c:Always drive at the posted freeway speed limit even if traffic is slower.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, as long as it is safe and legal. Matching the speed of traffic makes it easier to find a gap and merge smoothly without forcing other drivers to brake suddenly.

question: Alcohol in any concentration is classified as what?
options: a:Neither.,b:A stimulant.,c:A depressant (it slows nerve impulses and bodily functions).
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity, reaction time, and coordination, and it impairs judgment. Even small amounts can affect driving ability and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle on a two-lane road, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:See the vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.,c:Have passed the other vehicle’s front bumper.
note: On a two-lane road, you should only move back into your lane after passing when you can see the entire front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, including its headlights. This ensures you have left enough space and reduces the risk of cutting the other driver off or causing a rear-end collision.

question: During the first nine months with a probationary license under age 18, what restrictions apply?
options: a:You cannot drive at all between midnight and 5:00 a.m.,b:Limits on the type and number of passengers and restrictions on late-night driving.,c:No restrictions apply.
note: New drivers under 18 with a probationary or intermediate license typically face limits on how many and what type of passengers they can carry, and they are often restricted from driving late at night except for specific exceptions like work or school. These rules are designed to reduce distractions and crash risk during the highest‑risk period of driving.

question: After consuming alcohol, when is reaction time slower?
options: a:After working hard.,b:After sleeping.,c:After drinking alcohol.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows the central nervous system. After drinking, your reaction time increases, your coordination and judgment worsen, and it takes longer to respond to hazards. Even small amounts of alcohol can affect driving ability, so you should never drive after drinking.

question: Which is a likely consequence of tailgating other drivers?
options: a:Can frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Reduces collisions by preventing being 'cut off.'.,c:Cannot result in a traffic citation.
note: Tailgating, or following too closely, gives you very little time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. It greatly increases the risk of rear‑end collisions and can anger or intimidate other drivers, contributing to road rage. Always leave a safe following distance of at least three seconds in good conditions, and more in bad weather or at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:
options: a:Ignore the guard and follow surrounding traffic.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Assume the guard is not authorized to direct traffic.,d:Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
note: Crossing guards are authorized to control traffic in school zones to protect children and pedestrians. You must obey their signals and instructions just as you would obey a traffic signal or police officer. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and proceed only when the crossing guard indicates it is safe.

question: What is the best response when another driver is tailgating you?
options: a:Slam on your brakes to get the other driver to back off.,b:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the tailgater.,c:Change lanes or gradually slow down to encourage them to pass.
note: If another driver is following too closely, the safest response is to make it easy for them to pass. Signal early, change lanes when it is safe, or gradually slow down so they can go around you. Never slam on your brakes or speed up, as both can increase the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about changing lanes is true?
options: a:Look over your right shoulder for a right lane change and over your left shoulder for a left lane change.,b:You only need to use your mirrors.,c:Vehicles with two outside mirrors have no blind spots.
note: When changing lanes, always use your mirrors and then look over the shoulder on the side you are moving toward to check your blind spot. Mirrors alone cannot show everything, and all vehicles have blind spots even with multiple mirrors.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are divided by which color lines?
options: a:Red,b:White,c:Yellow
note: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction, such as on multi-lane roads and freeways. Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. Red is not used to separate travel lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection, in what order should you scan?
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Before entering an intersection, scan left, then right, then left again. Traffic from the left is usually closer to you, so you check it twice to be sure it is safe before you proceed.

question: Where are truck blind spots typically located?
options: a:Only on the right side of the truck.,b:Only directly in front of the truck.,c:Directly behind the truck and along the immediate left and right sides of the cab.
note: Large trucks have big blind spots directly behind them and along both sides, especially near the cab. If you are directly behind a truck or driving close along the side of the cab, the driver may not see you. As a rule, if you cannot see the truck driver’s mirrors, the driver likely cannot see you.

question: When approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what is the required action?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed.,b:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be alert, reduce speed as needed, and be prepared to yield to other traffic or pedestrians if necessary.

question: If your wheels run off the pavement edge, what should you do first?
options: a:Stop in the lane and put on hazard lights.,b:Turn sharply back onto the pavement immediately.,c:Hold the wheel firmly
note: If your wheels run off the pavement, hold the steering wheel firmly to maintain control, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Once your speed is reduced and traffic allows, gently steer back onto the pavement without jerking the wheel.

question: Driving considerably slower than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,b:Often a hazard because others may attempt risky passes.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.
note: Driving much slower than the normal flow of traffic can be dangerous because other drivers may become impatient and attempt risky passing maneuvers. You should generally travel at the speed of traffic (within the speed limit) and avoid unnecessarily obstructing the flow.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, you should:
options: a:Glance briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Keep your eyes on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, briefly glance toward the right side of your lane and use the edge of the road or lane line as a guide. Avoid looking directly into the headlights so your eyes can recover more quickly and you maintain good visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When allowed to turn right on red, which requirement must you follow?
options: a:Slow down and turn without stopping.,b:Always use your hazard lights before turning.,c:Stop completely and make the turn from the lane nearest the right curb after yielding to traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning right on red where it is allowed, you must first come to a complete stop at the limit line or before the crosswalk, yield to pedestrians and all approaching traffic, signal your turn, and then turn from the lane nearest the right curb when it is safe.

question: If you are turning and a pedestrian without a traffic signal is crossing your path, who must yield?
options: a:Whoever started moving last must yield.,b:The driver must yield to the pedestrian.,c:The pedestrian must yield to the turning driver.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are lawfully crossing the street at intersections, even when there is no traffic signal. When you are turning and a pedestrian is crossing your path, you must wait until the pedestrian has safely crossed before completing your turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To check for objects in your blind spot before changing lanes, you should:
options: a:Only use the inside rearview mirror.,b:Look over your left or right shoulder (as appropriate).,c:Only use the left outside mirror.
note: Mirrors alone cannot show everything around your vehicle; there are blind spots along the sides. Before changing lanes, you should quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, while also using your mirrors and signal.

question: What is the best method to avoid hydroplaning?
options: a:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,b:Drive faster to get through puddles quickly.,c:Slow down when roads are wet and keep tires properly maintained.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. To reduce the risk, slow down on wet roads, avoid sudden moves, and keep your tires properly inflated and with good tread. Never speed up in water or rely on cruise control in heavy rain.

question: When approaching railroad tracks, what precautions should you take?
options: a:Speed up to cross before a gate lowers.,b:Look and listen,c:Drive around any lowered gate.
note: Railroad crossings require extra caution because trains cannot stop quickly. As you approach tracks, slow down, look both ways, and listen for trains. Be prepared to stop if a train is coming, and never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Only after you begin moving.,c:Whenever a passenger asks you to.,d:Only when reversing.
note: Before you start driving, adjust your seat and all mirrors so you have a clear view behind and to the sides of your vehicle. Setting mirrors before moving helps reduce blind spots and lets you focus on the road once the vehicle is in motion.

question: What does a red-and-white triangular sign at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Decrease speed and yield the right-of-way when necessary.,b:Always come to a full stop at the intersection.,c:Slow down if an emergency vehicle is approaching.
note: A red-and-white triangle is a yield sign. You must slow down, be ready to stop, and yield the right-of-way to traffic and pedestrians already in or close to the intersection.

question: If a vehicle has a two-part (lap and shoulder) seat belt system, you should:
options: a:Not use either belt if the airbag is present.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.,d:Use both the lap and the shoulder belts.
note: In a vehicle with both lap and shoulder belts, you must wear both. The lap belt should be low across the hips, and the shoulder belt across the chest. Using only one part greatly reduces protection and can cause serious injury.

question: Alcohol consumption causes which impairments?
options: a:Improved coordination.,b:Increased concentration.,c:Impaired judgment, coordination, and concentration.
note: Alcohol slows your brain and body functions. It harms judgment, coordination, reaction time, and concentration, making it harder to make safe decisions and respond quickly to traffic situations.

question: What can happen if you drink alcohol while taking prescription or over-the-counter medicines?
options: a:The combination can multiply the impairing effects of the alcohol or medicine.,b:The medicine will cancel alcohol's effects.,c:Alcohol will help the medicine work better.
note: Mixing alcohol with prescription or over-the-counter medicines can greatly increase drowsiness, dizziness, and confusion. The combined effects can be much stronger than either alone and can make driving extremely dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before changing lanes you should check your mirrors and what else?
options: a:Glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,b:Always slow down in your current lane.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly glance over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. This shoulder check lets you see vehicles in your blind spot that mirrors cannot show.

question: When a school bus ahead on your side has red lights flashing, what must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Slow to 10 mph and pass slowly.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus on your side of the road has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. Passing is illegal and extremely dangerous because children may be crossing the road in front of or behind the bus.

question: When driving to an unfamiliar area, what should you do?
options: a:Plan your trip in advance.,b:Should depend on road signs to find your way.,c:Only have to know generally where your destination is.
note: Before driving to an unfamiliar area, you should plan your trip in advance. Knowing your route, key turns, and exits reduces the need to look for directions while driving, which helps you stay focused on the road and avoid distractions. You should not rely only on road signs or a vague idea of where you are going.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:Blind spots can be checked solely with the rearview mirror.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots—areas you cannot see with your mirrors alone. Large trucks and buses have much larger blind spots on all sides than passenger cars, which means they may not see you if you are driving alongside or close behind them. You must avoid lingering in a truck’s blind spots and use both mirrors and quick head checks to see areas your mirrors miss.

question: What does a green arrow on a traffic signal indicate?
options: a:Traffic in the lane must turn in the arrow direction; it has the same authority as a circular green.,b:The arrow is used only on one-way streets.,c:You may proceed only if accompanied by a circular green light.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement in the direction of the arrow. Traffic coming toward you or crossing you is stopped by a red light, so you may proceed in the direction of the arrow after checking that the intersection is clear. For that specific movement, the green arrow has the same authority as a circular green light.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering public traffic from a driveway or private road should:
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way.,b:Force their way into traffic.,c:Yield to drivers already on the public road.
note: When you enter a public road from a driveway, alley, or private road, you must yield the right-of-way to all vehicles, bicycles, and pedestrians already on the public road or sidewalk. Wait until traffic is clear and it is safe before pulling out; you are responsible for merging smoothly without forcing other road users to slow or change lanes suddenly.

question: When is it appropriate to sound a sharp blast of your horn?
options: a:To greet a friend.,b:To urge someone to drive faster.,c:When another vehicle is in immediate danger of hitting you.,d:When the driver ahead is driving under the speed limit.
note: Use your horn to warn others of immediate danger, such as when another vehicle is about to hit you or move into your lane. Do not use the horn to greet people, show anger, or push other drivers to go faster.

question: How do sudden wind gusts affect highway driving?
options: a:They only cause visibility issues.,b:They can cause problems for all vehicles,c:They only affect large vehicles.
note: Sudden wind gusts can push any vehicle sideways, making it harder to stay in your lane, especially at highway speeds. They can also blow dust, snow, or debris that reduces visibility, so all drivers must be prepared to steer and slow as needed.

question: A solid red arrow in a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,b:The arrow is only advisory.,c:The same as a circular red light; you must stop and may not turn in that direction.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and you are not allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow until it changes to green or a permitted signal. It has the same stop requirement as a circular red light, but it applies specifically to that turn movement.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, where should you park if possible?
options: a:Stop in the right lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled highway.,c:Stop where you are.
note: If your car becomes disabled, you should move it completely off the traveled portion of the highway when it is safe, with all four wheels off the roadway. This reduces the risk of being hit by passing traffic and keeps lanes clear.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is behind you on a city street, what must you do?
options: a:Stay in your lane and slow down.,b:Keep driving to the right edge and slow down but do not stop.,c:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop until it passes.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches from behind on a city street, you must pull as far to the right as you safely can and stop until it has passed. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over and stop.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, what must you do?
options: a:The pedestrian must yield the right-of-way.,b:You must yield the right-of-way.,c:Honk your horn to let them know you are there.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog always have the right-of-way. You must slow down or stop as needed and allow them to cross safely, never trying to hurry them or drive through while they are in or near your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a two-lane road where traffic moves in the same direction in two lanes and vehicles are passing you on the right, what should you do if the driver behind wants to go faster?
options: a:Drive onto the left shoulder to let others pass.,b:Stay in your lane to avoid impeding traffic.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.
note: On a two-lane road where both lanes go in the same direction, the left lane is generally for passing and faster traffic, and the right lane is for slower traffic. If vehicles are already passing you on the right, you should stay in your lane and avoid weaving or sudden lane changes. Do not move into the right lane unless it is clearly safe and appropriate; focus on maintaining a safe, steady position and speed.

question: Many crashes are caused by which of the following?
options: a:Drivers keeping to the speed limit.,b:Drivers yielding right-of-way properly.,c:Drivers traveling too fast for conditions.,d:Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots frequently.
note: A major cause of crashes is driving too fast for conditions, even if you are below the posted speed limit. You must adjust your speed for rain, fog, traffic, curves, and poor visibility so you have enough time and distance to react safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two drivers arrive at an open (uncontrolled) intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on the right has the right-of-way.,b:The driver on the left has the right-of-way.,c:Both drivers must use caution and be prepared to yield.
note: At an open (uncontrolled) intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right has the right-of-way and may proceed first when it is safe.

question: What should you allow a motorcycle to do when sharing the road?
options: a:Drive on the shoulder beside the motorcycle.,b:Allow the motorcycle to use a complete lane.,c:Allow the motorcycle to use only half of a lane.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to the full use of a traffic lane, just like any other vehicle. You must not crowd them, share their lane, or drive alongside them in the same lane, because they need space to maneuver and maintain stability.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights at night, where should you look?
options: a:Toward the right side of the road ahead.,b:Directly at the oncoming headlights.,c:Over your shoulder.
note: Looking toward the right edge of your lane (not at oncoming headlights) reduces glare and helps prevent temporary blindness from high beams while still letting you track your lane position.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A curb painted red indicates:
options: a:A loading zone.,b:An area reserved for picking up and dropping off passengers only.,c:No stopping, standing, or parking at any time (except where specifically posted, such as a bus zone).
note: A red curb means no stopping, standing, or parking at any time, except when signs specifically allow it (for example, a bus zone). You may not use a red curb as a loading or passenger zone unless it is clearly posted for that purpose.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian walking along the roadway and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, what should you do?
options: a:Honk your horn to get the pedestrian to move over.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop for you.,c:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.
note: When a pedestrian is in the roadway and a vehicle is coming toward you, you should not try to squeeze between them. Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass first, then pass the pedestrian only when you can give them plenty of space.

question: Broken yellow lines on streets and highways are used to:
options: a:Indicate no passing zones.,b:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. When the yellow line is broken, you may pass another vehicle on the left if it is safe and legal to do so.

question: What is the best way to avoid hydroplaning when it is raining?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as in ideal conditions.,b:Apply brakes as soon as the car starts to skid.,c:Slow down and reduce your speed.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on a film of water and lose contact with the road. The best way to avoid it is to slow down in the rain and drive at a speed that matches the wet conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how far should you stay behind?
options: a:Farther behind than you would follow a passenger vehicle.,b:No more than one car length behind the truck.,c:As close as possible so the trucker can see you.,d:Directly beside the truck in the truck's blind spot.
note: Large trucks need more space to stop and have bigger blind spots than passenger cars. By staying farther back than you would behind a car, you give yourself more time to react and make it easier to see the road ahead while staying out of the truck’s blind spots.

question: When should you allow a larger following distance behind a motorcycle?
options: a:When you are behind a motorcycle, allow a larger following distance.,b:When driving more slowly.,c:When you may need to use your horn.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can stop or swerve more quickly than cars, and riders are more vulnerable in a crash. You should leave a larger following distance—at least three to four seconds—so you have enough time and space to react safely if the motorcycle slows or stops suddenly.

question: As a pedestrian, what is the safest practice when vehicles are approaching?
options: a:Always insist on the right-of-way when using a crosswalk.,b:Never enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching.,c:Enter a crosswalk at any time because drivers must stop.
note: Even when you have the right-of-way in a crosswalk, you should never step into the street if approaching vehicles are too close or moving too fast to stop safely. Make eye contact with drivers, wait until it is clearly safe, and then cross, continuing to watch for turning or inattentive drivers.

question: If an approaching driver fails to dim high beams, where should you focus your vision?
options: a:At the wheels of the approaching vehicle.,b:Toward the left side of the road.,c:Toward the right side of the road.
note: Bright high beams from oncoming traffic can temporarily blind you. To reduce glare, briefly look toward the right side of your lane, using the right edge of the road or the white line as a guide, while using your peripheral vision to track the oncoming vehicle and keep your car in your lane.

question: How should drivers equipped with ABS brake on snow or ice?
options: a:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.,b:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: With Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS), you should press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down, even on snow or ice. The ABS automatically pumps the brakes for you to help prevent wheel lockup and maintain steering control. Pumping the brakes yourself can interfere with the ABS and reduce its effectiveness.

question: If you borrow an unfamiliar vehicle, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Assume all vehicles operate the same and drive normally.,b:Ignore minor defects to avoid embarrassing the owner.,c:Take a few minutes to locate and test essential controls such as lights
note: Familiarizing yourself with an unfamiliar vehicle before driving is important for safety. Locate and test the lights, wipers, turn signals, horn, and mirrors so you can operate them quickly in traffic. Also check for obvious safety defects, such as bad tires or inoperative lights, and avoid driving the vehicle until serious issues are corrected.

question: If your vehicle has a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Signal and pull into the slow lane and continue driving.,b:Stop in your driving lane and leave hazard lights off.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and pull off the road to a safe location.
note: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, you should warn other drivers and move out of traffic. Turn on your hazard lights, signal, and carefully steer to the shoulder or another safe location off the roadway. Once stopped, keep your hazards on and, if available, use flares or reflective triangles so other drivers can see your disabled vehicle.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,b:Use cruise control when approaching railroad crossings to maintain speed.,c:You must stop when instructed by a flagger
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous, and trains have the right-of-way. You must stop when a flagger, stop sign, or active warning devices (flashing lights, gates, bells) tell you to. Never try to beat a train; it cannot stop quickly and always has priority over road traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never do?
options: a:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.,c:Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.
note: When changing lanes, you should always check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to clear your blind spot, and be aware of other drivers moving into the same lane. However, you should not change lanes by crossing the centerline while you are in an intersection, because traffic movements there are more complex and this can create unexpected conflicts with other vehicles and turning traffic.

question: What do your brake lights communicate to drivers behind you?
options: a:That you are turning right.,b:That your emergency brake is on.,c:That you are slowing down or stopping.,d:That you are changing lanes.
note: Brake lights warn drivers behind you that you are slowing down or stopping. This gives them time to reduce speed and maintain a safe following distance. Because they are a key safety feature, you must keep your brake lights clean and in good working order.

question: When you see a pedestrian with a white cane or guide dog crossing, what should you do?
options: a:Sound your horn and slowly pass.,b:Speed past to avoid delay.,c:Stop until the person is safely out of your path.,d:Carefully drive around them without stopping.
note: Blind pedestrians using a white cane or guide dog have the absolute right-of-way. You must stop and wait until they have completely crossed and are well clear of your vehicle before proceeding. Do not honk, rush past, or try to drive around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning onto a multi-lane street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:The middle lane.,b:The lane marked with an arrow only.,c:The lane closest to the one you came from.
note: When you turn onto a multi-lane street, you must turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are coming from. This keeps traffic organized and prevents side-swipe collisions with vehicles turning from the opposite direction.

question: Where is parking prohibited?
options: a:In a parking lot.,b:On a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane.,c:On a hill.
note: You may not park on a crosswalk or in a marked bicycle lane because these areas must remain clear for pedestrians and cyclists. Parking on a hill is allowed if it is not otherwise prohibited and you park legally, set the parking brake, and turn your wheels correctly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to other drivers?
options: a:Only when they are on a road to your left at an unmarked intersection.,b:Only when your traffic signal is a green arrow.,c:When entering a street from a garage
note: When entering a street from a driveway, alley, or garage, you must yield to traffic already on the road and to pedestrians on the sidewalk. Vehicles already on the roadway have the right-of-way, so you must wait until it is safe before pulling out.

question: What is the purpose of highway pavement markings?
options: a:They are only for construction zones.,b:They provide information and guidance for drivers.,c:They are usually not important.
note: Highway pavement markings are important safety devices. They provide information and guidance by showing lane boundaries, where passing is allowed, turn lanes, crosswalks, and other warnings so drivers can position their vehicles correctly and anticipate road conditions.

question: How should you drive in work zones?
options: a:Speed up to get through quickly.,b:Maintain your usual speed through the zone.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop; obey posted limits.
note: In work zones you must slow down, obey all posted work zone speed limits and signs, and be ready to stop suddenly for workers, equipment, or lane shifts. Fines are often higher in work zones, and driving carefully protects both workers and drivers.

question: If your tires feel like they have lost contact with the road surface, what should you do?
options: a:Pump the brakes quickly and firmly.,b:Shift into a lower gear to slow down.,c:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and avoid braking.
note: If your tires lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), gently ease off the accelerator and keep the steering wheel straight. Avoid braking or turning suddenly, because that can cause a skid. As your tires slow and water clears, they will regain traction.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is passing prohibited?
options: a:At intersections, curves, and railroad crossings.,b:Only where there is a broken center line.,c:On hills, curves, intersections, and railroad crossings where visibility is limited or signs/markings prohibit passing.,d:Only when there is oncoming traffic.
note: Passing is prohibited anywhere your view or safety is limited, such as on hills and curves, and it is also illegal at intersections and railroad crossings in most situations. You must not cross the center line to pass when you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic or where signs or road markings prohibit passing.

question: In the rain you should use which headlights?
options: a:Interior lights for visibility.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.,d:Parking lights only.
note: In rain, always use low beam headlights. Low beams help you see and be seen without causing glare from the raindrops. High beams can reflect off rain, fog, or snow and make it harder to see. Parking lights or interior lights alone do not provide enough visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?
options: a:The protected turning time is ending; prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up to complete your turn before the light changes.,c:You may turn without signaling.,d:The turn is protected until the next signal change.
note: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turning phase is ending. You should prepare to stop and must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians. If you are already in the intersection and cannot stop safely, you may complete the turn with caution before the signal changes.

question: What should you adjust first when you get into a car to drive?
options: a:Your seat position.,b:Your rearview mirror.,c:Your steering wheel tilt.
note: Before you start driving, adjust your seat so you can comfortably reach the pedals, steering wheel, and controls and have a clear view of the road. Once your seating position is correct, then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel so they work with your driving position.

question: If you are being tailgated, what should you do if there is an open lane to the right?
options: a:Never slow down abruptly.,b:If there is not an open lane to your right, c:Move over to the right.
note: If another driver is following too closely and there is an open lane to your right, safely move into that lane and let them pass. This reduces the risk of a rear-end collision. Never brake suddenly when being tailgated; instead, change lanes when safe or gradually slow to encourage the tailgater to pass.

question: When driving in fog, what should you do regarding lights and speed?
options: a:Turn your lights on and off to warn others.,b:Slow down and use high beam headlights.,c:Slow down and use low beam headlights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beam headlights so you can see and be seen. High beams can reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. If visibility becomes too poor to drive safely, pull completely off the road and wait until conditions improve.

question: Fatigue while driving increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being early for appointments.,c:Improved concentration over long trips.
note: Driving while tired slows your reactions, harms your judgment, and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. This greatly increases your chances of drifting out of your lane or missing hazards and can lead to serious crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where two vehicles arrive at exactly the same time, which vehicle proceeds first?
options: a:The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.,b:The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.,c:Drivers must make hand motions to communicate with each other.
note: At a four-way stop, if two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The vehicle on the right goes first when it is safe. Clear right-of-way rules help prevent confusion and collisions at intersections.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering interstate traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Force their way into traffic if necessary.,b:Expect other drivers to yield to them.,c:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.
note: When entering an interstate or freeway, you must yield to vehicles already on the highway. Use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, look for a safe gap, signal, and merge without forcing other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly.

question: A person using a white cane or guide dog is most likely to be:
options: a:A blind person.,b:A deaf person.,c:A person involved with a traffic study.
note: A person using a white cane or a guide dog is almost always a blind or visually impaired pedestrian. Drivers must always yield the right-of-way, use extra caution, and never honk or block their path. Stop well back from crosswalks so they can hear traffic and cross safely.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:Only if you are involved in a crash.,b:Only if you are stopped and cited.,c:Whenever stopped by an officer or involved in a collision or citation.
note: You must carry proof of financial responsibility (usually auto insurance) whenever you drive. Law enforcement can require you to show it if you are stopped for any reason, cited for a violation, or involved in a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you use your turn signal?
options: a:When changing lanes, pulling into or out of a parking space, or entering traffic from an alley or parking area.,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Only during the maneuver itself, not beforehand.
note: Turn signals must be used before you change lanes, turn, or move into traffic from a curb, driveway, alley, or parking space. Signaling in advance gives other road users time to see your intentions and adjust safely; do not wait until you are already making the maneuver.

question: To improve visibility in rain or fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:High beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, or snow, use low beam headlights. Low beams reduce glare and help you see the road while making your vehicle more visible to others. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and can make it harder for you and other drivers to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are waiting in an intersection to complete a left turn, how should your wheels be positioned?
options: a:Keep your wheels straight while waiting.,b:Turn your wheels to the left while waiting.,c:Flash your headlights to request right-of-way.
note: When waiting in an intersection to turn left, keep your wheels straight. If your wheels are turned and you are hit from behind, your vehicle can be pushed into oncoming traffic. With wheels straight, a rear-end impact is more likely to push you forward rather than into opposing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate highway, what should you do?
options: a:Always stop before entering the highway.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Select a safe gap and merge into the lane of traffic.
note: When merging onto an interstate, use the entrance ramp and acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of traffic, signal, choose a safe gap, and merge smoothly into a single lane of traffic. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never try to cross multiple lanes at once.

question: How can you avoid alcohol-related crashes?
options: a:Say no if someone offers you a drink while you're driving.,b:Decide before you start drinking that you will not drive.,c:Drink coffee to sober up.,d:Consume a small amount so you are safe to drive.
note: The safest way to avoid alcohol-related crashes is to decide before you drink that you will not drive and to arrange a sober driver or alternate transportation. Once you have been drinking, your judgment is impaired, so relying on a later decision is unsafe. Coffee, cold showers, or small amounts of alcohol do not make it safe to drive.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do first?
options: a:Move injured people immediately to a safer spot.,b:Ignore the accident if damage is minor.,c:Stop immediately and call for police or medical help if needed.,d:Keep driving to your destination.
note: If you are involved in a crash, you must stop at the scene, check for injuries, and call police or medical help if needed. If possible and safe, move vehicles out of traffic, but do not move seriously injured people unless there is immediate danger such as fire. Leaving the scene or ignoring the crash is illegal.

question: Which substances may impair driving and could lead to a DUII arrest?
options: a:Inhalants such as glue or paint.,b:Beer.,c:Controlled substances such as illegal drugs or some prescription medicines.
note: Driving can be impaired by any substance that affects your judgment, coordination, or reaction time. Alcohol (including beer), inhalants like glue or paint, illegal drugs, and even some prescription or over‑the‑counter medicines can all make it unsafe and illegal to drive. A DUI or similar impaired‑driving charge can result from alcohol, drugs, or a combination of substances, not just one type.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
