question: What is the correct way to use a freeway exit ramp?
options: a:Keep a constant freeway speed on the ramp.,b:Slow down to the exit speed before entering the ramp.,c:Begin slowing only after you are on the exit ramp.
note: On a freeway, maintain freeway speed until you have safely entered the exit ramp, then slow down to the posted ramp speed. Slowing on the main freeway lane can surprise drivers behind you and increase the risk of a rear‑end collision.

question: The habit of turning your head to check blind spots is:
options: a:A good driving habit.,b:Unnecessary.,c:A bad driving habit.,d:Only required when backing up.
note: Checking blind spots by briefly turning your head before changing lanes or merging is an important defensive driving habit. Mirrors do not show everything, so a quick glance over your shoulder helps you see vehicles, motorcycles, or bicycles that may be hidden.

question: You must report an accident when property damage to any one person's property is at least how much?
note: You must report a crash to law enforcement if there is an injury, death, or property damage of $1,000 or more to any one person’s property (different thresholds apply for government property).

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes on a highway, which steps should you take?
options: a:Signal only.,b:Increase your speed before changing lanes.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes.
note: When changing lanes on a highway, you should signal your intention, check your mirrors, and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot. Change lanes only when it is safe and without speeding up excessively or cutting off other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal shows a steady green arrow, what should a driver do?
options: a:Should slow to a stop if it is safe to do so.,b:Should merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.,c:May turn in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection.
note: A steady green arrow means you are allowed to turn in the direction of the arrow from the proper lane. Make the turn when it is safe, yielding to any vehicles or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you hear a siren behind you while driving, what is the correct response?
options: a:Speed up to get out of the way.,b:Stop immediately where you are without signaling.,c:Pull over to the right and stop to allow the emergency vehicle to pass.
note: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights from an emergency vehicle approaching from behind, you must safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, unless directed otherwise by police. This gives the emergency vehicle a clear path. Check mirrors and signal, move right when it is safe, and remain stopped until the vehicle has passed and it is safe to re-enter traffic.

question: Which technique helps maintain safe awareness while driving?
options: a:Using high beams in poor visibility.,b:Staring fixedly at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.
note: Good defensive driving means constantly being aware of what is happening all around your vehicle. You should scan ahead and check your mirrors every few seconds so you know what is beside and behind you. Avoid staring at one spot on the road, which reduces your ability to notice changing conditions and hazards.

question: Which roadway is most likely to be icy in cold weather after snow or rain?
options: a:A road in a shaded area,b:A hilly road,c:A residential road
note: In cold weather after snow or rain, shaded areas of the road are often the iciest because they receive less sunlight, so water and slush freeze sooner and melt later. Bridges, overpasses, and shaded curves can stay slippery even when other parts of the road look clear, so reduce speed and drive smoothly in these areas.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is steady yellow and you have not entered the intersection, what is the correct action?
options: a:Speed up to beat the red light.,b:Reduce speed and proceed without stopping.,c:Come to a safe stop.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you are expected to stop safely before the crosswalk or stop line. Only continue through a yellow if you are too close to stop safely when it first appears; you should never speed up to beat the red.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The largest vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:The car on the left has the right-of-way.,c:The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions. Always approach uncontrolled intersections slowly and be prepared to yield, especially if another vehicle is coming from your right.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a traffic control signal that is not working?
options: a:If the intersection appears clear,b:Treat the intersection as an all-way stop and come to a full stop before proceeding.,c:Drive quickly through to clear the intersection.
note: When a traffic signal is completely out (no lights in any direction), you must treat the intersection as an all‑way stop. Come to a complete stop at the limit line or before entering the crosswalk, then proceed only when it is your turn and the way is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your interstate exit, what should you do?
options: a:Quickly cut across traffic to reach the exit.,b:Keep driving to the next exit and use it to return safely.,c:Make a U-turn on the interstate.
note: If you miss your exit on an interstate or freeway, continue to the next exit. Do not stop, back up, cut across lanes, or make a U‑turn on the highway. Exit safely at the next opportunity and then re‑enter in the opposite direction if needed.

question: How is having a driver license best described?
options: a:Privilege.,b:Requirement.,c:Right.
note: A driver license is a privilege granted by the state, not a guaranteed right. You must meet requirements to obtain it, and it can be suspended or revoked if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: How should you check blind spots to see vehicles hidden from mirrors?
options: a:Use turn signals without looking.,b:Rely solely on the inside rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on outside mirrors.,d:Look over your shoulder.
note: Mirrors do not show areas directly alongside and slightly behind your vehicle, called blind spots. Before changing lanes or merging, quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to check these blind spots, in addition to using your mirrors and signals.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:Call your insurance company when you get home.,b:Leave a note with your name and address on the vehicle.,c:Wait at the scene until the owner returns.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, you must stop and leave a note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, address, and contact information, and report the collision as required by local law. This ensures the owner can reach you about the damage.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, you should:
options: a:Cautiously drive around them.,b:Honk and expect them to yield.,c:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,d:Speed up to pass before they finish.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even where no marked crosswalk exists.

question: How is drinking alcohol and driving classified as a traffic problem?
options: a:A minor traffic safety problem.,b:A serious traffic safety problem.,c:Safe if you have only had a few drinks.
note: Driving after drinking alcohol is treated as a serious traffic safety problem because it greatly reduces judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even a small amount of alcohol can impair driving and increase the risk of crashes, injuries, and deaths.

question: If you see a sign that says 'Reduced speed, 35 mph,' what does it mean?
options: a:The new 35 mph limit begins at that sign.,b:The new 35 mph limit starts at the next speed sign.,c:You have extra time to slow down before the reduced zone.
note: When you reach a sign that shows a reduced speed limit, the new speed limit applies starting at that sign. You should already be slowing so that by the time you reach the sign, you can travel at or below the posted reduced speed.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates?
options: a:When the train has passed.,b:Under no circumstances.,c:When the lights have stopped flashing.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around lowered railroad crossing gates. You must wait until the train has passed, the warning lights stop flashing, and the gates are fully raised before proceeding.

question: When passing a vehicle that has just parked at the side of the road, what should you assume?
options: a:You should speed up to pass quickly.,b:The driver will not open the door.,c:The driver may open a door or step out
note: When passing a recently parked vehicle, you should assume someone inside may open a door or step into your path without warning. Slow down if needed, leave extra space, and be ready to stop to avoid a collision with a door or pedestrian.

question: On average, how quickly does the body eliminate alcohol?
options: a:About two standard drinks per hour.,b:About three standard drinks per hour.,c:About one standard drink per hour.
note: The body typically metabolizes alcohol at about one standard drink per hour. This rate can vary with body size, sex, health, and how much food is in the stomach, but planning on only one drink per hour is a safe guideline for driving decisions.

question: Which combination gives the best protection in a collision?
options: a:No restraint at all.,b:Only a lap and shoulder belt.,c:Both lap/shoulder belt and an airbag.,d:Only an airbag.
note: The safest protection in a crash comes from using both the lap/shoulder belt and an airbag together. The seat belt keeps you properly positioned and prevents ejection, while the airbag provides extra cushioning in moderate to severe frontal crashes. Airbags are designed to work with seat belts, not replace them.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving considered a distraction?
options: a:It occupies the driver's hands and attention.,b:It is an activity that draws the attention of other drivers.,c:It causes the driver to be concerned about the cost of the call.
note: Using a cell phone while driving is dangerous because it takes your attention away from the driving task. It can occupy your hands, your eyes, and your mind, which slows your reaction time and makes it easier to miss hazards. Even hands‑free calls can be mentally distracting and increase crash risk.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a 'Yield' sign, what is your responsibility?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic close enough to cause conflict.,b:Always proceed without slowing.,c:Yield only to vehicles on your right.
note: At a Yield sign, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let cross or merging traffic go first if it is close enough to be a hazard. Only proceed when you can enter or cross the roadway without forcing other drivers, bicyclists, or pedestrians to slow or stop suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a crosswalk, who must yield?
options: a:Pedestrians must always wait for a green light before crossing.,b:Construction workers must yield to you.,c:You must yield to pedestrians in marked and unmarked crosswalks.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether they are marked or unmarked, when there is no traffic signal or when the signal gives pedestrians the right‑of‑way. You must slow or stop as needed so pedestrians can cross safely, especially in school zones and areas with heavy foot traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a left turn at an intersection, what must you do?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,b:You should never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:You should always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Wait until there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear before completing your turn.

question: How should you adjust your driving on slippery roads?
options: a:Always drive at the posted maximum speed.,b:Use cruise control to maintain a steady speed.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: On slippery roads, reduce your speed, increase your following distance, and make all steering, braking, and accelerating movements gently. Do not use cruise control, because you need full control to respond quickly if the vehicle begins to skid.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle traveling in the same direction, how should you pass?
options: a:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle being passed.,b:Pass as slowly as possible.,c:Pass as safely and as quickly as possible.
note: When passing, move into the passing lane, accelerate to pass the other vehicle promptly without exceeding the speed limit, and return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror. Lingering in the blind spot is unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a stop is required but there is no stop line or crosswalk, where should you stop?
options: a:Only if you can see at least 200 feet in both directions before stopping.,b:You are not required to stop.,c:At the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic without entering it.
note: If there is no stop line or crosswalk, stop at the point nearest the intersecting roadway where you can see approaching traffic, but before entering the intersection. This lets you check for cross traffic while keeping your vehicle out of the flow of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red?
options: a:Yes — if you entered on a yellow light it's acceptable.,b:Yes — if traffic is heavy and unavoidable.,c:No — you must not block the intersection under any circumstances.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you are sure you can clear it completely, even if the light is green or yellow. Blocking the intersection can trap cross traffic, create gridlock, and increase the risk of crashes.

question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?
options: a:Drivers may not pass.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions.,c:Drivers may pass or change lanes if it is safe.
note: A single dashed white line separates lanes moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, what should you expect?
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:Expect the child to be in total control of the bicycle.,c:Expect the unexpected.
note: Children on bicycles are often unpredictable and may suddenly swerve, stop, or enter your path. Slow down, give them extra space, and be prepared for unexpected movements.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What must you do when facing a green arrow signal?
options: a:Wait until the light turns yellow before proceeding.,b:Proceed in the direction of the arrow after yielding to traffic and pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Stop completely and wait for a green circular signal.,d:Proceed immediately without checking for traffic or pedestrians.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected turn in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians already in the intersection or still clearing it before you proceed.

question: What must you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?
options: a:Try to outrun it to reach your destination first.,b:Continue driving but stay out of its way.,c:Speed up and move into the emergency lane.,d:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and/or siren approaches from any direction, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping until it has passed, unless directed otherwise by law enforcement.

question: What greatly increases stopping distances and the severity of crashes?
options: a:Slow speeds,b:Night drives.,c:High speeds
note: At higher speeds, your vehicle needs a much longer distance to stop, and crash forces increase dramatically. This greatly raises both stopping distance and the severity of any collision.

question: Which action helps reduce road rage incidents?
options: a:Talk on your cell phone while driving.,b:Always signal when changing lanes.,c:Use your horn frequently.
note: Always using your turn signal when changing lanes or turning lets other drivers know what you plan to do. Clear communication reduces surprises, misunderstandings, and frustration, which helps prevent aggressive driving and road rage.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before changing lanes or turning must you signal by law?
options: a:You only need to signal when you are about to move into another lane or turn.,b:Signal only while you are turning or changing lanes.,c:Signal continuously for at least 100 feet before turning or changing lanes, and longer at higher speeds if required by local law.
note: The law requires signaling in advance — generally at least 100 feet — before changing lanes or turning.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,b:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,c:The speed you drive does not affect safety.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it causes other drivers to brake suddenly, change lanes, or make risky passing maneuvers. You should generally drive with the flow of traffic, but always within the posted speed limit and adjusted for conditions.

question: If you have a green light but pedestrians are crossing against the DON'T WALK signal, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if there are no cars.,b:Stop and allow the pedestrians to cross safely.,c:Honk to warn them and proceed,d:Speed up to get through before they reach your path.
note: Even if you have a green light and pedestrians are crossing against the signal, you must yield to them if they are in the crosswalk or your path. Stop and wait until they have safely crossed before you proceed.

question: The driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk. What is the correct action?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at 10 mph or slower.,b:Change lanes to go around the stopped vehicle.,c:Stop and remain stopped until you are sure the crosswalk is clear of pedestrians.
note: If the driver ahead of you stops at a crosswalk, you must also stop. There may be pedestrians in the crosswalk that you cannot see. Passing a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk is extremely dangerous and is illegal in many states because it puts pedestrians directly in your path.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors while driving?
options: a:Only when you are slowing down.,b:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Checking your mirrors often helps you stay aware of traffic behind and beside you so you can react early to lane changes, braking, or hazards. Do not wait only until slowing or turning; frequent quick glances keep you informed without taking your eyes off the road for long.

question: Before driving after a winter snowfall, what parts of your vehicle should you clear of snow and ice?
options: a:Turn signals only,b:Headlights only,c:Windows only,d:All windows, lights, and mirrors
note: Before driving after snow or ice, you must clear all windows so you can see in every direction, and you should also clear headlights, taillights, brake lights, and turn signals so other drivers can see you. Driving with snow or ice on glass or lights is unsafe and often illegal.

question: If you are worried, nervous, angry, or crying, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Should take the time to calm down and focus on driving before starting the engine.,b:Will drive no differently than they would if they were thinking more clearly.,c:Can drive faster because you are more in touch with your senses.
note: Strong emotions like anger, worry, or crying can distract you and slow your reaction time. Before driving, calm yourself and make sure you can focus fully on the road. If you cannot concentrate, wait until you are composed or have someone else drive.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may pass another vehicle if the line dividing your lane and the lane you wish to enter is what type of line?
options: a:Double solid yellow,b:Solid yellow,c:Broken white or broken yellow on your side of the road
note: You may only pass when the line next to your lane is broken, and it is safe and legal to do so. Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed to change lanes or pass. Solid yellow or double solid yellow lines mean passing is not allowed from your side.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, what is usually best practice?
options: a:Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.,b:Accelerate to a speed that matches freeway traffic and blend in.,c:Turn on your hazard lights until safely on the freeway.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of freeway traffic, then merge smoothly when there is a safe gap. Entering too slowly forces other drivers to brake or swerve and can cause collisions.

question: What are the colors of standard warning signs that indicate hazards ahead?
options: a:Red letters on a green background.,b:White letters on a blue background.,c:Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.,d:Black letters on a white background.
note: Standard warning signs that alert you to hazards ahead are usually yellow with black symbols or letters. These signs warn about curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, and other conditions that require extra caution. Orange warning signs are used in work zones to indicate construction or maintenance hazards.

question: Slowing down just to look at collisions or unusual events on the roadside typically:
options: a:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,b:Prevents rear-end collisions.,c:Causes traffic congestion.
note: Slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual on the roadside is called rubbernecking. It distracts you from the road, causes sudden slowdowns, and often leads to traffic congestion and rear-end collisions. Keep your attention on driving and maintain a safe, steady speed unless you must slow for safety or directions from officials.

question: If you have had several beers, which action will reduce the effects of alcohol?
options: a:Waiting several hours.,b:Drinking several cups of coffee.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Once alcohol is in your system, only time allows your body to metabolize it and reduce its effects. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks may make you feel more awake, but they do not lower your blood alcohol concentration or restore safe driving ability. If you have been drinking, you must wait long enough for the alcohol to wear off before driving.

question: Distracted drivers are at greater risk when using which device?
options: a:CD players.,b:Radio.,c:Cell phones (including hands-free devices).
note: Cell phones, including hands-free systems, are a major source of driver distraction because they take your mind off driving and often your eyes or hands as well. This greatly increases crash risk. While any in-car device can distract you if misused, phone conversations and texting are especially dangerous and should be avoided while driving.

question: When you see or hear an emergency vehicle with lights or siren, what must you do?
options: a:Pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, regardless of the direction it is coming from.,b:Only pull over if the emergency vehicle is following you.,c:Only pull over if it is approaching from the opposite direction.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with flashing lights or siren, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as close as safely possible to the right edge of the road and stopping until it has passed. This applies whether it is coming from ahead or behind, unless you are in a divided roadway where it is clearly separated by a median and moving in the opposite direction.

question: How do defensive drivers think and act?
options: a:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:They expect no breaks and give none.,c:They consider what other drivers might do and prepare to react.
note: Defensive drivers constantly scan the road, think about what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do next, and keep enough space and time to react safely. They do not assume others will always follow the rules; instead, they are prepared to slow, stop, or change lanes to avoid a collision.

question: How should you respond to a pedestrian who is blind and guided by a dog or carrying a white cane?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield the right-of-way if you are at a corner.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog is legally blind or visually impaired and is given special protection in traffic laws. You must always yield the right-of-way, stop well back from the crosswalk, and never honk or try to direct them. Let them find their way using their cane or dog, and only proceed when they are safely out of your path.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you reach an intersection where you want to turn but are not in the proper lane, what should you do?
options: a:Drive to the next intersection and make the turn from the proper lane.,b:Quickly cut across traffic to make the turn.,c:Turn from your current lane after signaling.
note: If you realize too late that you are in the wrong lane for a turn, you should continue straight and make your turn at the next safe intersection. Sudden lane changes or cutting across traffic can cause crashes because other drivers are not expecting your movement and may not have space or time to react.

question: If a driver is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot safely change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass.,b:Speed up to increase the gap.,c:Apply your brakes suddenly then resume speed.
note: When someone is following too closely and you cannot safely change lanes, the safest response is to maintain a steady speed and gradually slow down to increase the following distance and encourage the tailgater to pass when it is safe. Never slam on your brakes to “teach them a lesson,” because sudden braking can cause a rear-end collision and is considered aggressive driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you normally signal?
options: a:At least 100 feet before the turn.,b:At least 50 feet before the turn.,c:At least 25 feet before the turn.
note: You should signal well in advance of a turn—commonly about 100 feet before—so others know your intentions; among the choices, 75 feet is the closest.

question: What problem can result from continuous hard braking on ice or snow?
options: a:Locking the front wheels and losing steering control.,b:Helping you stop faster.,c:Keeping the brakes from freezing.
note: On ice or snow, pressing the brakes hard and continuously can cause the front wheels to lock. When the front wheels are locked, they slide instead of rolling, and you lose the ability to steer the vehicle. To maintain control on slippery roads, brake gently and progressively and steer smoothly, using longer following distances so you do not need hard braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If an officer is directing traffic at a signalized intersection, whom should you obey?
options: a:Honk at the officer.,b:Follow the directions given by the officer.,c:Follow the directions indicated by the traffic light.
note: When a police officer or other authorized person is directing traffic, you must follow their hand signals and instructions, even if traffic lights or signs show something different. The officer’s directions temporarily override the normal traffic control devices to keep traffic moving safely or to handle special situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Where there is a red traffic light.,b:Both of the above.,c:At any intersection where a police officer orders you to stop.
note: You are required to stop at steady red traffic lights and whenever a police officer or authorized person directs you to stop. Both situations are mandatory: traffic signals control normal flow, and officers can override or supplement those controls when needed. Failing to stop in either case is a traffic violation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching an intersection with a steady yellow light and you have not entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Stop safely before entering the intersection if you can do so.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Proceed through the intersection at the same speed.
note: A steady yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you have not yet entered the intersection, you should stop before the crosswalk or stop line if you can do so safely. If you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through the intersection with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear-end collision.

question: What is the purpose of rumble strips on the road?
options: a:To test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,b:To alert drivers to tire problems.,c:To provide traction for motorcycles.,d:To alert inattentive drivers via sound and vibration that they have left the travel lane.
note: Rumble strips are raised or grooved patterns on the road that create noise and vibration when you drive over them. This alerts inattentive or drowsy drivers that they are drifting out of their lane or approaching a hazard, such as a stop sign, toll plaza, or work zone, giving them time to correct their path.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean regarding passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed only from your direction of travel.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means no passing is allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: To improve visibility during rain or fog, use which lights?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or sleet, always use low beam headlights. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and actually make it harder to see.

question: Which statement is true about drowsy driving?
options: a:Opening a window or turning up the radio is enough to stay alert.,b:Drinking strong black coffee is a reliable way to remain safe to drive.,c:Drowsy drivers can perform so poorly they may appear impaired or drunk.
note: Drowsy driving can slow your reaction time, impair judgment, and cause you to drift out of your lane, similar to a drunk driver. Tricks like opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking coffee are not reliable; the only real solution is rest or switching drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Reduce speed and proceed with caution.,b:Stop, then proceed when it is safe to do so.,c:Stop completely
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to pedestrians and other traffic, and then proceed only when it is safe. You do not remain stopped the entire time it is flashing; you stop, check, then go when clear.

question: If a train is approaching and is a danger, what must you do?
options: a:Pass other vehicles to get through first.,b:Cross quickly if you think you can beat it.,c:Not cross the tracks until the train has completely passed.,d:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: If a train is approaching and could be a danger, you must not cross the tracks. Wait until the train has completely passed and the tracks are clear in both directions before crossing. Never try to beat a train; trains are much faster and closer than they appear and cannot stop quickly.

question: Large vehicles compared with smaller cars generally have:
options: a:Smaller blind spots.,b:Larger blind spots.,c:No blind spots.
note: Larger vehicles like trucks, buses, and large SUVs have bigger blind spots than smaller cars. These blind spots are areas around the vehicle that the driver cannot see using mirrors alone, especially directly behind, along the sides near the rear, and sometimes in front of the vehicle. Because of this, you should avoid lingering alongside or close behind large vehicles.

question: What do pennant-shaped traffic signs signify?
options: a:Speed limits.,b:No passing zones.,c:School zones.
note: Pennant-shaped signs are yellow and point to the right; they are used exclusively to mark the beginning of a no passing zone. They are usually placed on the left side of the road to warn drivers that passing other vehicles is not allowed in that area.

question: If a lane is separated by a single broken white line on a highway, what are you allowed to do?
options: a:You cannot cross the line to pass.,b:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.,c:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross a broken white line to change lanes or pass another vehicle when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check mirrors, signal, and check your blind spot before moving into another lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is a good general rule to follow regarding passing?
options: a:Try to get to the front of slow-moving traffic at all costs.,b:Pass on the right whenever possible.,c:Drive with the flow of traffic and pass only as needed.
note: A safe passing rule is to drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit and pass only when necessary and clearly safe. Passing increases your risk because it requires moving into another lane, often into oncoming traffic on two-lane roads. Never pass just to be first in line or if you cannot complete the pass safely within the legal speed limit.

question: Who must wear seat belts in a moving vehicle under Wisconsin law?
options: a:Only children under 16 years old.,b:Only the driver.,c:Everyone in the vehicle.
note: Wisconsin law requires the driver and all passengers to wear seat belts in a moving vehicle, with very limited exceptions. Seat belts greatly reduce the risk of serious injury or death in a crash by keeping occupants from being thrown around inside the vehicle or ejected.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement, what is the safest way to return to the road?
options: a:Stop quickly on the shoulder and then pull back on.,b:Accelerate and sharply steer back onto the road.,c:Slow down
note: If your right wheels drop off the pavement, keep a firm grip on the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow down gradually. Once the car is under control and there is a clear gap in traffic, gently steer back onto the pavement. Sudden braking or jerking the wheel can cause you to lose control or skid into traffic.

question: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, what is the safest reaction?
options: a:Stay calm and move out of the aggressive driver's way.,b:Flash your vehicle's lights to let the aggressive driver know he is wrong.,c:Call the police immediately.
note: If an aggressive driver cuts you off, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and create space by slowing down or changing lanes when safe. Do not retaliate or try to teach the other driver a lesson. If the behavior is extreme or ongoing, you may report it later from a safe location, but your first priority is to avoid escalation and get out of their way.

question: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicates you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed immediately.,b:Not pass other vehicles.,c:Expect a traffic signal ahead.
note: A solid yellow line on your side of the centerline means you must not pass other vehicles because sight distance or other conditions make passing unsafe. You may cross it only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe to do so.

question: If you park in an unusual area, what should you ensure?
options: a:Park with your reverse lights on.,b:Park five feet from the curb.,c:Make your vehicle visible to approaching drivers from any direction.
note: When you must park in an unusual or nonstandard area, make sure other drivers can clearly see your vehicle from all directions. Use your lights or hazard flashers if needed and avoid locations where your parked vehicle could surprise approaching traffic or block their view.

question: When is it appropriate to use your horn?
options: a:When traveling through an intersection.,b:When passing a bicyclist.,c:When you see a child who is about to run into the street.
note: Use your horn to warn others of a potential collision, not as a routine signal. If you see a child about to run into the street, a quick horn tap can alert the child and nearby drivers to prevent a crash. Avoid using the horn unnecessarily, such as just because you are passing a bicyclist or moving through a normal intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in an intersection and an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Drive slowly and let it pass without pulling over.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection and remain there.,c:Continue through the intersection
note: If an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches while you are already in an intersection, you should continue through the intersection to clear it, then pull to the right side of the road and stop. Stopping in the middle of the intersection can block the emergency vehicle and create additional hazards.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline on a roadway indicate?
options: a:A construction zone is ahead.,b:Passing is permitted from either direction when safe.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and indicates that passing is allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction when it is safe and legal to do so. Drivers must still check for oncoming traffic, ensure sufficient passing distance, and obey any additional signs or restrictions.

question: What is the most important rule about speed in curves?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed entering the curve and then slow at the sharpest part.,b:Accelerate gently before entering the curve.,c:Slow down before you enter the curve.
note: You should slow down before entering a curve so your vehicle is at a safe, controlled speed as you go through it. Braking hard while already in the curve can cause loss of traction and control, especially in poor conditions.

question: Which activities can cause distracted driving?
options: a:Eating, drinking, smoking, changing radio stations, or using a cellphone.,b:Only talking on a phone.,c:Only changing a CD.
note: Distracted driving includes any activity that takes your eyes off the road, your hands off the wheel, or your mind off driving. Eating, drinking, smoking, changing radio stations, and using a cellphone all reduce your attention and increase crash risk.

question: Regarding pedestrians, what must a driver do?
options: a:Make sure the pedestrian sees the vehicle before proceeding.,b:Yield only when the pedestrian is legally entitled to it.,c:Yield the right-of-way to all pedestrians
note: Drivers must use extreme care around pedestrians and do everything possible to avoid hitting them. You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in crosswalks and should be prepared to yield even when a pedestrian is crossing unexpectedly or outside a crosswalk to prevent a collision.

question: What happens to tire effectiveness as speed increases on a wet roadway?
options: a:Water does not affect cars with good tires.,b:Deep water is less dangerous than shallow water.,c:As you drive faster on wet roads, your tires lose effectiveness and your risk of hydroplaning increases.
note: As speed increases on a wet roadway, your tires have less time to squeeze water out from under the tread. This reduces traction and increases the risk of hydroplaning, where your tires ride on top of the water and lose contact with the road. Slowing down in wet conditions helps your tires maintain grip.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you change lanes?
options: a:Quickly and often.,b:Gradually and carefully.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: You should always change lanes gradually and carefully. Check your mirrors, signal, look over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and move smoothly into the next lane when it is safe. Avoid sudden or frequent lane changes, which increase the risk of a collision.

question: What do yellow centerlines on the roadway separate?
options: a:Carpool lanes from regular lanes.,b:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,c:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.
note: Yellow centerlines separate traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads. A broken yellow line means you may pass when it is safe, while a solid yellow line means you may not cross it to pass.

question: Is it legal to drive under the influence of a medication that impairs your driving?
options: a:Yes — if you do not feel drowsy.,b:Yes — if a physician prescribed it.,c:No — driving under the influence of impairing medication is not permitted.
note: It is illegal and unsafe to drive under the influence of any substance that impairs your ability to drive safely, including prescription or over-the-counter medications. If a medication affects your alertness, coordination, or judgment, you must not drive while using it.

question: An arrow painted on the pavement in your lane means:
options: a:You must stop before making the movement indicated by the arrow.,b:You may choose to ignore it if no other traffic is present.,c:Drivers in that lane must make the movement indicated by the arrow.
note: Arrows painted on the pavement show the required or permitted direction of travel from that lane. If the arrow shows a turn, drivers in that lane must make that turn when it is safe and allowed by signals; you may not go straight if the lane is marked for turns only.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are in a designated left-turn lane and oncoming traffic is present, what should you do before turning?
options: a:Turn your front wheels left to be ready.,b:Move to the left of the center lane immediately.,c:Signal before you reach the intersection and keep wheels straight until safe to turn.
note: When waiting to turn left, signal in advance and keep your front wheels pointed straight while you wait for a safe gap. If your wheels are turned left and another vehicle hits you from behind, your car can be pushed into oncoming traffic, causing a serious head‑on collision.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which lights should you use?
options: a:Low-beam headlights.,b:High-beam headlights.,c:Parking lights only.
note: Use low‑beam headlights when following another vehicle at night so you do not shine bright lights into the driver’s mirrors. High beams can blind or distract the driver ahead, increasing the risk of a crash. Low beams provide enough light for you to see while reducing glare for others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your lane after passing another vehicle, what should you make sure of?
options: a:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Beep your horn.
note: After passing another vehicle, do not move back into your original lane until you can see both of the passed vehicle’s headlights in your inside rearview mirror. This tells you there is enough space between your vehicle and the one you passed, so you can return safely without cutting them off.

question: What must you do at a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights?
options: a:Stop well behind the gates and wait until they are lifted and the tracks are clear.,b:Drive around the gates if you do not see a train.,c:Slow down and creep around the gates.
note: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you must stop well behind the gate and wait. Do not drive around or under the gates, even if you do not see a train. Trains are fast and cannot stop quickly, and signals may activate before you can see the train approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a highway marked by double solid yellow lines, you may:
options: a:Cross only to make a left turn into or from an alley, private road, or driveway.,b:Cross to pass slower vehicles when no oncoming traffic is present.,c:Cross these lines under no circumstances.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and mean that passing is not allowed from either direction. However, you may carefully cross these lines to make a left turn into or out of a driveway, alley, or side road when it is safe and legal to do so.

question: When driving in fog, which lights should you use?
options: a:Four-way flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:High beam headlights.
note: In fog, you should always use low‑beam headlights. High beams reflect off the water droplets in the fog and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams aim light down toward the road and reduce glare, improving your ability to see lane lines and the edge of the road.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Closer behind the truck than usual.,b:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.,c:Farther back than you would for a passenger car.
note: Large trucks need more time and distance to stop and have big blind spots directly behind them. By staying farther back than you would behind a passenger car, you give yourself more time to react and make sure the truck driver can see you in their mirrors.

question: What lane width entitlement do motorcycles have?
options: a:The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.,b:Only half the lane width.,c:Only the bicycle lane.,d:They must share the lane with other motorcycles only.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to use a full traffic lane, just like any other motor vehicle. You should not crowd them or share their lane; instead, give them the same space and respect you would give a car.

question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum recommended following distance?
options: a:Two seconds.,b:Six seconds.,c:Four seconds.
note: Under ideal conditions, leave at least four seconds between you and the vehicle ahead to allow enough time to react and stop if necessary.

question: If you hit an unattended parked vehicle and cannot find the owner, what must you do?
options: a:You have done enough if you drive away.,b:Leave a written notice with your name and contact information.,c:Wait until the police arrive and do nothing else.
note: If you hit a parked vehicle and cannot locate the owner, you must stop and leave a written note in a secure, visible place on the vehicle with your name, contact information, and a brief description of what happened. In many states you are also required to promptly report the collision to law enforcement.

question: Signs that require drivers to obey specific directions are called:
options: a:Information signs.,b:Warning signs.,c:Regulatory signs.
note: Regulatory signs are the signs you are legally required to obey. They include speed limit signs, stop signs, yield signs, and other signs that state traffic laws or required actions. Ignoring these signs can result in tickets or other penalties.

question: Compared to daytime driving, how hazardous is driving at night?
options: a:No more or less dangerous.,b:More dangerous because of reduced visibility and increased chances of impaired or tired drivers.,c:Less dangerous.
note: Driving at night is more dangerous than daytime driving because you can see less of the road, it is harder to judge distance and speed, and there is a higher chance of encountering tired or impaired drivers. Always slow down and increase following distance at night.

question: Which is an effective measure to reduce the risk of hydroplaning?
options: a:Ensure you always drive at the posted speed.,b:Reduce your speed when driving in the rain.,c:Keep your tires dramatically underinflated to increase contact area.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road, which is more likely at higher speeds. To reduce the risk, slow down in rain, avoid standing water, and keep your tires properly inflated with good tread. Underinflating tires is unsafe and does not prevent hydroplaning.

question: On a dimly lit street at night, how should you drive with respect to what your headlights illuminate?
options: a:Use high beams to better see the road ahead.,b:Keep instrument panel lights bright for visibility to others.,c:Drive slowly enough to be able to stop within the area lit by your headlights.
note: At night you must drive at a speed that allows you to stop within the distance you can see with your headlights. This is called not overdriving your headlights. If you cannot stop in the area they illuminate, you are going too fast for the conditions.

question: When approaching a school bus with its stop arm extended, how should drivers respond?
options: a:Come to a complete stop and wait to proceed.,b:Honk before passing on the left.,c:Continue driving if you believe children are not present.
note: When a school bus has its stop arm extended and red lights flashing, drivers in most situations must stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the lights stop flashing. This protects children who may be crossing the road. Some states have specific rules for divided highways, but you should always be prepared to stop when you see a school bus loading or unloading children.

question: When a steady green arrow is displayed, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles in the intersection.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only after the green arrow turns off.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected movement in that direction. You may proceed in the direction of the arrow if you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear, but you must still yield to any pedestrians in the crosswalk and vehicles already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your turn or exit on a freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and turn there safely.,b:Stop and back up on the shoulder.,c:Make a quick U-turn on the freeway.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you must never stop, back up, or make a U‑turn on the freeway. Continue driving to the next exit, leave the freeway there, and then find a safe route to go back to your intended exit.

question: Is it permitted to park on the shoulder of a freeway?
options: a:Only in an emergency.,b:If no part of your vehicle is on the road.,c:As long as you turn on your four-way flashers.
note: On freeways, stopping or parking on the shoulder is generally illegal except for emergencies, such as a breakdown or medical issue. You may stop on the shoulder only when it is truly an emergency and it is safe to pull completely off the roadway, with hazard lights on if possible.

question: What does a flashing yellow arrow for left turns allow you to do?
options: a:Must come to a complete stop.,b:May turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,c:Should merge into the lane in the arrow's direction without yielding.
note: A flashing yellow arrow for a left turn means you may turn left, but the turn is not protected. You must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, and only turn when there is a sufficient gap and it is safe to complete the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper sequence for changing lanes?
options: a:Check mirrors, signal, then change lanes without checking blind spots.,b:Signal, check mirrors, check blind spot, then change lanes when safe.,c:Speed up then signal.,d:Signal and change lanes immediately.
note: The proper lane-change sequence is: first signal your intention, then check your mirrors, quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot, and finally change lanes only when it is safe. Signaling alone is not enough; you must also confirm that the lane is clear before moving.

question: If your vehicle is equipped with airbags, what is true about seat belts?
options: a:Seat belts should be worn only behind the back.,b:Seat belts are not necessary.,c:Seat belts should still be worn.
note: Airbags are designed to work together with seat belts, not replace them. In a crash, the seat belt keeps you properly positioned and prevents you from being thrown forward, while the airbag cushions the impact. You should always wear the lap and shoulder belt correctly, even in vehicles equipped with airbags.

question: What is the effect of excessive speed on crash severity?
options: a:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,b:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.,c:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.
note: The faster you are going, the more energy your vehicle has and the longer it takes to stop. In a crash, this extra energy is transferred to people and vehicles, which greatly increases the chance of serious injury or death. Excessive speed also reduces your time to react and avoid hazards.

question: When is it legal to cross center yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the vehicle ahead moves to the right to let you pass.,b:When the yellow line on the opposite side is broken.,c:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. You may only cross them to pass when the line next to your lane is broken and it is safe to do so. If the line next to your lane is solid, you are not allowed to pass, even if the line on the other side is broken.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, what should you remember about traction?
options: a:Your tires do not have as much traction as they do on pavement.,b:Visibility is better than on pavement.,c:Your tires grip the road better than when you are driving on pavement.
note: On gravel or dirt roads, the loose surface reduces how well your tires can grip the road. This means it takes longer to stop and your vehicle can slide or skid more easily, especially when turning or braking hard. You should slow down and drive smoothly to maintain control on these surfaces.

question: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing to load or unload children, drivers must:
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and then pass cautiously.,b:Proceed once you think the children have cleared the roadway.,c:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and the stop arm extended, traffic in both directions (unless on a divided highway with a physical median, per state law) must stop. You must remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn, because children may be crossing the road and can be hard to see.

question: How must you yield the right-of-way to an emergency vehicle using siren and flashing lights?
options: a:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it has passed.,b:Stop immediately,c:Drive as closely to the right edge of the road as possible and stop.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches using its siren and flashing lights, you must move as far to the right side of the road as you safely can and come to a complete stop. Stay stopped until the emergency vehicle has passed. Do not block intersections and do not keep driving alongside or in front of the emergency vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer orders you to stop even though the traffic light is green, what should you do?
options: a:Obey the traffic signal.,b:Obey the officer.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings. If an officer tells you to stop, you must stop even if the traffic light is green. Follow the officer’s instructions carefully and proceed only when directed to do so.

question: Approaching a railroad crossing with no gates or flashing lights but a crossbuck, what should you do?
options: a:Only continue once cleared to do so by a flagger,b:Turn your radio down to hear if there may be an approaching train.,c:Approach all tracks with extreme caution and cross only when you know that there is no train coming.
note: At a railroad crossing with only a crossbuck and no gates or flashing lights, you must slow down, look and listen for trains in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Cross only when you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline means traffic is moving in opposite directions and passing on the left is allowed when it is safe and the way ahead is clear. You must still check for oncoming traffic and ensure you can complete the pass without speeding or cutting off another vehicle.

question: Before stopping your vehicle at a traffic signal or sign, you should first:
options: a:Press down hard on the accelerator.,b:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,c:Set the parking brake.
note: Before stopping for a traffic signal or sign, check your mirrors so you know how close vehicles behind you are and how fast they are approaching. This helps you brake smoothly and gives drivers behind you time to react, reducing the risk of being rear-ended.

question: To avoid losing traction on wet roads, you should:
options: a:Brake firmly.,b:Make abrupt turns.,c:Slow down.
note: On wet roads, your tires have less grip and can hydroplane. Slowing down is the best way to keep traction because it reduces the water buildup under your tires and gives you more time to react. If you start to lose control, ease off the gas, avoid hard braking or sudden steering, and gently steer in the direction you want to go.

question: A red arrow pointing right on a traffic signal means:
options: a:You may not turn in that direction until the light changes to green.,b:You may turn after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:You may turn after you come to a complete stop.
note: A solid red arrow means you must stop and you may not turn in the direction of the arrow. You must wait until the signal changes to green or a green arrow appears before making the turn, unless a specific sign allows turns on red arrows in that jurisdiction. Treat it like a red light for that direction of travel.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When driving in traffic, the safest approach is to:
options: a:Fluctuate your speed to keep alert.,b:Drive with the flow of traffic at a safe speed.,c:Always drive slower than the flow to be cautious.,d:Drive faster than most traffic.
note: Driving at a speed that matches the flow of traffic, while staying within the posted speed limit and adjusting for conditions, is usually safest. Large speed differences between you and other vehicles increase the risk of collisions because other drivers may not anticipate your much slower or faster speed.

question: When must drivers yield to pedestrians?
options: a:Only if the pedestrian is on the same side of the road as the driver.,b:Even if the pedestrian crosses the street carelessly.,c:Only when the pedestrian is in a crosswalk.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and often at unmarked crosswalks, and must do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian, even if the pedestrian is crossing carelessly or against a signal. You are responsible for using caution and yielding when a pedestrian is in your path, regardless of who technically has the right-of-way.

question: When should you look over your shoulder to check a blind spot?
options: a:Pulling toward or away from a curb.,b:Turning left or right.,c:Changing lanes.,d:Both a and c.
note: Blind spots are areas you cannot see in your mirrors. You should look over your shoulder whenever you change your vehicle’s lateral position, such as when changing lanes or pulling toward or away from a curb, to be sure no one is in your blind spot.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a freeway, how should your speed compare to traffic on the freeway?
options: a:You should drive much more slowly than freeway traffic.,b:You should be driving at or near the speed of freeway traffic.,c:You should always be at the posted speed limit regardless of traffic.
note: When using a freeway on‑ramp, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed that matches the flow of traffic, as long as it does not exceed the speed limit. Matching the speed of traffic makes it easier and safer to merge because you are not forcing other drivers to brake or swerve.

question: The effect that lack of sleep has on driving ability is most comparable to the effect of what?
options: a:The effect that amphetamines have.,b:The effect that alcohol has.,c:The effect that anger has.
note: Driving while very tired affects you much like alcohol: it slows your reaction time, harms your judgment, and makes it harder to stay in your lane or notice hazards. Being awake for a long time can impair you to a level similar to having alcohol in your system, which is why drowsy driving is so dangerous.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, how should you drive?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Speed up to maintain momentum.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, your tires have less grip, so it takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid. You should slow down below the posted speed and drive smoothly, allowing extra space so you can brake and steer gently without losing control.

question: If a pedestrian with a guide dog is at a corner ready to cross, what should you do before turning right?
options: a:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.,b:Wait until the person crosses the street.,c:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.
note: A pedestrian using a guide dog or white cane has the right‑of‑way. When you are turning and they are at the corner ready to cross, you must stop and wait until they have safely crossed the street before you turn. Do not give verbal instructions or rev/turn off your engine to signal them; simply yield and allow them to cross independently.

question: What color are pavement markings that separate lanes moving in opposite directions?
options: a:Yellow and white.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions, such as the centerline on a two‑way road. White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction and also mark the right edge of the roadway.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs typically indicate:
options: a:Regulatory instructions.,b:General warning signs.,c:Construction and maintenance warning areas.
note: Orange signs are used for construction and maintenance warning areas. They alert drivers to road work, lane shifts, workers, and other temporary conditions so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which sign that you can see in your rearview mirror tells you it is safe to return to the driving lane after passing?
options: a:When the driver you passed waves you back.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror. This shows you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return safely without cutting them off.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you in a no-passing zone, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the road to let them pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Maintain your speed and position so they can re-enter safely.
note: If another driver is passing you, even in a no‑passing zone, you should maintain a steady speed and lane position. Sudden speeding up or slowing down can create a collision risk. Holding a consistent speed helps the passing driver complete the maneuver and return to the lane safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is a permitted way to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Pass by using the shoulder of the highway.,b:Pass in a curve or on a hill because the chance of oncoming traffic is small.,c:None of these are permitted.
note: You may not pass on the shoulder or in areas where you cannot see oncoming traffic, such as sharp curves or hills. Passing is only allowed where it is clearly legal and you have enough clear sight distance to do so safely. If your only choices are using the shoulder or passing on a curve or hill with limited visibility, neither is permitted.

question: When are roads most slippery during a rainstorm?
options: a:After it has been raining for several hours.,b:The day after it rains.,c:For the first 10 to 15 minutes of a rainstorm.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first 10–15 minutes of a rainstorm. Oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the new rainwater and create a slick film, reducing traction until the buildup is washed away.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Interstate driving requires which of the following?
options: a:Both the ability to safely drive at higher speeds and constant alertness.,b:Only the ability to drive fast.,c:Only occasional alertness.
note: Interstate driving usually involves higher speeds, heavier traffic, and more lane changes. To drive safely, you must be able to control your vehicle at high speed and stay constantly alert to changing traffic and road conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it ever permissible to drive off the roadway onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only if the vehicle ahead is turning left.,b:No — under no circumstances.,c:Only when there are two or more lanes in your direction.
note: On most U.S. roads, it is illegal and unsafe to drive off the paved roadway or onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies, not for passing, and using it to pass can lead to collisions with vehicles re‑entering the lane or stopped on the shoulder.

question: How can stress affect your driving?
options: a:It decreases the likelihood of an accident.,b:It lowers your ability to concentrate on driving.,c:It causes you to fall asleep at the wheel.
note: Stress and strong emotions can distract you, narrow your attention, and slow your decision‑making. This reduces your ability to concentrate on traffic, signs, and hazards, which increases your risk of making mistakes and being involved in a crash.

question: When following another vehicle at night, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Use your high beam headlights.,b:Use your high beams until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.,c:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.
note: When you follow another vehicle at night, you must use low‑beam headlights so your lights do not shine directly into the driver’s mirrors and blind them. High beams are only for use when you are not following closely behind someone and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: Why should drivers be extra alert for motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians?
options: a:They are harder to see and are less protected than motorists.,b:They follow different traffic laws.,c:They always have the right-of-way.
note: Motorcyclists, bicyclists, and pedestrians are smaller and can be hidden in blind spots or by other vehicles, and they have little or no protection in a crash. Because they are harder to see and more vulnerable to injury, drivers must watch carefully and give them extra space.

question: What adjustment should you make to your following distance when driving at night?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use high beams to improve visibility.,c:Look directly at oncoming headlights to judge distance.
note: At night you cannot see as far ahead, and hazards are harder to detect. You should increase your following distance so you have more time to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Use your headlights correctly and avoid looking directly at oncoming headlights so you are not blinded.

question: What does an advisory (curve/turn) speed sign indicate?
options: a:May be ignored in rainy conditions if traffic is light.,b:Shows a recommended driving speed for the curve and should be reduced in adverse conditions.,c:Is yellow with black lettering.
note: An advisory speed sign shows the recommended safe speed for a specific curve or turn under ideal conditions. It is not a mandatory speed limit, but you should treat it seriously and slow down, especially in rain, snow, or other adverse conditions, because your vehicle will have less traction and may not handle the curve safely at higher speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:If you might hit another vehicle.,b:When visibility ahead is limited.,c:Near blind pedestrians.
note: Use your horn to warn others when there is a risk of a collision, such as when another driver may not see you. Do not use your horn around blind pedestrians; they rely on consistent sound cues and can be startled or disoriented by sudden honking. Instead, slow down, yield, and pass only when it is clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?
options: a:When the car in front of you is disabled.,b:When turning left into a driveway.,c:When doing so would interfere with traffic.
note: A single broken line (white between lanes in the same direction, yellow between opposite directions) means you may cross it to pass or change lanes only when it is safe. You must not cross if doing so would interfere with oncoming traffic or vehicles behind you; you need enough space and time to complete the maneuver without forcing others to slow or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the intersection is blocked by traffic ahead while you face a green light, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the vehicles ahead and enter the intersection.,b:Turn left and find another route.,c:Stay out of the intersection until traffic ahead clears.
note: A green light means you may go only if the intersection is clear. If traffic ahead is stopped and you cannot fully clear the intersection, you must wait behind the stop line until there is enough space. Entering and stopping in the intersection can block cross traffic when the light changes and may result in a citation.

question: What should be your first response when visibility is reduced?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Turn on windshield wipers only.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: When visibility is reduced by fog, heavy rain, or snow, you should immediately turn on your low‑beam headlights so others can see you more easily. You should also reduce your speed and use wipers as needed, but making your vehicle visible with headlights is the first key step for safety.

question: If your vehicle does not have ABS and you must stop quickly, what should you do?
options: a:Hold down the brake pedal without releasing.,b:Firmly pump the brake pedal.,c:Tap the brakes lightly and repeatedly.
note: In a vehicle without ABS, you should firmly pump the brakes to slow or stop quickly. This helps prevent the wheels from locking, which allows you to maintain some steering control. In an ABS‑equipped vehicle, you would instead press the brake pedal firmly and hold it down.

question: If you are emotionally upset when you get to your car after a work incident, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Play loud music to drown out thoughts.,b:Drive fast on the interstate to let off steam.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before you begin driving.
note: Strong emotions like anger or frustration can seriously affect your judgment, reaction time, and attention. If you are upset, you should wait and take a few minutes to calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road and make safe decisions.

question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always do what to check for hazards?
options: a:Stop,b:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings, you must actively scan for hazards by looking left, right, and ahead along the sides of your vehicle. Constantly checking to the sides helps you see pedestrians, cyclists, trains, and cross traffic that may enter your path, so you can react in time.

question: If you hear a siren but can't see the emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down but do not stop until you see it.,b:Pull to the curb and stop so you can check if it is on your street.,c:Keep driving until you see the vehicle.
note: When you hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle, you should safely pull as far to the right as possible and stop. Staying stopped until you are sure the vehicle is not approaching your path helps keep the way clear for emergency responders and prevents sudden conflicts in traffic.

question: If you experience a tire blowout while driving, which is correct?
options: a:Tap or pump the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Do not brake hard; use your brakes lightly only after you have the vehicle under control, then move off the road safely.

question: How does smoking or preparing to smoke while driving affect your driving?
options: a:It helps keep you alert.,b:It is a distracting activity that can take your hands or eyes off the road.,c:It has no effect.
note: Smoking or preparing to smoke while driving is a distraction. It can take one or both hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road, increasing the chance of a crash. Any activity that diverts your attention or control from driving is unsafe.

question: Which of these statements about passing a motorcycle is true?
options: a:A motorcycle with two people is always more stable than one with a single rider.,b:It is acceptable for other drivers to follow motorcycles very closely.,c:The driver of a passenger vehicle must change lanes completely when passing a motorcycle.
note: Motorcycles are entitled to a full lane, just like any other vehicle. When passing, you must move completely into the adjacent lane and never crowd or share the lane with the motorcycle.

question: Which statement is true about alcohol's effect on mental and driving skills?
options: a:Alcohol does not affect driving skills.,b:Only a BAC above the legal limit will impair these skills.,c:Even the smallest amount of alcohol can limit concentration
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can slow your reaction time, reduce concentration, and impair judgment. There is no amount of alcohol that is guaranteed to be safe for driving, even if it is below the legal BAC limit.

question: What is the most common color for warning signs?
options: a:Green,b:Yellow,c:Red
note: Most general warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow with black symbols or words. They alert drivers to conditions such as curves, intersections, or pedestrian crossings ahead.

question: What does a steady red traffic signal require you to do?
options: a:Stop at the stop line (or, if none, before the crosswalk or intersection).,b:Stop only if there is a pedestrian in the crosswalk.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: At a steady red light you must stop before entering the intersection. If there is a stop line, you stop at that line. If there is no stop line but there is a crosswalk, you stop before entering the crosswalk. If neither is present, you stop before entering the intersection. The legal requirement is to stop at the first of these that applies, not to pull up into the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic from a curb, what should you do?
options: a:Should wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Should wait for the first two vehicles to pass.,c:Should enter and drive well below the speed of other traffic for a while.
note: When pulling away from a curb into moving traffic, you must signal, check mirrors and blind spots, and wait for a gap large enough to let you accelerate up to the speed of traffic without forcing others to brake suddenly.
