You do not just wait for an arbitrary number of vehicles to pass, and you should not enter and drive significantly slower than traffic if you can safely avoid it.

question: Which factor does NOT affect stopping distance?
options: a:The condition of your vehicle's brakes.,b:Your reaction time.,c:The time of day.
note: Stopping distance is made up of reaction distance and braking distance. It is affected by your reaction time, the condition of your brakes and tires, vehicle weight, speed, and road surface conditions. The time of day by itself does not change how far it takes the vehicle to stop, even though it may affect visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a steady red traffic light, a driver should:
options: a:Continue because they have the right-of-way.,b:Proceed through the intersection if there is no traffic.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped until it turns green or a permitted turn is completed.
note: A steady red means stop. Drivers may turn right on red after yielding, unless prohibited by sign.

question: If your vehicle begins to hydroplane, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid braking.,b:Maintain or increase speed to push through the water.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to slow the vehicle quickly.
note: Hydroplaning happens when your tires ride on top of water and lose contact with the road. If this occurs, ease off the accelerator and slow down gradually, keeping the steering wheel straight. Avoid braking or making sudden turns until your tires regain traction, because hard braking can cause a skid and loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, into which lane should you turn?
options: a:Into the second lane if it is unobstructed.,b:Into any lane you prefer.,c:Into the first available lane of the one-way street.
note: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, you must turn into the first available lane going your direction, which is the lane closest to you on the one-way street. This keeps traffic organized and prevents conflicts with vehicles already in or entering other lanes.

question: If the road ahead is flooded, what is the safest action?
options: a:Turn around and find another route.,b:Drive in the center of the roadway.,c:Slam on the brakes immediately.
note: If the road ahead is flooded, you should never try to drive through the water. Even shallow water can hide deep holes, debris, or washed-out pavement, and moving water can sweep a vehicle away. The safest choice is to turn around and find another route.

question: What should you expect from children playing near the road?
options: a:They will know when it is safe to cross.,b:They will follow crossing signals.,c:They may run into the street without looking.,d:They will always stop at the curb before crossing.
note: Children near the road are unpredictable and may suddenly run into the street without looking. As a driver, you should slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop quickly because children often do not judge traffic speed or danger correctly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is correct when changing lanes or passing on an interstate?
options: a:You should always use cruise control.,b:Stop on the shoulder of the road if you are tired.,c:Signal, check your mirrors, and glance over your shoulder before changing lanes or passing.
note: When changing lanes or passing on an interstate, you must always signal to let other drivers know your intentions. In addition to signaling, check your mirrors and quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot before moving into another lane. Use the shoulder only for emergencies, and do not rely on cruise control for lane changes or passing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If the traffic light turns from green to solid yellow as you approach an intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Consider it the same as a caution sign and continue without slowing.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Stop before entering the intersection unless you are too close to stop safely.
note: A solid yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You must stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are too close to the intersection to stop safely when the light turns yellow, continue through with caution rather than braking hard and risking a rear-end collision.

question: Like alcohol and drugs, what effect can drowsiness have on driving?
options: a:It can impair judgment and slow reaction time.,b:It improves alertness.,c:It makes you a better driver.
note: Drowsiness affects driving much like alcohol or drugs. When you are sleepy, your reaction time slows, your awareness of what is happening around you drops, and your judgment becomes less reliable. This makes it harder to notice hazards and respond in time, greatly increasing crash risk.

question: Which types of drugs can impair driving?
options: a:Only marijuana.,b:Illegal drugs.,c:Many drugs, including illegal, prescription, and over-the-counter medicines, can impair driving.
note: Many different drugs can impair driving, including illegal drugs, prescription medications, and over‑the‑counter medicines such as some cold or allergy remedies. Any drug that makes you drowsy, affects your thinking, or slows your reactions can make it unsafe and often illegal to drive. Always read labels and follow medical advice before driving after taking any medication.

question: Where are stop lines typically painted?
options: a:In curves and on hills.,b:At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.,c:Next to churches and schools.
note: Stop lines are solid white lines painted across traffic lanes at intersections and before crosswalks. They show you the exact place to stop so you do not enter the crosswalk or intersection while waiting for a signal or sign.

question: What can help drivers conserve gasoline while driving?
options: a:Accelerating quickly at every green light.,b:Sitting in the driveway with the engine running.,c:Slowing down gradually instead of braking hard and accelerating again.
note: To conserve fuel, drive smoothly by looking ahead, easing off the accelerator early, and slowing down gradually instead of braking hard and then speeding up again. Rapid starts and stops waste gasoline and put more wear on your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, when may you turn left onto another one-way street?
options: a:Only when traffic on the street you are turning into moves to the left.,b:When traffic on that street moves to the right.,c:Only if you increase your speed before the turn.
note: On a one‑way street, you may turn left onto another one‑way street only if traffic on the street you are turning onto flows to the left. You must make the turn from the proper lane, obey any signs or signals, and yield to pedestrians and other traffic.

question: What happens to your field of vision as you increase your vehicle's speed?
options: a:Makes it easier to see cross traffic.,b:Decreases your field of vision.,c:Increases your field of vision.
note: As your speed increases, your side (peripheral) vision effectively narrows and you see less of what is happening to the sides of the road. This reduced field of vision makes it easier to miss hazards, pedestrians, or cross traffic, which is why you should slow down when conditions are complex or visibility is limited.

question: When facing an aggressive driver, what is the safest response?
options: a:Avoid eye contact, slow down, let them pass, and increase distance.,b:Cut them off to slow them down.,c:Retaliate by tailgating.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, the safest response is to avoid any confrontation. Do not make eye contact, do not gesture, and do not try to block or race them. Instead, slow down slightly, let them pass, and increase your following distance so you have more time and space to react if they do something unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a turn, how should you change your speed?
options: a:Reduce your speed to maintain control.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Vary your speed unpredictably.
note: Before and during a turn, you should slow to a safe speed so you can maintain full control of the vehicle and stay in your lane. Enter the turn at a reduced speed, then gently accelerate as you complete the turn if conditions allow. Speeding up into a turn makes it easier to skid or drift out of your lane.

question: What is the safest way to cross railroad tracks?
options: a:Rely only on gates to tell you when to cross.,b:Listen and look both ways,c:Cross quickly when a train is approaching.,d:Proceed if the red lights are not flashing.
note: At railroad crossings, always slow down, look and listen carefully in both directions, and be prepared to stop. Never rely only on gates or lights; a malfunction is possible. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming and there is enough space to clear the tracks completely without stopping on them.

question: Before changing lanes on a multilane highway you should do which of the following?
options: a:Turn on your headlights.,b:Check mirrors and blind spot; signal your intention.,c:Sound your horn.
note: Before changing lanes, check your rearview and side mirrors, then quickly glance over your shoulder to check your blind spot in the direction you want to move. Signal well in advance to let other drivers know your intention, and only move when it is safe and there is enough space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic signals are not functioning due to a power outage, how should drivers proceed at the intersection?
options: a:Turn on your hazard lights and proceed through the intersection without stopping.,b:Park your vehicle as far off the road as possible and wait for power to be restored.,c:Treat the intersection as a four-way stop and proceed when it is your turn.
note: When traffic signals are completely dark due to a power outage, you must treat the intersection as an all-way (four-way) stop. Come to a complete stop, yield to vehicles that arrived first, and then proceed cautiously when it is your turn and the way is clear.

question: What is a common effect of eating or drinking while driving?
options: a:Have trouble staying in their lanes and controlling their vehicle.,b:Are better drivers because they are not hungry.,c:Make no driving errors.
note: Eating or drinking while driving is a form of distracted driving. Your hands, eyes, and attention are partly off the driving task, which can cause you to drift out of your lane, react more slowly, and have more difficulty controlling the vehicle safely.

question: Which statement is true about seat belts and child restraints?
options: a:You should always make sure all your passengers are using a seat belt or child restraint.,b:You should never place a rear-facing infant restraint in the front seat of a vehicle with airbags.,c:All of the above,d:An airbag can be dangerous to an infant or small child
note: Safe use of restraints means: always ensure every passenger is properly buckled, use child restraints that match the child’s age and size, and never place a rear-facing infant seat in front of an active airbag because the airbag can seriously injure or kill an infant or small child.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Interior dome light.,b:Parking lights only.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog because their light pattern aims down toward the road and reduces glare. High beams reflect off the water droplets in fog and can bounce light back into your eyes, making it harder to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you are turning or changing lanes, when must you signal?
options: a:Always signal your intentions in advance, even if no visible traffic is present.,b:Only signal when other vehicles are present.,c:Only signal when driving at night.
note: You must always signal before turning or changing lanes, even if you do not see other traffic. Signaling in advance gives other road users time to react and is required by law in all normal driving conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate from a ramp, what should you do after checking for a gap?
options: a:Expect traffic to allow you to enter since you have the right-of-way.,b:Merge carefully into the gap after accelerating to match traffic speed.,c:Wait for the lane to clear completely before merging.
note: When entering an interstate, use the ramp and acceleration lane to reach the speed of traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and then merge smoothly into a safe gap. Do not assume other drivers will yield to you; you must adjust your speed and position to merge safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals?
options: a:Only during the maneuver itself,b:Only when other traffic is present.,c:Whenever you turn, change lanes, or enter traffic, signal in advance to alert others.
note: Turn signals should be used every time you turn, change lanes, or enter traffic from a parked position, driveway, or alley, and they must be activated well in advance of the maneuver. Signaling early gives other drivers time to see your intentions and adjust safely, even if you think no one is around.

question: When changing lanes, which of the following should you NOT forget to do?
options: a:Neglect side and rearview mirrors.,b:Fail to signal at all.,c:Check for other drivers who may also be moving into the same lane.
note: Before changing lanes, always check your mirrors, look over your shoulder to check blind spots, and signal your intention so others know what you plan to do. Failing to signal at all is dangerous because nearby drivers cannot anticipate your lane change and may collide with you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where should your vehicle be positioned when making a right turn?
options: a:Near the center of the roadway.,b:Close to the left side of the street.,c:As close as possible to the right side of the road.
note: For a right turn, you should position your vehicle as close as safely possible to the right edge or curb. This shortens the turn, keeps you out of oncoming traffic, and prevents other vehicles or cyclists from trying to squeeze by on your right.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what sequence of actions should you take?
options: a:Do not immediately use your brakes and gradually slow down before pulling off the road.,b:Take your foot off the gas and immediately apply the brakes.,c:Gradually slow down and then speed up.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, because it can cause you to lose control. Once you have slowed and the vehicle is stable, carefully steer to the side of the road and stop in a safe place.

question: If you are driving in another vehicle's blind spot, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,c:Stay in the blind spot to avoid being seen by others.
note: Staying in another driver’s blind spot is dangerous because they may change lanes or turn without seeing you. Either gently speed up to move ahead where you can be seen in their mirrors, or slow down to fall back so you are clearly visible. Avoid lingering alongside another vehicle.

question: Which of the following is a telltale sign of a drunk driver?
options: a:They are weaving between lanes.,b:They are driving more slowly than the normal traffic flow.,c:They are making quick and sudden stops.
note: Impaired drivers often show several warning signs, including weaving between lanes, driving much slower than the flow of traffic, making sudden or erratic stops, drifting, or inconsistent speeds. Any of these behaviors can indicate a drunk or impaired driver and should make you increase your following distance and avoid passing close to them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How long before turning should you signal?
options: a:Immediately as you begin the turn.,b:Only when other vehicles are nearby.,c:At least 100 feet before turning, which is usually about three to four seconds in city driving.
note: Activate turn signals roughly three to four seconds before making the turn to alert others of your intent.

question: When parking on any hill, what steps should you take?
options: a:Let one rear wheel touch the curb.,b:Leave front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.,c:Set the parking brake, leave the transmission in Park (or in gear), and turn the front wheels so the vehicle would roll away from traffic if it moved.
note: Whenever you park on a hill, always secure the vehicle by setting the parking brake and leaving the transmission in Park (or in gear for a manual). Turn the front wheels so that if the brakes fail, the vehicle will roll away from traffic: turn wheels toward the curb or road edge when facing downhill, and away from the curb when facing uphill with a curb. Never rely on just the transmission to hold the car.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situations should you not attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only when the speed limit is low.,b:On a hill or curve or in any area where your view of oncoming traffic is blocked or passing is prohibited.,c:When on a divided highway, even if signs or markings prohibit passing.
note: You must not pass when you cannot clearly see oncoming traffic, such as on hills or curves, or in marked no‑passing zones. Passing is also prohibited at intersections, railroad crossings, and when there is a solid yellow line on your side. On a divided highway, you may pass when it is legal and safe, using the proper lane.

question: How can you avoid being in a truck or bus driver's blind spot?
options: a:Never pass them.,b:Avoid driving alongside them and avoid tailgating.,c:Flash your headlights at them.
note: Large trucks and buses have big blind spots along both sides and directly behind them. To stay visible, avoid driving right next to them for long periods and do not follow closely. Either pass safely and promptly or drop back so the driver can see you in their mirrors.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, if another vehicle arrives at the same time and is on your right, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and yield to the vehicle on your right.,b:Drive into the intersection and make the other vehicle stop.,c:Speed up and get through the intersection.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals), if you and another vehicle arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. Slow down, let the vehicle on your right go first, and then proceed when it is safe. Never speed up to beat the other driver into the intersection.

question: What is a safe method to drive through a curve?
options: a:Slow down before entering the curve and gently speed up as you exit.,b:Maintain a constant speed through the whole curve.,c:Speed up entering and slow down exiting.
note: Before entering a curve, slow down so you can steer smoothly and keep good control. As you go through the curve and can see the road ahead clearly, gently accelerate as you exit. Braking hard in the middle of a curve can cause skidding or loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, what should you do to ensure it is safe?
options: a:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move and check mirrors.,b:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror and then move.,d:Make the move quickly without signaling.
note: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move. This head check lets you see vehicles in your blind spot that mirrors may miss. Signal, make sure the lane is clear, and then change lanes smoothly.

question: Which statement about sudden changes in weather is true?
options: a:You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.,b:Be particularly aware of vehicles coming up behind you in inclement weather.,c:A sudden change in weather calls for a change in driving.
note: When the weather changes suddenly—such as rain, fog, snow, or strong wind—you must adjust how you drive. Slow down, increase your following distance, and use the correct lights so you can see and be seen. Changing conditions always require changing your driving behavior.

question: If you become tired while driving, what is the best action?
options: a:Drink coffee and continue driving.,b:Open a window and keep driving.,c:Stop to rest or switch drivers.
note: If you feel drowsy, the safest choice is to stop and rest or change drivers. Short-term fixes like coffee are not reliable.

question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:Yes — it's always the safest practice.,b:No — driving too slowly can block traffic and be unsafe.,c:Yes
note: You should drive at a speed that is safe for conditions and within the speed limit, not simply slower than everyone else. Driving much slower than the normal flow, without a good reason, can cause other drivers to brake or change lanes suddenly and may be illegal if you block traffic. Adjust your speed to weather, visibility, and traffic, while staying near the general flow when it is safe and lawful.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After stopping at a stop sign, in what order should you scan the intersection?
options: a:Look left first, then right, then left again.,b:Look right first, then left, then right again.,c:Check your rearview mirror for tailgaters.
note: At a stop sign, you must come to a complete stop and then scan carefully before entering the intersection. Look left first because traffic from the left is usually closer to you, then look right, and then look left again just before you move. This pattern helps you detect any vehicles, bicycles, or pedestrians that may have entered your path while you were checking the other side.

question: Before driving, what should you remove from your vehicle?
options: a:Only the windshield and passenger window.,b:Only the windshield.,c:All snow, ice, and frost from windows, mirrors, lights, and as much as practical from the roof and hood.
note: Before driving in snowy or icy conditions, you must clear all snow, ice, and frost from your vehicle so you can see in every direction and so debris does not blow off and endanger others. This includes all windows, mirrors, lights, and often the roof and hood, not just the windshield or one side window. Full visibility and preventing snow from flying off your car are important for safe driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive slower than the flow of traffic, what may happen?
options: a:You will demonstrate defensive driving.,b:You will improve traffic flow.,c:You may interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.
note: Driving so slowly that you obstruct the normal movement of traffic can earn you a citation; match the flow when safe and lawful.

question: How many behind-the-wheel driving hours must an applicant under 18 complete before applying for a probationary license?
options: a:40 hours total,b:30 hours total,c:50 hours total
note: In many states, drivers under 18 must log at least 50 hours of supervised driving, including a required number of night hours, before applying for a probationary or intermediate license. These hours help new drivers gain enough real-world experience in different conditions to drive safely on their own.

question: If another driver cuts you off, what should you do?
options: a:Flash your high beams repeatedly.,b:Pull alongside and yell at them.,c:Speed up and tailgate them.,d:Let it go and continue driving safely.
note: If another driver cuts you off, stay calm and avoid reacting with aggression. Do not speed up, tailgate, or confront the other driver. Instead, slow slightly if needed, create a safe following distance, and continue driving defensively. This reduces the risk of a crash and helps prevent road rage incidents.

question: Is it legal to cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Only if there is no oncoming traffic.,b:No.,c:Yes.
note: A double solid yellow centerline means passing is not allowed for traffic in either direction. You may cross double solid yellow lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway, side road, or alley, or when directed by law enforcement or traffic control. You may not cross them just to pass another moving vehicle.

question: When driving near heavy trucks you must allow for:
options: a:The truck's ability to swerve quickly.,b:The reduced size of truck blind spots.,c:The increased stopping distance required by large vehicles.,d:The decreased stopping distance of trucks.
note: Large trucks and other heavy vehicles need much more distance to stop than passenger cars because of their size and weight. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them, do not brake suddenly, and give them extra space so they have enough room to stop safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver who arrived before you.,b:The driver on your left.,c:The driver across from you.,d:The driver who signals first.
note: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive: the first vehicle to stop is the first to go. If two or more vehicles arrive at the same time, the driver must yield to the vehicle on their right. Clear communication with turn signals and making eye contact can help, but right-of-way is based on arrival order and position, not on who signals first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which technique helps avoid crashes on snow- or ice-covered roads?
options: a:Get off highways as quickly as possible.,b:Add extra weight to the vehicle to improve traction.,c:Reduce your speed and increase following distance.
note: On snow or ice, you should slow down and leave much more space between you and the vehicle ahead. Lower speed gives you more time to react and reduces the chance of skidding, and extra following distance allows for the much longer stopping distances on slippery roads.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean about passing?
options: a:Passing is allowed only from your direction.,b:Passing is allowed from both directions.,c:Passing is not allowed from either direction.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed from either direction. You may cross these lines only to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe, but you may not cross them to pass another vehicle.

question: Which behavior describes an inattentive driver?
options: a:Stares at objects off the roadway or daydreams while driving.,b:Maintains eye contact during a conversation with a passenger while driving.,c:Only watches the vehicle ahead of their vehicle.
note: An inattentive driver is not fully focused on the driving task. Daydreaming or staring at objects off the roadway takes your eyes and mind away from traffic conditions, which greatly increases the risk of missing hazards and being involved in a crash.

question: If you are driving and a tire suddenly goes flat, what should you do?
options: a:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,b:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.,c:Slow down gradually and not brake.
note: If a tire suddenly goes flat or blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly, ease your foot off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down gradually. Avoid hard braking, which can cause loss of control. Once you have slowed and the vehicle is stable, steer to a safe place off the road and stop.

question: What is true about double solid yellow lane markings?
options: a:Both lanes may pass.,b:Neither lane may pass.,c:The lane to the right may pass.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and indicate that passing is prohibited for vehicles in both directions. You must stay in your lane and may only cross these lines to turn left into or out of a driveway or side road when it is safe.

question: What is a good habit to relieve fatigue on a long trip?
options: a:Do arm exercises every hour.,b:Drive with one eye open at a time.,c:Stop and rest every two hours.
note: On long trips, fatigue builds up and slows your reactions. A good habit is to stop and rest about every two hours so you can stretch, walk around, and refresh yourself. If you feel drowsy, you should find a safe place to rest or stop for the day rather than trying to fight sleep while driving.

question: What single practice most reduces your risk of injury or death in a crash?
options: a:Staying in the right lane on multilane highways.,b:Limiting driving to weekdays.,c:Wearing your seat belt.
note: Wearing your seat belt is the single most effective way to reduce your risk of serious injury or death in a crash. Seat belts keep you from being thrown from the vehicle, spread crash forces over stronger parts of your body, and help you stay in position to control the vehicle.

question: In rainy weather, when are turning and stopping most hazardous?
options: a:After it has been raining all day.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:During the first half hour of rain.
note: Roads are most slippery during the first part of a rainstorm. Oil and other residues on the road surface mix with the fresh rainwater and create a slick film, making turning and stopping especially hazardous during roughly the first half hour of rain. As the rain continues, much of this residue is washed away and traction gradually improves, though you should still drive with caution.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, the best action is to:
options: a:Stop driving and rest.,b:Open your window to get fresh air.,c:Drink caffeine and continue driving.,d:Turn up the radio volume.
note: When you start to feel tired while driving, the safest choice is to stop driving and rest. Fatigue slows your reaction time and affects judgment much like alcohol. Opening a window, turning up the radio, or drinking caffeine may make you feel more awake briefly, but they do not restore alertness enough to drive safely.

question: What does Wisconsin's Implied Consent Law require of drivers?
options: a:Penalties become more severe after a first OWI conviction.,b:Drivers must submit to alcohol testing when requested by a police officer.,c:Drivers under age 21 cannot drive after drinking any alcohol.
note: Under Wisconsin’s Implied Consent Law, anyone who drives on Wisconsin roads has already agreed to take a chemical test (such as a breath, blood, or urine test) if a law enforcement officer lawfully requests it. Refusing the test can lead to license suspension and other penalties, separate from any OWI charge.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution.,c:Stop before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means you do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it acceptable to stop in a travel lane on the roadway?
options: a:You may stop to drop off passengers.,b:None of the above,c:You may stop to look up an address.,d:You may make a U-turn or back up if you get on the wrong entrance ramp of the freeway.
note: You should not stop in a travel lane except for reasons like traffic, signals, or emergencies. Do not stop in a moving lane to drop off passengers, look for an address, or back up or make a U‑turn on a freeway ramp. If you miss a turn or exit, continue to the next safe place to turn around.

question: Blue traffic signs provide information about:
options: a:Construction and maintenance.,b:Motorist services (rest areas, gas, food, lodging, hospitals).,c:Regulatory requirements.,d:Distance to cities.
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, hospitals, and other facilities that may be needed while traveling.

question: How should you check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Only use the outside mirrors.,b:Turn your head to look over your shoulder to check the blind spot.,c:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.
note: Every vehicle has blind spots that mirrors cannot show. Before changing lanes, quickly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure no vehicle is in your blind spot.

question: A badly worn or defective suspension can cause:
options: a:Squealing brakes.,b:Slack in the steering.,c:Vehicle control problems.
note: A worn or defective suspension system makes it harder to control the vehicle, especially over bumps or in turns. It can cause poor stability, increased body roll, and longer stopping distances, all of which increase the risk of losing control.

question: Which of these does NOT affect blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:How much time passes between drinks.,b:Your body weight.,c:The type of alcoholic beverage you drink.
note: Blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is mainly affected by how much alcohol you drink, how quickly you drink it (time between drinks), and your body weight and metabolism. The type or brand of alcoholic beverage does not change how your body processes alcohol; a standard drink has about the same amount of alcohol whether it is beer, wine, or liquor.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood can affect what?
options: a:Only your knowledge.,b:Your right-of-way privileges.,c:Your judgment and physical coordination.
note: Any amount of alcohol can begin to affect your judgment, coordination, and reaction time, even if you are below the legal limit. This makes it harder to make safe decisions, respond quickly, and control the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is blocking the intersection when your light turns green, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter the intersection to establish your right-of-way.,b:Don't enter the intersection until you can get completely across.,c:Continue into the intersection and wait for traffic to clear.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless there is enough space to completely clear it, even if the light is green. Entering when you cannot get through blocks cross traffic and is illegal and unsafe.

question: Which driving skills are affected by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Only reaction time and coordination.,b:Only alertness and concentration.,c:All of the above (alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination).
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect all major driving skills. They reduce alertness and concentration, slow reaction time, and harm coordination and judgment, making it harder to notice hazards and control the vehicle safely.

question: For drivers 21 or older, driving with what minimum BAC is illegal?
options: a:0.02 percent.,b:0.08 percent.,c:0.05 percent.
note: In most U.S. states, it is illegal for drivers 21 and older to operate a vehicle with a BAC of 0.08% or higher. Even lower levels can be unsafe, but 0.08% is the typical legal limit for a DUI per se violation.

question: When must you always stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:If the crossing is in a city or town with frequent trains.,b:If there isn't room on the other side for your vehicle to completely clear the tracks.,c:Only if you are carrying two or more children.
note: You must never drive onto railroad tracks unless there is enough space on the other side for your entire vehicle to clear the tracks completely. If traffic or a signal would make you stop on the tracks, you must wait before the crossing until you can fully clear it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway from an on-ramp you should:
options: a:Enter slowly and traffic must yield to you.,b:Stop before merging and wait for a large gap.,c:Speed up beyond traffic to force your way in.,d:Signal, use the acceleration lane to match freeway speed, and merge when safe while yielding to freeway traffic.
note: When entering a freeway, you should signal, use the on‑ramp and acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic, and then merge when it is safe, yielding to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not stop on the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and never force your way in.

question: Orange-colored traffic signs are used to indicate:
options: a:School zones.,b:Work zones and construction.,c:Regulatory requirements.,d:Hospital services.
note: Orange traffic signs and devices are used in work zones and construction areas. They warn drivers about road work, maintenance operations, and temporary traffic control changes so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In a roundabout who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Drivers entering the roundabout.,b:Drivers intending to go straight across.,c:Drivers already circulating in the roundabout.,d:Pedestrians only.
note: In a roundabout, drivers already circulating inside the roundabout have the right‑of‑way. Drivers approaching and entering must slow down, yield to traffic in the circle and to pedestrians in crosswalks, and only enter when there is a safe gap.

question: To help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, what should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Speed up to enter curves and slow to exit.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.
note: To avoid skidding on slippery surfaces, slow down before you enter a curve or intersection. Braking hard while you are turning can cause your tires to lose traction and the vehicle to skid, especially on wet, icy, or sandy roads.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When backing up, what should you do to see clearly?
options: a:Press hard on the gas pedal to move quickly.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Look directly through the rear window over your right shoulder.
note: When backing up, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window over your right shoulder, using your mirrors only as a supplement. Back up slowly and be ready to stop if anything enters your path.

question: Which factor affects how alcohol is absorbed by the body?
options: a:Height,b:Intelligence,c:Weight
note: Alcohol affects people differently based on factors like body weight, biological sex, how much and how quickly they drink, and whether they have eaten. Intelligence and height do not meaningfully change how alcohol is absorbed or how impaired you become.

question: If your accelerator becomes stuck while driving, what is the correct sequence of actions?
options: a:Slam on your brakes.,b:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.,c:Turn off the ignition using care, after shifting to neutral and steering to safety.
note: If your accelerator sticks, keep your eyes on the road and steer straight, shift to neutral if possible, and turn off the ignition without locking the steering wheel. Then apply the brakes and steer to a safe place off the road. Never turn the key so far that the steering locks, and avoid slamming on the brakes while the engine is still pushing the car forward.

question: While passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:
options: a:Drive closely to the parked vehicles to make room for moving traffic.,b:Be prepared for a person or vehicle to unexpectedly enter your lane.,c:Assume pedestrians will wait for you to pass.
note: When passing parked vehicles, leave extra space and be ready for doors to open, cars to pull out, or pedestrians to step from between vehicles. Expect the unexpected and adjust your speed and lane position so you can stop or steer away safely.

question: A good driver should monitor which areas around the vehicle?
options: a:Only directly in front of the car.,b:Only the middle of the road.,c:All around the vehicle, including front, sides, and rear.
note: A safe driver constantly scans all around the vehicle: ahead, to the sides, and behind. Checking mirrors and blind spots helps you see vehicles, pedestrians, and other hazards in time to react safely, instead of focusing only on what is directly in front of you.

question: If an emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you, what is the proper action?
options: a:Stop immediately and prevent them from passing.,b:Make every effort to give the emergency vehicle a clear path of travel.,c:Speed up to avoid the emergency vehicle.
note: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights and siren approaches, you must yield the right‑of‑way. Safely move to the right side of the road and stop if possible, so the vehicle has a clear path. Never speed up or block their way.

question: Why might a large truck need to swing wide when turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction?
options: a:May complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,b:May have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,c:Must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Large trucks have a much wider turning radius and the rear wheels track closer to the curb than the front wheels. To avoid hitting the curb, parked cars, or other vehicles, a truck may need to swing wide when turning right, especially on multi‑lane roads.

question: Why is a leaky exhaust system dangerous?
options: a:A loss of hearing.,b:Pollution.,c:Carbon monoxide poisoning.
note: A leaky exhaust system can let carbon monoxide enter the passenger compartment. Carbon monoxide is colorless and odorless and can quickly cause sickness, unconsciousness, or death. Any exhaust leak should be repaired immediately.

question: If you experience a sudden tire blowout while driving, how should you react?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly,b:Apply the brakes firmly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: If a tire blows out, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the vehicle going straight. Ease your foot off the accelerator and let the car slow down gradually. Do not slam on the brakes, because hard braking can cause you to lose control. When the vehicle has slowed, steer to a safe place off the road and stop.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what emergency action should you take?
options: a:Flash your headlights.,b:Start to prepare to slow down slowly.,c:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, you should immediately slow or stop and use a sharp blast of your horn to warn them. The horn is used to alert others to danger, not to express anger. Always be prepared to brake quickly in these situations.

question: How is a driver distraction defined?
options: a:Anything that improves safety.,b:Anything that makes you drive slower.,c:Anything that causes you to focus more on driving.,d:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.
note: A driver distraction is anything that takes your attention away from the driving task. This can be visual (eyes off the road), manual (hands off the wheel), or cognitive (mind off driving). Any of these increase crash risk because you are not fully focused on traffic, road conditions, and vehicle control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you respond to a flashing yellow traffic signal?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop.,c:Speed up to clear the intersection.,d:Turn on hazard lights.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution, not stop. You must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards, and continue through the intersection only when it is safe. Treat it as a warning, not a stop signal.

question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what is the best action?
options: a:Stay in your car and wait for help.,b:Get out and walk for help immediately.,c:Lay down and sleep in the car.
note: If you are stranded in a snowstorm, it is usually safest to stay with your vehicle. The car provides shelter and is easier for rescuers to see than a person on foot. Run the engine only periodically for heat, keep the exhaust pipe clear of snow, and conserve fuel while waiting for help.

question: What do temporary construction signs look like?
options: a:Green background with white writing.,b:Orange background with black writing.,c:Red background with white writing.,d:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Temporary construction and work zone signs are typically orange with black letters or symbols. The orange color alerts drivers that they are entering a work area and should slow down, watch for workers and equipment, and be prepared for lane shifts or sudden stops.

question: If you drink socially, what helps ensure a safe trip home?
options: a:Ride home with a friend who has not been drinking.,b:Drink coffee before driving.,c:Take a cold shower before driving.
note: If you have been drinking, the only safe choice is not to drive. Arranging a ride with a sober driver, using a taxi or rideshare, or planning a designated driver before you drink are safe options. Coffee, cold showers, or other tricks do not lower your blood alcohol level or make you safe to drive.

question: If there are two adjacent railroad tracks and one train passes, what should you do?
options: a:You must always stop before crossing the tracks.,b:Look for another train on the other track before proceeding.,c:It is always safe to proceed after one train passes.
note: When there are multiple railroad tracks, you must never assume it is safe to cross just because one train has passed. Another train may be coming on the other track, sometimes hidden by the first train. After the first train clears, wait, look, and listen carefully in both directions and only proceed when you are sure no other trains are approaching.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross a dashed white line?
options: a:At any time even if unsafe.,b:When it is safe to change lanes.,c:Only during daylight hours.
note: Broken (dashed) white lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross them to change lanes or pass, but only when it is safe and legal to do so. Always check mirrors, signal, and check blind spots before moving.

question: What does a flashing yellow traffic signal tell drivers to do?
options: a:Stop as if it were a stop sign.,b:Yield to all pedestrians.,c:Proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow traffic signal means you must slow down and proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to stop for other vehicles, pedestrians, or hazards in the intersection.

question: Why should you increase your following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:Because other drivers tend to pull behind large vehicles before passing them.,b:Because following closely will get you caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,c:To better see around the sides of the vehicle and avoid its blind spots.
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses block your view of the road ahead and have large blind spots directly behind and along their sides. By increasing your following distance, you improve your ability to see around them and reduce the chance of staying in their blind spots, giving you more time to react to traffic or hazards.

question: Why should you avoid sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses?
options: a:Because they require much longer distances to stop due to their size and weight.,b:Because small vehicle drivers cannot see trucks in their mirrors.,c:Because large trucks always travel at higher speeds.
note: Large trucks and buses are much heavier than passenger cars and need more time and distance to stop. If you cut in front of them and brake suddenly, the driver may not be able to stop in time, greatly increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: When you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or hear a siren, what must you do?
options: a:Keep driving in your lane without stopping.,b:Pull to the right curb or edge of the road and stop.,c:Slow down and keep moving in your lane.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights and/or siren, you must yield the right‑of‑way by pulling as far to the right as safely possible and stopping. Stay stopped until the vehicle has passed and it is safe to reenter traffic. This gives emergency responders a clear, predictable path and reduces the risk of collisions.

question: When you hear a fire engine siren behind you, you must:
options: a:Pull over to the side of the road and stop.,b:Slow down and continue driving in lane.,c:Turn on your hazard lights and keep going.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: If a fire engine or other emergency vehicle is coming from behind with lights and siren on, you must pull over to the right side of the road and stop, when safe. Do not speed up, stop in the middle of your lane, or continue driving slowly in the lane. Stopping at the side of the road makes your actions predictable and gives the emergency vehicle room to pass quickly and safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a divided multilane highway, if you see or hear an approaching emergency vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Never change lanes for an emergency vehicle on a divided highway.,b:Stop immediately in your lane, even if traffic is behind you.,c:Safely move to the right and slow down or stop if needed to give the emergency vehicle a clear path.
note: Move over or slow down to give emergency vehicles a clear path; do not attempt to outdrive them.

question: What is defensive driving?
options: a:Following the vehicle ahead closely to block others.,b:Identifying dangerous situations and taking action to avoid crashes.,c:Advancing ahead of slow drivers to protect yourself.
note: Defensive driving means constantly scanning the road, anticipating what other drivers, pedestrians, and cyclists might do, and adjusting your speed or position early to avoid trouble. Instead of reacting at the last second, you leave space, avoid aggressive maneuvers, and plan escape routes so you can prevent collisions before they happen.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Exiting the freeway onto a downhill, curving ramp, what should you do?
options: a:Maintain freeway speed while on the ramp.,b:Begin braking once you are in the curve.,c:Slow to a safe speed before entering the curve.
note: When exiting a freeway onto a downhill, curving ramp, you should slow to a safe speed before you enter the curve. Braking hard while already in the curve, especially on a downhill, can cause skidding or loss of control. Use the advisory speed signs for the ramp as a guide and enter the curve at or below that speed.

question: What color are signs that indicate areas of public recreation or cultural interest?
options: a:Red.,b:Green.,c:Brown.
note: Brown traffic signs are used for guidance to recreational and cultural areas. They point to parks, campgrounds, historic sites, and similar destinations so drivers can easily find public recreation and cultural points of interest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?
options: a:Only when you see a police car.,b:Whenever anything makes driving conditions less than perfect.,c:Only when entering a highway with other cars.
note: The posted speed limit is the maximum speed allowed in ideal conditions, not a target speed. You must slow down below the limit whenever weather, visibility, traffic, road surface, or hazards make the posted speed unsafe so you can stop and react in time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When you see a 'Merging traffic' sign on the freeway, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Make room for entering vehicles by changing lanes or adjusting speed when safe.,b:Always remain at your current speed.,c:Honk at incoming traffic to warn them away.
note: A merging traffic sign warns that vehicles will be entering your lane. You should help them merge safely by creating space: if possible, change lanes away from the merge area or adjust your speed to allow a safe gap, while keeping control and obeying other traffic laws.

question: What does BAC stand for?
options: a:Blood alcohol capacity.,b:Blood alcohol concentration.,c:Basic alcohol content.,d:Body alcohol count.
note: BAC stands for Blood Alcohol Concentration. It is the amount of alcohol in your bloodstream, usually measured as a percentage, and is used to determine legal impairment for driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you yield to emergency vehicles?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:Only when other vehicles yield first.,c:When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
note: You must always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using a siren and/or flashing red or blue lights. Safely pull over to the right edge of the road and stop, or otherwise clear a path, so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: As alcohol accumulates in your blood, it:
options: a:Reduces risk-taking behavior.,b:Improves eyesight.,c:Slows your reactions and increases confidence,d:Speeds up your reactions.
note: Alcohol slows your brain and body, so your reaction time gets longer and your coordination worsens. At the same time, it lowers inhibitions and judgment, so you may feel more confident and take more risks even though your driving ability is reduced.

question: What does a single broken white centerline allow you to do?
options: a:You must stay within your lane.,b:You may cross the centerline to change lanes.,c:You may change lanes only from the left lane.
note: A single broken white line separates lanes of traffic moving in the same direction. You may cross it to change lanes or pass when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking mirrors and blind spots and signaling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which factors affect braking distance?
options: a:The speed your vehicle is traveling.,b:The condition of your brakes and tires.,c:The condition of the pavement.,d:All of the above
note: Braking distance increases as your speed increases and is also affected by how well your brakes and tires work and how good or bad the road surface is. Wet, icy, or gravel roads, worn tires, or poor brakes all make it take longer to stop, so all of these factors matter.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your freeway exit, what should you do?
options: a:Continue to the next exit and leave there.,b:Make a U-turn through the median.,c:Back up or stop on the highway to return to the exit.
note: If you miss your exit on a freeway, stay calm and continue to the next exit, then re-route from there. Never stop, back up, or make a U-turn on the freeway or in the median, because those maneuvers are illegal and extremely dangerous at high speeds.

question: Why does driving at night require increased caution?
options: a:Because drivers cannot see as well at night.,b:Because traffic volume is higher at night.,c:Because roadways are always more slippery at night.
note: At night, your headlights only let you see a limited distance ahead, and it is harder to see pedestrians, animals, and unlit objects. Because visibility is reduced, you need to slow down, increase following distance, and use your lights properly to give yourself more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To enter a gap in highway traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Check traffic to the side and behind you, and make sure the gap is large enough before merging.,b:Speed up and let the other vehicles make way.,c:Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
note: When entering a gap in highway traffic, you must check traffic to the side and behind you, and also judge the speed and distance of vehicles in front of and behind the gap. Focusing only on the vehicles behind the gap is unsafe; you need a full picture of surrounding traffic to merge smoothly and avoid cutting off vehicles already on the highway.

question: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to which road users?
options: a:Only pedestrians.,b:Only bicyclists.,c:Pedestrians, bicyclists, and vehicles already in the roundabout.
note: Before entering a roundabout, you must yield to all road users already in the roundabout and to pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks at the entry and exit. This includes vehicles circulating in the roundabout, as well as pedestrians and bicyclists who are crossing or about to cross.

question: The blind spot behind a large truck can extend about how far behind the truck's cab?
options: a:100 feet.,b:200 feet.,c:80 feet.
note: Large trucks have very large blind spots, especially directly behind them. The area directly behind a truck can extend up to about 200 feet where the truck driver may not see you. Staying out of this zone gives you a better view of the road ahead and makes it more likely the truck driver can see your vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when should you move back into the right (driving) lane?
options: a:After signaling for three seconds.,b:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your inside rearview mirror.,c:When you are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: After passing, you should not move back into the right lane until you can see both headlights of the vehicle you passed in your inside rearview mirror. This indicates you have enough space ahead of that vehicle to return safely without cutting them off or forcing them to brake suddenly.

question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?
options: a:He or she is a police officer.,b:He or she is deaf.,c:He or she is blind.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is blind or visually impaired. You must use extra caution, slow down, and be prepared to stop. Always yield the right-of-way to blind pedestrians at crossings and never honk or rev your engine to hurry them; allow them to cross safely at their own pace.

question: Which of these correctly describes the slow-moving vehicle emblem?
options: a:A rectangular red sign.,b:A circular green sign.,c:A reflective orange triangle.
note: The slow-moving vehicle emblem is a reflective orange triangle with a red border. It is mounted on vehicles that typically travel 25 mph or less, warning faster traffic to use extra caution and be prepared to slow down.

question: What is commonly used on some highways to direct drivers into proper turning lanes?
options: a:Flashing red lights.,b:White lines on the side of the road only.,c:Arrows painted on the roadway or signs showing lane use.
note: Arrows painted on the roadway and lane-use control signs show which lanes are for turning or going straight. Drivers must follow these arrows to be in the correct lane before reaching the intersection.

question: Which behavior blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,b:Using public transportation instead of driving.,c:Slowing down to look at a collision or unusual event (rubbernecking).
note: Rubbernecking—slowing down just to look at a crash or something unusual—disrupts traffic flow and can cause additional collisions. Keep your attention on the road ahead and maintain a safe, steady speed.

question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light require you to do?
options: a:Stop and then proceed when the signal changes to green or a green arrow.,b:Stop and then proceed when it is clear.,c:Proceed slowly through the intersection.
note: A red arrow means you must stop and remain stopped in the direction of the arrow until a green light or green arrow appears, unless a specific sign allows a turn on red and it is safe and legal to do so.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Challenge them.,b:Speed up to match their behavior.,c:Get out of their way and avoid confrontation.
note: When you encounter an aggressive driver, do not engage or compete. Safely create space, let them pass, and avoid eye contact or gestures. If necessary, contact authorities rather than confronting the driver.

question: If you're involved in a serious motor vehicle crash, what is your first action?
options: a:Call the police.,b:Determine whether anyone is injured.,c:Stop your vehicle.
note: Stop your vehicle if possible and move it off the roadway. If anyone is injured call 911 and provide assistance. You must report crashes to law enforcement when there is an injury, death, or more than $1,000 in property damage (or over $200 in damage to government property).

question: When preparing to enter a freeway, how should you check traffic on the freeway?
options: a:Use only your rearview mirror.,b:Use only your side mirrors.,c:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder in addition to mirrors.
note: Use mirrors and a shoulder check to confirm lane position and blind spots before merging onto freeway traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before making a left turn, the driver should:
options: a:Sound your horn.,b:Swing to the right side of your lane.,c:Yield to oncoming vehicles.
note: Yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic when making a left turn; only turn when it is safe to do so.

question: Drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving:
options: a:Do not have sufficient control over their bodies or vehicles.,b:Are always aware of the risks they are taking.,c:Become better drivers because they are more careful.
note: Alcohol impairs judgement, vision, concentration, and reaction time; drivers under the influence cannot control their vehicles as well.

question: Regarding small children riding in vehicles, which statement is correct?
options: a:Children are safe if standing in the back of a vehicle.,b:Children must be secured in appropriate child seats or restraints; holding them by an adult is not safe.,c:Small size prevents children from being hurt in a crash.
note: Children who are too small for regular safety belts must use approved child seats. No adult can safely hold a child during a crash or sudden stop.

question: If visibility is very poor due to fog, you should slow down and:
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers.,b:Switch your headlights to the low beam setting.,c:Use your high beam headlights to improve vision.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, always use low-beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture in the air and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams and fog lights (if equipped) help you see the road and help others see you without creating glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should drivers treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Treat it the same as a stop sign: stop, then proceed when safe.,b:Drive through if there is no crossing traffic.,c:Continue driving because you have the right-of-way.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and proceed only when it is safe. Do not drive through without stopping, even if you think no one is coming.

question: Why should you not use high-beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:It improves visibility too much and blinds other drivers.,b:Vehicles behind you will not see you.,c:The light will reflect back into your eyes.
note: High-beam headlights in fog or mist cause the light to reflect off the tiny water droplets and back into your eyes, creating glare and reducing how far you can see. Use low beams so the light aims down at the road and improves visibility without as much reflection.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate about passing?
options: a:Not permitted from either direction.,b:Permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side with the broken line. Drivers on the side with the solid yellow line must not cross it to pass. This marking controls where it is safe and legal to enter the opposing lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a green arrow changes to a steady green light, what must you do when turning?
options: a:You retain the exclusive right-of-way to turn.,b:You may no longer turn and must go straight.,c:You may turn but must yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected turn, meaning oncoming traffic is stopped. When the arrow goes away and you have a steady green light, you may still turn, but it becomes an unprotected turn. You must yield to oncoming vehicles and pedestrians in the crosswalk before turning.

question: In fog, rain, or snow, which headlights setting should you use?
options: a:High beams.,b:Fog lights only.,c:Low beams.
note: In fog, rain, or snow, you should use low beam headlights. High beams can reflect off moisture in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams provide better visibility and reduce glare for you and other drivers.

question: If it begins to sleet or snow while you're driving, what should you do?
options: a:Allow extra following distance between you and the vehicle ahead.,b:Approach other vehicles with the same caution as in clear weather.,c:Keep your windshield and mirrors cleared only when stopped.
note: When it starts to sleet or snow, the road becomes slippery and stopping distances increase. You should slow down and allow extra following distance so you have more time and space to react. Keep your windshield and mirrors clear at all times so you can see hazards early.

question: Which method checks the blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Using your side mirror.,b:Using the inside rearview mirror.,c:Turning your head and looking over your shoulder.
note: Before changing lanes, you must check areas your mirrors cannot see, called blind spots. To do this, briefly turn your head and look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move. Mirrors alone are not enough to detect vehicles in your blind spots.

question: If there are oncoming cars to your left and parked vehicles to your right, how should you steer?
options: a:Steer closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.,b:Steer closer to the oncoming vehicles than to the parked vehicles.,c:Keep a middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.
note: When you have oncoming traffic on one side and parked cars on the other, steer a middle course between them. This gives you the greatest possible space cushion from both hazards and reduces the risk of sideswiping a parked car or colliding with oncoming traffic.

question: When the center of the road has a solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, you may:
options: a:Pass if traffic is clear.,b:Only in an emergency.,c:If you are on an expressway.
note: A solid yellow line means no passing from that side, while a broken yellow line means passing is allowed from that side when it is safe. If the broken yellow line is next to your lane, you may cross it to pass another vehicle, but only when you have enough clear distance ahead and no oncoming traffic.

question: What does a flashing yellow light at an intersection indicate?
options: a:Stop and wait for a green light.,b:Caution—slow down and proceed with care.,c:Continue normally without slowing.
note: A flashing yellow light means proceed with caution. You do not have to stop, but you must slow down, look carefully for cross traffic and pedestrians, and be prepared to yield if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you must slow or stop where others may not expect it, how should you warn drivers behind you?
options: a:Sound your horn continuously.,b:Tap your brake pedal quickly several times.,c:Wave your left arm out the window.
note: When you need to slow or stop in a place others might not expect, tap your brake pedal several times. This flashes your brake lights and gives drivers behind you extra warning so they can slow safely.

question: After a minor, no-injury intersection collision with little damage, what should you do if possible?
options: a:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane to a safe location.,b:Never move your vehicle for any reason.,c:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until law enforcement arrives.
note: After a minor crash with no injuries, if the vehicles are drivable and it is safe, you should move them out of the traffic lane. Moving to the shoulder or a safe nearby location helps prevent additional collisions and keeps traffic flowing. Turn on hazard lights and exchange information once you are safely out of the way.

question: How can you help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away?
options: a:Drive 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,b:Suddenly slow to create space.,c:Maintain a steady speed and signal intentions in advance.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early for turns or lane changes helps the driver behind you judge distance and adjust smoothly. This reduces sudden braking and tailgating, making it easier for them to maintain a safe following distance.

question: Seat belts are most effective when worn by whom?
options: a:Passengers only on long trips.,b:The driver only.,c:All occupants in the vehicle.
note: Seat belts protect everyone in the vehicle. All occupants should buckle up, because unbelted passengers can be thrown around in a crash and injure themselves or others, even at lower speeds.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When do you have the right-of-way to turn left?
options: a:Always when turning from the left lane.,b:When a green arrow is pointing left.,c:When the light is a steady green circle.,d:When a flashing yellow arrow is displayed.
note: A steady green left arrow gives you a protected left turn. Oncoming traffic has a red light and must stop, so you have the right-of-way to turn left after checking that the intersection is clear.

question: If you must slow down on a slippery road, what should you do first?
options: a:Firmly apply your brakes.,b:Apply the parking brake.,c:Take your foot off the gas pedal.
note: On a slippery road, ease off the accelerator first so your vehicle slows gradually. If you need to slow more, brake gently and steadily to avoid skidding; sudden or hard braking can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left, to whom must drivers yield the right-of-way?
options: a:Other drivers who are already in the intersection.,b:Oncoming traffic (and any pedestrians in the intersection).,c:Pedestrians only.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight or turning right, and to pedestrians and bicyclists in the crosswalk or intersection. Turn only when the way is clear and it is safe.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the solid line.,b:Passing is permitted from either lane.,c:Passing is allowed from the lane next to the broken line.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line, and is prohibited from the side with the solid line. Always pass only when it is safe and legal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving an alley, driveway, or parking lot and crossing a sidewalk, what must you do?
options: a:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk or sidewalk area.,b:Expect pedestrians on the sidewalk to yield the right-of-way.,c:Stop only if pedestrians are on the sidewalk.
note: When exiting an alley, driveway, or parking lot across a sidewalk, you must stop before crossing the sidewalk area and yield to all pedestrians. Only after the sidewalk is clear may you continue toward the road.

question: At dusk or on overcast days, what should you do about your vehicle lights?
options: a:Use your four-way flashers while driving.,b:Use only your parking lights.,c:Turn on your headlights.
note: At dusk or on overcast days, you should turn on your headlights so other drivers can see you more easily. High beams must be dimmed to low beams when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle or when following another vehicle closely, to avoid blinding other drivers.

question: If you notice a vehicle defect affecting safe operation, you should:
options: a:Only fix the problem when you can afford it.,b:Drive more slowly and ignore it.,c:Have the defect corrected as soon as possible before driving.
note: If your vehicle has a defect that affects safe operation—such as bad brakes, worn tires, or broken lights—you should have it repaired before driving. Operating a vehicle with known safety defects increases your risk of a crash and can be illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking next to a curb, when should you use your turn signal?
options: a:Never during curb maneuvers.,b:Only when pulling away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:When pulling next to or away from the curb.
note: You must signal any time you change your vehicle’s position on the road, including when pulling toward a curb to park and when leaving the curb to reenter traffic. Signaling lets other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians anticipate your movement and adjust safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of these is a correct passing practice?
options: a:Return to your lane immediately after passing without checking.,b:Use mirrors and look over your left shoulder to check the blind spot when passing to the left.,c:Only signal at least 100 feet before changing lanes.
note: Before passing to the left, signal, check your mirrors, and look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot. Only move back into your lane when you can see the front of the vehicle you passed in your rearview mirror, ensuring you have enough space.

question: When roads are snowy or icy, you should:
options: a:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than you would otherwise.,b:Drive as you would under normal conditions.,c:Use your cruise control.
note: On snowy or icy roads, reduce speed and make all speed and steering changes gradually to maintain traction. Sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering can cause skids. Never use cruise control on slippery surfaces because it can cause the wheels to spin and you may lose control.

question: When driving on the highway, consistently looking far ahead helps you:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Spot police officers to avoid a ticket.,c:Keep up with the speed of traffic.
note: Looking far ahead on the highway lets you see slowing traffic, lane closures, or hazards early so you can brake or change lanes smoothly instead of making sudden, last‑second moves. This reduces hard braking, sudden swerves, and rear‑end collisions.

question: Lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions are divided by what color lines?
options: a:Red.,b:Black.,c:Yellow.
note: Yellow center lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction, and edge lines are also white on the right side of the road in most situations.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass another vehicle, when should you signal?
options: a:Signal early enough for other drivers to know your intentions.,b:Signal only if there is visible traffic behind you.,c:Signal just after you begin changing lanes.
note: You must signal well in advance before changing lanes or passing so other drivers have time to see your signal and adjust. Signaling only when you start moving or only if you see traffic behind you does not give others enough warning.

question: As daylight fades, which lights should you use to help others see your vehicle?
options: a:Emergency flashers.,b:Low beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: As it gets darker, you should turn on your low beam headlights so others can see you and you can see the road. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for driving, and emergency flashers are only for breakdowns or emergencies, not normal driving.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How does vehicle speed affect stopping distance and crash severity?
options: a:Stopping distance and crash severity decrease as speed increases.,b:Stopping distance and crash severity increase as speed increases.,c:Speed has no effect on stopping distance or crash severity.
note: The faster you drive, the longer it takes to stop and the harder you will hit in a crash. Stopping distance increases with speed, and crash force rises sharply as speed goes up, which greatly increases the chance of serious injury or death.

question: At a school crossing sign, how should you proceed?
options: a:Always stop.,b:Always sound your horn when you see children.,c:Watch for children and be ready to stop.
note: A school crossing sign is a warning sign. It tells you to slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You are not required to stop every time you see the sign, but you must always yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and drive with extra caution in school areas.

question: If your car stalls or breaks down on the highway, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn at passing motorists.,b:Use your four-way flashers and move off the road as far as possible.,c:Sit in your car and wait for help without signaling.
note: If your vehicle stalls or breaks down on a highway, signal and carefully move as far off the roadway as possible, preferably onto the shoulder. Turn on your four-way (hazard) flashers so other drivers can see that your vehicle is disabled. This reduces the risk of a collision and alerts others to use extra caution when passing.

question: On slippery roads, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive as you would on dry roads.,c:Use alternate routes.
note: On slippery roads, your tires have less traction, so it takes longer to stop and it is easier to skid. You should slow down and increase your following distance so you have more space and time to react. Avoid sudden braking or sharp steering. Choosing another route may sometimes help, but the key safety action is to increase your following distance.

question: If you're angry after an argument, what is the safest action before driving?
options: a:Drive on the interstate to 'let off steam.',b:Loudly play the radio to distract yourself.,c:Take a few minutes to calm down before driving.
