note: Strong emotions like anger, fear, or sadness can distract you, slow your reactions, and lead to risky decisions. If you are upset after an argument, the safest choice is to wait and give yourself time to calm down before driving so you can focus fully on the road and other users.

question: When approaching an accident scene, what is the appropriate action?
options: a:Keep your attention on your driving.,b:Stop if you are involved or if emergency help has not yet arrived.,c:Keep moving.
note: When approaching an accident scene, keep your attention on your driving and do not slow or stop just to look. You should only stop if you are directly involved in the crash or if emergency help has not yet arrived and you can safely offer assistance. Unnecessary stopping or slowing can cause additional crashes and traffic backups.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:An area only used by road construction workers.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:The area designated for pedestrians to cross the roadway.
note: A crosswalk is the part of the roadway set aside for pedestrians to cross, whether it is painted on the road or unmarked at an intersection. Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before passing another vehicle?
options: a:Check your mirrors and blind spots.,b:Re-enter your lane within 10 feet of the passed vehicle.,c:Honk your horn at least three times.
note: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots, signal, and be sure you have enough space and time to pass safely. Return to your lane only when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:Motorcyclists do not follow the same rules as cars.,b:Motorcycles can stop more quickly than cars,c:Motorcycles brake more slowly than cars.
note: Motorcycles are lighter and can stop very quickly. If you follow too closely, you may not have enough time or space to react if the motorcyclist brakes suddenly, increasing the risk of a rear-end collision.

question: After stopping for a passing train, what should you do before proceeding?
options: a:Look for a second train and wait until signals and gates are clear.,b:Proceed as soon as the first train passes.,c:Wait only for the gates to begin to lift before you go.
note: After a train passes, always look and listen for another train on any other track, and do not proceed until the gates are fully raised and all warning lights and bells have stopped.

question: What helps someone sober up after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Nothing but time will remove alcohol's effects.,b:Drinking tomato juice and lime.,c:Drinking hot coffee.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise do not speed up sobriety and cannot make you safe to drive.

question: Which statement best describes backing your vehicle?
options: a:Dangerous if you have a helper.,b:Always dangerous.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing is always risky because your view is limited and it is harder to judge space and see pedestrians or small objects. Even with a helper, you must move slowly, check mirrors and over your shoulder, and be ready to stop immediately.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you're waiting to turn left at a multilane intersection and oncoming traffic blocks your view, what is the safe action?
options: a:Accelerate rapidly when the first lane you need to cross is clear.,b:Wait for an oncoming driver to wave you across the intersection.,c:Wait until you can see all the lanes you need to cross before making the turn.
note: When turning left across multiple lanes, you must not start your turn until you can clearly see that every lane you must cross is free of oncoming traffic. Never rely on another driver waving you through, and never accelerate blindly into lanes you cannot see.

question: Why is driving at night more hazardous than daytime driving?
options: a:Headlights make objects appear closer.,b:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.,d:Roads are always more slippery at night.
note: Night driving is more hazardous mainly because you cannot see as far ahead. Headlights limit your view and glare from other vehicles can further reduce visibility, so you must drive more slowly and carefully to give yourself enough time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A posted speed limit indicates:
options: a:The maximum safe speed under all conditions.,b:The suggested speed under ideal conditions.,c:The maximum or minimum legal speed under ideal conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum (or sometimes minimum) legal speed allowed on that road under ideal conditions. You are required to slow down below the posted limit whenever weather, traffic, or road conditions make the posted speed unsafe.

question: When you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what must you do?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead and reduce speed.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Increase speed to pass the work zone quickly.
note: Orange signs and cones mean you are entering a work zone. You must slow down, watch for workers, equipment, and sudden lane shifts, and be prepared to stop or change lanes only when it is safe and directed.

question: When passing a large vehicle, what should drivers of small vehicles be prepared for?
options: a:Loud noises.,b:Wind gusts that can affect vehicle direction.,c:Excess air pollution.
note: Large trucks and buses push a lot of air around them, especially at higher speeds. As you pass, this air turbulence can cause sudden wind gusts that tug your vehicle sideways. Hold the wheel firmly and be ready to make small steering corrections so you stay in your lane and maintain a safe path.

question: If you are already inside an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your speed to get out quickly.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection.,c:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.
note: A yellow light warns that the signal is about to turn red. If you are already in the intersection when it turns yellow, you should keep moving and clear the intersection safely rather than stopping in the middle. Stopping suddenly in the intersection can confuse or endanger other drivers behind you.

question: If you must make an emergency stop, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on emergency flashers and stay in your vehicle if it is safe to do so.,b:Get out immediately and walk to seek help.,c:Blow your horn at passing cars to alert them.
note: If you must make an emergency stop, first move as far off the roadway as you safely can. Turn on your hazard flashers so other drivers see you. In most situations it is safer to stay inside your vehicle with your seat belt on, away from moving traffic, unless there is an immediate danger such as fire or being struck.

question: If the centerline has one solid yellow and one broken yellow line and the broken line is next to your lane, what does this mean?
options: a:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are allowed to pass from your lane if it is safe.
note: A centerline with one solid yellow and one broken yellow line means passing is allowed only from the side with the broken line. If the broken line is next to your lane, you may pass when it is legal and safe, with enough clear distance ahead and without interfering with oncoming traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection, what is the proper action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and proceed.,b:Yield to vehicles approaching from your right and be prepared to stop.,c:Always come to a full stop before proceeding.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection, no signs or signals assign right-of-way, so drivers must use right-of-way rules and caution. You must yield to vehicles already in the intersection and to vehicles approaching from your right. Slow down, be prepared to stop, and proceed only when you are sure it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the correct action at a yield sign before entering another roadway?
options: a:Only yield to traffic on your right.,b:Always come to a complete stop before entering the intersection.,c:Slow down and yield to traffic in the road you are entering.
note: A yield sign means you must slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary, giving the right‑of‑way to traffic and pedestrians already in the roadway you are entering. You do not always have to stop, but you must not enter if it would force others to slow or stop suddenly.

question: What is the only thing that can reduce blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only time lowers your blood alcohol concentration. Your body must metabolize the alcohol, and this process cannot be sped up by coffee, food, cold showers, or exercise. You may feel more awake, but your BAC and level of impairment remain the same until enough time passes.

question: At night, which road user is hardest to see?
options: a:Road signs.,b:Other motorists.,c:Pedestrians.
note: Pedestrians are usually the hardest to see at night because they are smaller, often unlit, and may wear dark clothing. Signs are reflective and vehicles have lights, so you should slow down and scan carefully for people walking along or crossing the road.

question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Brake hard.,b:Maintain a constant speed and allow the pass.,c:Speed up to block the pass.
note: When another vehicle is passing you, maintain a steady speed and stay in your lane so the driver can judge the pass safely. Do not speed up or brake suddenly; if needed, you may slightly reduce speed to make the pass safer and easier.

question: On a two-lane road without bicycle lanes, what is the safest way to pass a bicyclist traveling in your direction?
options: a:Slow down and wait until there is no traffic approaching,b:Do not pass until you come to a traffic signal or stop sign.,c:Continue driving straight; the bicyclist should get out of your way.
note: On a two‑lane road without a bike lane, slow down and wait until there is no oncoming traffic and you can give the bicyclist plenty of space—at least 3 feet, and more at higher speeds. Treat the bicycle like a slow‑moving vehicle and only pass when it is clearly safe.

question: What is the safest way to pass a bicyclist?
options: a:Drive partially into the bicycle lane until you can pass.,b:Honk to alert the bicyclist you are about to pass.,c:Slow down and give the bicyclist as much space as possible.
note: When passing a bicyclist, slow down and leave as much space as possible—ideally at least 3–4 feet where required by law. Do not honk or crowd the bicycle lane; wait until it is safe, then pass with plenty of room.

question: Who must you give the right-of-way to?
options: a:No one crossing the street.,b:Any pedestrian crossing in a marked crosswalk or in any crosswalk at an intersection.,c:Only pedestrians at marked crosswalks.
note: You must yield to pedestrians in marked crosswalks and in unmarked crosswalks at intersections. Even where not legally required, you should be prepared to yield to anyone crossing the street to prevent a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from on-ramps on your right while on an interstate, what is the best action when safe?
options: a:Move to the left lane.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Maintain your lane and speed.
note: On interstates, the right lane is where traffic enters from on-ramps. When it is safe, moving to the left lane makes it easier for merging vehicles to enter and helps prevent sudden braking or lane changes.

question: If a tire blows out while driving, what steering and speed control technique should you use?
options: a:Maintain your current speed and steer straight.,b:Try to steer straight while gradually slowing by removing your foot from the gas pedal.,c:Brake hard immediately.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the steering wheel firmly and try to keep the vehicle going straight. Do not brake hard; instead, ease your foot off the gas so you slow down gradually. Once the vehicle is under control and your speed has dropped, steer to a safe place off the road and brake gently to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, what must you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,b:Stop and remain stopped until the light turns green.,c:Come to a complete stop, then proceed when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, then yield to any traffic or pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, and proceed only when it is safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your freeway lane, what should you do?
options: a:Brake suddenly to discourage merging.,b:Maintain your exact position at all costs.,c:Make room for merging vehicles when safe.,d:Assert your right-of-way by speeding up.
note: On freeways, you should cooperate with merging traffic. When it is safe, adjust your speed or change lanes to create a gap so vehicles entering from an on‑ramp can merge smoothly. This reduces sudden braking and helps prevent collisions.

question: When you approach a stopped school bus with lights flashing and arm extended, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed carefully.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if you don't see children.,c:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is withdrawn and the bus moves.
note: When a school bus has flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the arm is withdrawn, and the bus moves again, unless your state has a specific divided‑highway exception. This protects children who may be crossing the road.

question: At a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Keep your speed constant.,b:Sound your horn to alert children.,c:Always come to a complete stop whether posted or not.,d:Watch for children and be prepared to stop.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing or walking near the roadway. You should slow down, watch carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You only must stop when required by a sign, signal, or the presence of pedestrians.

question: Why is extra space in front of a large truck needed?
options: a:Other drivers when they want to slow down.,b:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,c:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
note: Large trucks are heavy and need much more distance to stop than passenger cars. Leaving extra space in front of a truck gives the truck driver the room needed to slow or stop safely and helps prevent rear‑end collisions if traffic suddenly changes.

question: When sharing the roadway with a truck, what is important to remember?
options: a:Trucks have a smaller turning radius than cars.,b:Trucks need less time to pass on downgrades.,c:Trucks require longer distances to stop than smaller vehicles.
note: Because trucks are much heavier than cars, they take longer to stop. When driving near trucks, avoid cutting in front of them and always leave extra space so the truck has enough distance to brake safely.

question: How is distracted driving best described?
options: a:Extremely risky behavior that endangers drivers, passengers, pedestrians, and bicyclists.,b:Very uncommon among drivers.,c:Not a serious concern.
note: Distracted driving is any activity that takes your attention away from driving, such as texting, eating, or adjusting controls. It greatly increases crash risk and endangers everyone on or near the road, so it is considered extremely risky behavior.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Speed up to pass before they move.,c:Swerve suddenly into the next lane.
note: When animals are near the roadway, slow down and be prepared to stop. Animals can move unpredictably into your path, and sudden swerving can cause you to lose control or collide with another vehicle. Controlled braking and caution are the safest responses.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a posted speed limit sign indicate?
options: a:Only a recommended driving speed.,b:The minimum speed you must travel.,c:The maximum legal driving speed under ideal road and weather conditions.
note: A posted speed limit is the maximum legal speed allowed on that road in ideal conditions, not a target or minimum speed. In rain, fog, heavy traffic, or other hazards, you must drive slower than the posted limit to be safe and legal.

question: A flashing red traffic signal at an intersection has the same requirement as what sign?
options: a:A slow sign.,b:A yield sign.,c:A stop sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, then proceed only when it is safe and after yielding to other traffic and pedestrians, just as you would at a stop sign.

question: What is the purpose of a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign?
options: a:To state traffic laws and regulations.,b:To direct you to towns and cities.,c:To warn about conditions on or near the road ahead.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to upcoming curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other conditions that may require you to slow down or adjust how you drive.

question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:It is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.,b:It lets other road users know your intentions.,c:It is always unsafe to turn off a signal before completing a turn.
note: You should keep your turn signal on throughout the entire turn so that drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians clearly understand where you are going. Signaling continuously helps others predict your path and adjust their speed or position, which reduces the risk of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When an emergency vehicle using lights and/or siren approaches, you must immediately:
options: a:Pull to the right and stop.,b:Pull to the right and slow down but remain moving.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and continue driving.
note: When an emergency vehicle with lights and/or siren approaches, you must yield the right-of-way by pulling as far to the right side of the road as safely possible and stopping. This creates a clear path so the emergency vehicle can pass quickly and safely.

question: If you leave your vehicle unattended you must:
options: a:Turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.,b:Only set the parking brake.,c:Leave the engine running for a short time.,d:Leave the door unlocked for emergency access.
note: When leaving your vehicle unattended, always stop the engine, remove keys, lock the ignition, and set the parking brake.

question: Parking downhill on a two-way street, how should you position the wheels?
options: a:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,b:Turn your wheels toward the curb (right).,c:Turn the wheels to the left away from the curb.
note: When parking facing downhill on a two-way street with a curb, turn your front wheels toward the curb (to the right). If the vehicle starts to roll, the front tire will rest against the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: If someone is injured in a crash, what should you do regarding moving them?
options: a:Move the injured immediately away from the scene.,b:Always leave the injured where they are without aid.,c:Drive them to a hospital yourself even if moving them might harm them.,d:Do not move the injured unless necessary; keep them warm and give first aid.
note: After a crash, moving an injured person can worsen neck, back, or internal injuries. Only move them if there is immediate danger, such as fire or risk of another collision. Otherwise, keep them warm, provide basic first aid if you are able, and wait for emergency medical help.

question: In poor weather conditions, what should drivers do regarding following distance?
options: a:Increase their following distance.,b:Decrease their following distance.,c:Increase their speed to reach their destination more quickly.
note: In rain, fog, snow, or any situation with reduced traction or visibility, you must increase your following distance. Extra space gives you more time to see hazards, react, and stop smoothly if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it acceptable to drive on the shoulder to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the shoulder is wide enough.,c:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.
note: You must not drive onto the shoulder to pass another vehicle. The shoulder is for emergencies and breakdowns, not for travel or passing. Passing on the shoulder is unsafe and illegal in almost all situations, even if the vehicle ahead is turning left.

question: When backing up, you should drive at no faster than:
options: a:A normal driving speed.,b:A slow jog.,c:A slow crawl.
note: When backing up, move at a very slow crawl—about the speed of a slow walk. Vehicles are harder to control in reverse and your view is limited, so backing slowly gives you time to check mirrors, look over your shoulder, and stop quickly if a person or object appears.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, you must slow down and:
options: a:Yield to any car already within the roundabout.,b:Both of the above.,c:Yield to any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.
note: As you approach and enter a roundabout, slow down and yield to all traffic already in the circle, as well as to any pedestrians and bicyclists in crosswalks. You may enter only when there is a safe gap in circulating traffic and it is clear of people crossing.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are driving so slowly that traffic is backing up behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, what should you do?
options: a:Pull off the right side of the road and let traffic pass.,b:Decrease your speed further.,c:Not let other cars pass your vehicle.
note: If your slow driving is causing a line of vehicles to form behind you on a two-lane, two-way road, you should safely pull off to the right when possible and let them pass. This keeps traffic flowing smoothly and reduces the risk of unsafe passing attempts by impatient drivers.

question: When stopped by police for a violation or equipment check, what must the driver produce?
options: a:Only proof of registration.,b:Driver license,c:Only proof of insurance.
note: When an officer stops you for a traffic violation or equipment check, you are generally required to show your driver license, vehicle registration, and proof of insurance. The license proves you are legally allowed to drive, the registration shows the vehicle is properly registered, and insurance demonstrates financial responsibility.

question: What is the best way to avoid a dangerous driving situation?
options: a:Turn off the radio and focus only ahead.,b:Keep your eyes fixed straight ahead at all times.,c:Be aware of what is happening around your vehicle.
note: Being aware of what is happening all around your vehicle is the key to avoiding dangerous situations. Good defensive drivers constantly scan ahead, to the sides, and behind, so they can spot hazards early and adjust speed or position before a problem develops.

question: What is the most common cause of traffic crashes?
options: a:Bad weather.,b:New drivers.,c:Human error.
note: Most crashes are caused by human error, not by weather or vehicle problems. Mistakes like inattention, following too closely, speeding, or misjudging gaps and other road users lead to the majority of collisions.

question: What does a flashing red traffic light at an intersection mean?
options: a:The same as a stop sign.,b:The light is about to turn green.,c:The same as a yield sign.
note: A flashing red light means you must come to a complete stop, just as you would at a stop sign. After stopping, yield to any traffic and pedestrians in or approaching the intersection, then proceed only when it is safe.

question: Why are roads especially slippery when it first starts to rain?
options: a:Because oil and residue make the surface slick; avoid fast turns and stops.,b:Because tire traction improves temporarily.,c:Because it is safer to test tires' traction uphill.
note: When it first starts to rain, water mixes with oil, grease, and other residue on the road surface, making it especially slippery. Until this layer is washed away, you should slow down and avoid sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp turns.

question: On the freeway, why should you look farther ahead than on city streets?
options: a:To see potential hazards early and prepare for changes in traffic.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop completely.,c:Because it helps you keep up with traffic speed.
note: On freeways, vehicles travel faster and need more distance to stop or change lanes safely. By looking farther ahead than you would on city streets, you can spot slow traffic, crashes, or debris early and adjust your speed or lane smoothly instead of making sudden, unsafe maneuvers.

question: At what speed should you travel?
options: a:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you even if over the limit.,b:Always at the posted speed limit regardless of conditions.,c:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions and within posted limits.
note: You must always choose a speed that is safe for current conditions—such as rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor visibility—and never exceed the posted speed limit. Even if the limit is higher, you are required to slow down when conditions make the normal speed unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When two vehicles reach an intersection at the same time with no signs or signals, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle whose driver honks first.,b:The vehicle approaching from the right.,c:The vehicle approaching from the left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where two vehicles arrive at about the same time, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. This rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals to direct traffic.

question: What are "no zones" around large trucks?
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or limit the truck's ability to stop and maneuver.,b:Areas where cars have extra space to pass safely.,c:Places where a truck must always stop.,d:Designated parking zones for trucks.
note: No-zones are the large blind spots and close-in areas around trucks where the truck driver cannot see you well or cannot stop or maneuver quickly if you suddenly slow or change position. Staying out of these areas—especially directly behind, alongside the cab doors, and close in front—reduces the risk of a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Approaching a steady green traffic light, what should you do?
options: a:Proceed if the intersection is clear, yielding to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection.,b:Treat it like a four-way stop.,c:Stop if a police officer is nearby.
note: A steady green allows you to go if the intersection is clear; yield to pedestrians and any vehicles already in the intersection.

question: When must vehicles remain stopped behind a school bus with red lights flashing?
options: a:Until all students are off the bus.,b:Until the stop arm is retracted.,c:Until the stop arm is withdrawn and the bus starts moving again.
note: When a school bus has its red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing, the stop arm is withdrawn, and the bus begins moving again. This ensures children have fully cleared the roadway and are safe before traffic resumes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are stopped in a line at a stop sign and the intersection clears after the vehicles ahead go, what must you do?
options: a:Must stop again at the stop sign or stop line before proceeding.,b:May slowly roll past the stop sign.,c:May proceed through the intersection without stopping again.
note: At a stop sign, you must make a complete stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk, or before entering the intersection. If you were stopped in a line of cars and moved forward without actually stopping at the stop line or crosswalk, you must stop again at the proper stopping point before proceeding, even if the intersection has cleared.

question: How should you treat all railroad crossings?
options: a:Safe to cross most of the time.,b:A good place to stop and wait.,c:Dangerous; always look and listen for trains.,d:Only dangerous when signals are flashing.
note: Railroad crossings are always potentially dangerous because trains cannot stop quickly and always have the right-of-way. You should slow, look, and listen for trains, and be prepared to stop even if signals are not flashing. Never assume the tracks are clear just because you do not see a train immediately.

question: If another car is in danger of hitting you, what should you do immediately?
options: a:Wave your arms.,b:Sound your horn.,c:Use your emergency lights.
note: If another vehicle may hit you, use your horn to warn the other driver immediately. A quick, loud horn blast is the fastest way to get attention and can help prevent a collision. Emergency flashers are for stopped or disabled vehicles, and waving your arms is much less effective than sounding the horn.

question: What are construction zone signs normally shaped and colored?
options: a:Round or octagonal with black and yellow.,b:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.,c:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black.
note: Construction and work zone signs are usually orange with black symbols or lettering and are most often diamond-shaped, though some may be rectangular. The bright orange color alerts drivers to temporary conditions such as road work, lane shifts, or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: If an oncoming vehicle's headlights are blinding you, you should:
options: a:Use your high beams until they dim theirs.,b:Flash your lights at the other driver.,c:Stare straight ahead to avoid missing signs.,d:Look toward the right edge of the road and slow down.
note: When oncoming headlights blind you at night, shift your gaze slightly to the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide. This reduces glare and helps you maintain lane position. Slow down as needed so you have time to react to any hazards while your vision is affected.

question: If weather or light conditions require lights, which should you use in fog, snow, or heavy rain?
options: a:High beams.,b:Parking lights.,c:Low beam headlights.
note: In fog, snow, or heavy rain, always use low beam headlights. High beams reflect off moisture droplets in the air and shine back into your eyes, making it harder to see. Low beams provide better forward visibility and make your vehicle more visible to others without creating extra glare.

question: What do work zone signs indicate?
options: a:Less than ideal conditions are present for driving.,b:It is summer.,c:You must immediately stop and back up.
note: Work zone signs are orange and warn that road work or maintenance is taking place ahead. They indicate that driving conditions may be less than ideal due to lane shifts, workers near traffic, equipment, or uneven surfaces. When you see these signs, slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, and follow posted instructions.

question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Squeeze between the vehicle and the curb to complete your turn.,b:Wait until the truck or bus completes its turn before you turn.,c:Quickly turn before the larger vehicle.
note: Large vehicles like trucks and buses often need extra space to make right turns and may swing wide or start from a lane away from the curb. Never try to squeeze between them and the curb or rush ahead of them. Wait until they complete the turn, then make your turn when the path is clear.

question: If your car begins skidding out of control, what should you avoid?
options: a:Apply the brakes gently only if needed and steer to regain control.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly.,c:Brake hard and hold the pedal down.
note: When your car begins to skid, the key is to avoid actions that further upset the vehicle’s balance. Do not slam or rapidly pump the brakes in a skid; this can lock the wheels (in non‑ABS systems) or reduce your ability to steer. Instead, ease off the accelerator and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. If you must brake and your car has ABS, apply firm, steady pressure and let the system work.

question: Why is maintaining a space cushion around your vehicle important?
options: a:It keeps traffic flowing faster.,b:It prevents distractions from other vehicles.,c:It allows you time to react to unexpected situations.
note: Maintaining a space cushion gives you room and time to react if another driver stops suddenly, swerves, or makes a mistake. Extra space improves your view of the road and lets you brake or steer smoothly to avoid hazards.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, you should:
options: a:Sound your horn and maintain speed.,b:Speed up to clear the area quickly.,c:Drive in the shoulder to avoid them.,d:Slow down and pass with caution.
note: When pedestrians are near the roadway, you must slow down, be ready to stop, and pass them carefully. Reducing speed gives you more time to react if they step into your lane and helps ensure their safety.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow mean?
options: a:The protected left turn is ending and drivers must prepare to stop and then yield to oncoming traffic.,b:Drivers must accelerate to complete the turn.,c:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic only if turning right.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow means the protected left-turn phase is ending. You should clear the intersection if you are already in it and then be prepared to stop and yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians once the signal changes.

question: What happens when you take drugs together with alcohol?
options: a:The risk of causing a crash increases.,b:It is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.,c:It reduces alcohol's effect.,d:It prevents impairment.
note: Alcohol and many drugs both affect judgment, coordination, and reaction time. When taken together, their effects usually combine or multiply, making you much more impaired and greatly increasing your chances of causing a crash.

question: What do orange-colored road signs typically indicate?
options: a:Construction, maintenance, or emergency operations ahead.,b:A school zone is ahead.,c:A railroad crossing is ahead.
note: Orange road signs are used for temporary traffic control in work or incident areas. They warn of construction, maintenance, or emergency operations so you can slow down, be alert for workers and equipment, and follow any changed traffic patterns.

question: Which skill is affected first by alcohol?
options: a:Judgment.,b:Vision.,c:Balance.
note: Alcohol first affects the parts of the brain that control judgment and decision‑making. A driver’s ability to make safe choices, assess risk, and control impulses is usually impaired before vision, balance, or coordination noticeably decline. This is why even small amounts of alcohol can make your driving decisions unsafe, even if you still feel physically in control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to exceed the posted speed limit?
options: a:Never.,b:When passing another vehicle.,c:When there is no traffic in your lane.
note: You must never drive faster than the posted speed limit. The speed limit is the maximum legal speed under ideal conditions, and it does not become higher when you pass another vehicle or when the road seems empty. In many situations—such as bad weather, heavy traffic, or poor visibility—you are required to drive even slower than the posted limit.

question: What helps reduce road rage and aggressive driving?
options: a:Allowing extra travel time.,b:Driving faster than other traffic.,c:Refusing to use turn signals.,d:Tailgating slower vehicles.
note: Allowing extra travel time reduces stress and the urge to rush, which helps prevent aggressive driving and road rage. When you are not in a hurry, you are more patient with traffic, less likely to tailgate, speed, or make risky maneuvers, and better able to stay calm if other drivers make mistakes.

question: At night when an oncoming vehicle approaches, which headlight setting should you use?
options: a:Should be on their high beam setting.,b:Should be on their low beam setting.,c:Should be off. Use your parking lights.
note: When an oncoming vehicle approaches at night, you must use low‑beam headlights. High beams can blind or severely glare other drivers, making it harder for them to see the road. Dim your lights to low beam when you are within about 500 feet of an oncoming vehicle and when following another vehicle closely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a road with two lanes going the same direction, which lane should you use?
options: a:The left lane at all times.,b:The right lane except to pass.,c:The left lane to avoid vehicles entering from the right.
note: On a road with two lanes going in the same direction, you should usually drive in the right lane and use the left lane only for passing or preparing for a left turn. Staying in the right lane keeps traffic flowing smoothly and leaves the left lane available for vehicles that need to pass safely.

question: When backing up, what is the safest method?
options: a:Open your door to see if it is safe to proceed.,b:Rely only on your mirrors.,c:Turn and look through the rear window while backing.
note: When backing up, you should turn your head and look directly through the rear window while moving slowly. Do not open your door or rely only on mirrors or cameras, because they can miss hazards in your blind spots.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading them across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: A pedestrian using a white cane or a guide dog is visually impaired and has the right-of-way at all times. You must stop or yield whenever they are crossing or preparing to cross, and allow them to cross safely, regardless of whether anyone else is present.

question: When driving in fog, what lighting should you use?
options: a:It is okay to drive at the maximum speed limit.,b:Turn on your hazard lights.,c:Turn on your low beam headlights.
note: In fog, use low-beam headlights so the light aims down at the road. High beams reflect off the fog and make it harder to see. Slow down and use your hazards only if you are stopped or moving much more slowly than traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When considering a pass on a two-lane road, what should you judge first?
options: a:Sounding your horn as you pass.,b:Flashing your headlights as you pass.,c:The distance and speed of any oncoming vehicles.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, first judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles to be sure you have enough clear space to pass safely. Only begin passing when you are certain you can complete it without forcing oncoming traffic or the vehicle you are passing to brake or swerve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street with a curb, which way should you turn the wheels?
options: a:Turn your front wheels slightly to the right.,b:Turn your front wheels sharply away from the curb.,c:Turn your front wheels sharply toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels sharply away from the curb. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will rest against the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are usually what color?
options: a:Blue,b:Green,c:White
note: Regulatory signs tell you what you must or must not do, such as speed limits, no parking, or one-way signs. In the U.S., these are typically white with black (and sometimes red) lettering or symbols, and they are legally enforceable.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:On the left side of the centerline.,b:Near the centerline before making the turn.,c:Near the right-hand side of the road.
note: For a left turn from a two‑way street, you should be in the lane closest to the centerline, staying just to the right of the centerline. This position shortens the turn, improves visibility of oncoming traffic, and keeps you out of the path of vehicles going straight.

question: If a driver sees an animal on the roadway, what is the safest response?
options: a:Try to swerve sharply around the animal at high speed.,b:Slow down and proceed with caution to avoid startling the animal.,c:Speed up to pass the animal quickly.
note: When you see an animal on or near the road, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop. Sudden swerving at speed can cause you to lose control or hit another vehicle, and animals may move unpredictably or be followed by others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is an important step to perform when preparing to turn?
options: a:Close your windows.,b:Increase your speed to clear the intersection.,c:Check traffic in all directions.,d:Always move to the left lane.
note: Before turning, you must check traffic ahead, behind, and to the sides to be sure the turn is safe. Then signal, adjust your speed, and position your vehicle correctly so you do not cut off other road users or turn unexpectedly.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, whom must you yield to?
options: a:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:You have the automatic right-of-way.,c:No one, if you begin the turn quickly.
note: When turning left, you must yield to oncoming vehicles that are close enough to be a hazard and to pedestrians in the crosswalk. Only start your turn when there is a safe gap in oncoming traffic and the crosswalk is clear.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you and vehicles on your right and left arrive at an uncontrolled intersection at the same time, who do you yield to?
options: a:Wait until there are no vehicles before proceeding.,b:Yield to the vehicle on your right.,c:Yield to the vehicle on your left.
note: At an uncontrolled intersection where vehicles arrive at the same time, you must yield to the vehicle on your right. This right‑of‑way rule helps prevent confusion and collisions when there are no signs or signals. If you and cars on both sides arrive together, wait for the vehicle on your right to go first, then proceed when it is safe.

question: Which recommendation does NOT improve safe night driving?
options: a:Tinting windows to reduce interior glare extensively.,b:Carrying a flashlight in your vehicle.,c:Keeping your windshield clean.
note: Carrying a flashlight and keeping your windshield clean both support safer night driving. A clean windshield reduces glare and improves visibility, and a flashlight can help you see outside the vehicle if you must stop. However, heavily tinting windows can significantly reduce your ability to see at night and is often restricted by law, so extensive tinting does not improve safe night driving.

question: What color are regulatory traffic signs most commonly?
options: a:Green.,b:White.,c:Yellow.
note: Regulatory signs tell you about laws and rules you must obey, such as speed limits, parking restrictions, and lane use. These signs are most commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green lettering or symbols, making them easy to recognize as rules you are required to follow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you turn onto a two-lane road with a broken yellow line down the center, what does that tell you about the road?
options: a:It is a one-way road.,b:The road is under repair.,c:Traffic moves in both directions (a two-way road).
note: A broken yellow line in the center of the road separates traffic moving in opposite directions, which means it is a two‑way road. The broken pattern also indicates that passing is allowed when it is safe and legal to do so, after checking for oncoming traffic and ensuring you have enough space to pass.

question: When must you use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a lighted street.,b:On a freeway.,c:When driving in fog.
note: Low beam headlights should be used in fog because high beams reflect off water droplets in the air and create glare, making it harder to see. Low beams provide better forward visibility in fog, rain, snow, or mist. Use low beams whenever visibility is reduced and when approaching or following other vehicles at night.

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do first?
options: a:Turn off the ignition immediately.,b:Brake as hard as possible.,c:Ease off the gas and steer in the direction of the skid to regain control.
note: When a vehicle begins to skid, your first response should be to ease off the accelerator and look and steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go. Do not slam on the brakes or turn off the ignition, as those actions can cause you to lose even more control.

question: Which statement about work zones is true?
options: a:You should slow down for the Cone Zone and expect higher fines for violations.,b:Fines are always identical to normal traffic fines.,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present.
note: In work zones, you must slow down, obey all signs and flaggers, and be prepared for sudden changes in traffic. Many states impose higher fines for speeding and other violations in work zones to protect workers and drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is driving below the posted speed limit illegal?
options: a:When in heavy traffic in a construction zone.,b:When driving slowly disrupts the normal flow of traffic.,c:Only when driving in rural areas.
note: It is illegal to drive so slowly that you impede the normal and reasonable movement of traffic; you may be cited for driving too slowly.

question: What is the best action to take on slippery roads?
options: a:Drive at the posted speed limit but with caution.,b:Drive more quickly.,c:Slow down.
note: On slippery roads caused by rain, snow, or ice, you should reduce your speed below the posted limit and increase your following distance. Lower speeds give you more time to react and help prevent skids and loss of control.

question: If you take a non-prescription drug, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Drink alcohol to counteract drowsiness.,b:Drive as usual regardless of warnings.,c:Read the drug label for warnings about driving.
note: Many over-the-counter drugs can cause drowsiness, slowed reaction time, or other side effects that make driving unsafe. Always read the label for driving or machinery warnings, and ask a doctor or pharmacist if you are unsure whether it is safe to drive.

question: What do double solid yellow centerlines mean?
options: a:Railroad crossing ahead.,b:Pedestrian crossing ahead.,c:No passing from either direction; you may cross only for left turns and, where allowed, to carefully pass very slow users when safe.
note: Double solid yellow centerlines mean vehicles in both directions may not cross the lines to pass other vehicles. You may cross them only to make a left turn (such as into a driveway or side road) or, in some states, to carefully pass very slow-moving road users like bicycles or farm equipment when it is clearly safe and legal. You must never use a double solid yellow to pass regular traffic at normal speeds.

question: How should you prepare for hazards ahead on the road?
options: a:Stare straight ahead at all times.,b:Continuously scan the road and roadsides for potential problems.,c:Drive with your left foot on the brake.
note: Searching ahead, to the sides, and behind helps you detect and respond to hazards early.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How close is it illegal to park to a fire hydrant?
options: a:10 feet,b:15 feet,c:20 feet
note: It is illegal to park within 10 feet of a fire hydrant.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow's direction?
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:You wait until the light changes.,c:You first come to a complete stop.
note: A steady green arrow means you have a protected movement in that direction. If you are in the correct lane and the intersection and crosswalks are clear of traffic, pedestrians, and hazards, you may proceed in the direction of the arrow even if the other signals are red. You do not need to stop first unless a sign or signal specifically requires it.

question: How should you drive through a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected and use extra caution.,b:Slightly increase your speed to clear it quickly.,c:Expect workers to yield to motorists.,d:Drive normally as if nothing changed.
note: Construction zones present unusual hazards; slow down, watch for workers, and follow signs and flaggers.

question: What is the only effective way to remove alcohol from your body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait for time to pass.,c:Take a cold shower.
note: Only time allows your body to process and eliminate alcohol. Coffee, cold showers, exercise, or other tricks do not lower your blood alcohol concentration; they may make you feel more awake but you are still impaired until enough time has passed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, what assumption should you avoid?
options: a:Assuming the other driver will signal for you to pass.,b:Assuming the other driver will maintain a constant speed.,c:Assuming the other driver will slow down or move over to make space for you to return to your lane.
note: When you pass, you must not assume other drivers will help you by slowing down, signaling, or making room. You are responsible for judging that there is enough clear space to pass and return safely without relying on the actions of others.

question: On rainy, snowy, or foggy days you should use headlights primarily to:
options: a:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,b:So others can see your vehicle.,c:To keep your engine warm.
note: In rain, snow, or fog, you turn on your low‑beam headlights so that other drivers can see your vehicle more easily. Headlights improve your visibility to others and help prevent collisions when conditions reduce how far you can see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing a slower vehicle on a two-lane, two-way road, what must you do to complete the pass legally and safely?
options: a:Flash your headlights at oncoming traffic.,b:Use the road shoulder to pass.,c:Move into the lane used by oncoming traffic to pass when it is safe and legal.
note: On a two‑lane, two‑way road, you pass by briefly moving into the lane used by oncoming traffic, but only where passing is legal and you have enough clear distance. Never use the shoulder to pass, and flashing headlights at oncoming traffic is not how you complete a legal pass.

question: Signs that warn drivers about hazardous conditions are called:
options: a:Warning signs.,b:Regulatory signs.,c:Information signs.
note: Warning signs are used to alert drivers to conditions such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or other hazards ahead. Paying attention to these signs gives you time to slow down or adjust your driving before you reach the hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which has priority if you must choose between obedience: a steady red light, a police officer's directions, or a stop sign?
options: a:A stop sign.,b:Directions from a police officer.,c:A steady red light.
note: Directions from a police officer override traffic signals, signs, and pavement markings. If an officer directs you to proceed against a red light or stop sign, you must follow the officer’s instructions because they are managing traffic for safety in that moment.

question: When driving in work zones, what should you do?
options: a:Follow the driver in front of you closely.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.
note: In work zones you should increase your following distance and avoid tailgating so you have time to react to sudden stops, lane shifts, or workers and equipment entering the roadway. Keeping a safe space cushion greatly reduces the risk of rear-end collisions in these changing conditions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about speed is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on some highways can be dangerous.,b:Speeding is safe if you are an experienced driver.,c:Speeding is never dangerous.
note: Driving much slower than the flow of traffic can be dangerous because it can cause sudden braking, lane changes, and rear-end collisions. Safe driving means adjusting your speed to the legal limit and to traffic, weather, and road conditions—not going excessively fast or excessively slow.

question: A school bus stopped ahead of you in your lane has red lights flashing. What must you do?
options: a:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,b:Proceed if you believe no children are nearby.,c:Stop and remain stopped for as long as the red lights are flashing.
note: When a school bus in your lane has its red lights flashing, you must stop and remain stopped until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn. This ensures children have a protected space to get on or off the bus and cross the road safely.

question: A flashing yellow light at an intersection means you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop immediately.,b:Wait for a green light before proceeding.,c:Slow down and proceed with caution.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed with caution, watching carefully for cross traffic, pedestrians, or hazards. You do not need to stop unless it is necessary for safety or to yield the right-of-way.

question: What does a flashing red traffic signal mean?
options: a:You may slow but do not need to stop.,b:The signal is broken and can be ignored.,c:It means the same as a stop sign — come to a complete stop and proceed when safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated exactly like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, yield to anyone with the right‑of‑way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: At a railroad crossing with flashing signals, what must you do?
options: a:Stop no closer than 15 feet from the rail if signals warn of an approaching train.,b:Look for a train and then speed up if none is visible.,c:Slow down and look for a train.
note: When the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, you must stop at least 15 feet from the nearest rail and remain stopped until the train has passed and the warning devices stop operating. Never drive around lowered gates or try to beat a train.

question: What should you do before entering a curve?
options: a:Brake hard as you enter the curve.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Reduce your speed.
note: You should slow down before you enter a curve. Entering too fast can cause your vehicle to skid or drift into another lane. Adjust your speed for the sharpness of the curve and road conditions, and be prepared to maintain a safe speed through the curve.

question: On slick roads, how should you make turns?
options: a:Take turns more slowly than usual.,b:Change lanes quickly before the turn.,c:Accelerate through the turn.,d:Brake sharply while turning.
note: On slick or slippery roads, turns must be made more slowly than usual. Reduce speed before the turn and steer smoothly to avoid skidding; sudden braking, sharp steering, or rapid acceleration in the turn can cause loss of control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Should slow down but never stop.,b:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.,c:Must yield the right-of-way to cross traffic that is close enough to cause conflict.
note: At a yield sign you must slow down and be prepared to stop. You must let cross traffic and pedestrians go first if they are close enough to be a hazard. Proceed only when you can enter or cross without interfering with other road users.

question: Which of the following is true concerning railroad crossings?
options: a:Not all railroad crossings are equipped with flashing red signals and gates.,b:You must stop at every railroad crossing regardless of signals.,c:It is against the law to go around lowered gates at a crossing.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to drive around or under lowered railroad crossing gates. When warning devices are active or a flagger directs you to stop, you must stop and wait until the gates are fully raised and signals stop before proceeding. Remember that some crossings have no lights or gates, so you must always look and listen for trains.

question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory traffic laws and regulations.,b:Directions to cities and towns.,c:Warning of special conditions or hazards ahead.
note: Yellow and black diamond-shaped signs are warning signs. They alert you to special conditions or hazards ahead, such as curves, intersections, pedestrian crossings, or changes in road width, so you can slow down and drive with extra caution.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to affect your driving ability?
options: a:Two,b:Three,c:One
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment, reaction time, and coordination. Even one drink can impair your ability to drive safely, especially for inexperienced drivers or those with low tolerance. The safest choice is not to drive after drinking at all.

question: If you feel drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Pull over at the next rest area or service area to take a break.,b:Try to fight drowsiness while driving.,c:Take caffeine pills and continue driving.
note: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should get off the road as soon as it is safe and rest, or switch drivers. Fatigue greatly slows your reaction time and can cause you to fall asleep at the wheel. Caffeine or trying to fight sleep are not reliable or safe substitutes for proper rest.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you to go through a red light intersection without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection as directed by the officer.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: A police officer’s directions always override traffic signals and signs. If an officer directs you to proceed through a red light, you should carefully follow the officer’s instructions, yielding as necessary to avoid conflicts, even though the signal is red.

question: When must you stop at an intersection?
options: a:When facing a flashing red light.,b:When facing a steady yellow light.,c:When seeing a yellow arrow.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians in all directions, and proceed only when it is safe.

question: What is the purpose of work zone barriers, drums, cones and signs?
options: a:To make drivers go faster.,b:To inconvenience drivers.,c:To mark parking for workers.,d:To keep traffic out of hazardous work areas.
note: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to guide traffic safely around or through construction areas and to separate drivers from workers and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street, you should begin the turn from:
options: a:Any lane as long as it's clear.,b:The lane closest to the left curb.,c:The lane in the center of the road.,d:The rightmost lane.
note: When turning left from a one-way street onto another one-way street, you should start from the lane closest to the left curb and turn into a lawful lane on the new street, usually the left lane.

question: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.,b:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,c:Flash your lights.
note: If a pedestrian starts to cross in front of your vehicle, you must slow down and be prepared to stop. Drivers are required to yield to pedestrians in crosswalks and must not try to pass in front of them or signal them with lights in a way that could confuse or endanger them.

question: A circular road sign typically warns drivers about what?
options: a:A school zone.,b:A no-passing area.,c:An upcoming railroad crossing.
note: Circular (round) warning signs are used exclusively to indicate an upcoming railroad crossing so drivers can slow down, look, and listen for trains.

question: Which traffic signal instructs drivers to slow down and proceed with caution?
options: a:A flashing red light.,b:A solid yellow light.,c:A flashing yellow light.
note: A flashing yellow light means you must slow down and proceed through the intersection with caution, watching carefully for other vehicles and pedestrians. You do not have to stop, but you must be prepared to stop if the situation requires it.

question: Which of these affect the impact of alcohol on a person?
options: a:The amount of food in the stomach,b:All of the above,c:How much time passes between drinks
note: The way alcohol affects you depends on several factors, including how much food is in your stomach and how much time passes between drinks. Food slows alcohol absorption, and more time between drinks allows your body to process alcohol. Because both listed factors influence intoxication, the correct choice is the one that includes all of them.

question: If the vehicle ahead is driven distractedly with one hand and talking, you should:
options: a:Try to pass immediately.,b:Give that vehicle extra space and be prepared for unexpected moves.,c:Follow their example and talk to your passenger.
note: When you see a distracted driver, increase your following distance and be ready for sudden stops, lane changes, or drifting. Giving extra space reduces your risk if they make an unexpected move. Do not copy their behavior or rush to pass if it is not clearly safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unsafe or illegal on an interstate?
options: a:Slower traffic keeping to the right.,b:Missing your exit and continuing to the next one.,c:Changing lanes without signaling.
note: On interstates, slower traffic should keep right, and if you miss your exit you must continue to the next one rather than stop or back up. Changing lanes without signaling is unsafe and illegal because other drivers need advance warning of your movements to avoid collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver's left arm and hand extended upward signals what?
options: a:Intends to stop.,b:Intends to turn right.,c:Plans to turn left.
note: Hand signals are used when turn signals are not working or are hard to see. A left arm straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at the elbow means a right turn, and a left arm bent downward means slowing or stopping. So a left arm and hand extended upward indicates a right turn.

question: If you park facing uphill on a street with a curb, how should you position the front wheels?
options: a:Leave the front wheels straight.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking facing uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and let the vehicle roll back gently until the tire rests against the curb. If the brakes fail, the curb will stop the car and keep it from rolling into traffic.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is true?
options: a:Any prescription drug is safe to use if you do not feel drowsy.,b:Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.,c:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
note: Many drugs can affect your ability to drive safely, including prescription and over‑the‑counter medicines. They can cause drowsiness, blurred vision, slowed reaction time, or poor judgment. You must always read labels and follow medical advice before driving after taking any medication.

question: How should a lap belt fit when correctly adjusted?
options: a:Is loose.,b:Is buckled snugly across your hip bones and low on your hips.,c:Is hidden beneath the seat.
note: A lap belt should be worn low and snug across the hips and pelvic bones, not across the soft part of the abdomen. Keeping the belt low on the hips helps the strong bones absorb crash forces and reduces the risk of internal injuries.

question: At a railroad crossing, what should you be especially aware of?
options: a:That crossings are always clear at night.,b:That you may drive faster than posted limits to clear the tracks.,c:That vehicles like school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials may be required to stop.,d:That you need only look in one direction.
note: Certain vehicles, such as school buses and trucks carrying hazardous materials, must stop at all railroad crossings. You should be prepared for these stops and always approach tracks cautiously, looking and listening for trains in both directions.

question: How far must you stay behind an active snowplow with its red or amber lights on (on roads posted 35 mph or more)?
options: a:At least 400 feet.,b:At least 300 feet.,c:At least 200 feet.
note: On roads with speed limits of 35 mph or higher, you must stay well back from a working snowplow with its red or amber lights on. Remaining at least 200 feet behind helps you avoid flying snow and debris, gives the plow room to work, and reduces the risk of a collision in low‑visibility conditions.

question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Stare at the driver as they pass.,b:Speed up to prevent them from passing.,c:Try to get out of their way and avoid confrontation.,d:Brake-check them to teach a lesson.
note: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, the safest response is to stay calm, avoid eye contact or gestures, and, when it is safe, move over or change lanes to let them pass. Do not speed up, brake-check, or engage with them, because that can escalate road rage and increase the risk of a crash.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto a crowded freeway, what should you do?
options: a:Use the acceleration lane to match the speed of traffic and check mirrors and blind spots before merging.,b:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Enter traffic without adjusting your speed because you have the right-of-way.
note: When merging onto a freeway, use the acceleration lane to reach a speed close to that of freeway traffic, check your mirrors and blind spots, and yield to vehicles already on the freeway. Do not stop at the end of the ramp unless absolutely necessary, and do not assume you have the right-of-way; you must merge only when there is a safe gap.

question: When parking facing uphill on a road without a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn them away from the edge of the road (to the left).,b:Keep the wheels straight ahead.,c:Turn them toward the edge of the road (to the right).
note: When parking facing uphill without a curb, turn your front wheels toward the edge of the road (to the right). If the vehicle rolls, it will move away from the roadway instead of into traffic. With a curb and uphill, you turn the wheels away from the curb; without a curb, you turn them toward the edge.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid collisions with vehicles in your blind spots you should:
options: a:Adjust your mirrors every few minutes.,b:Honk your horn before changing lanes.,c:Turn your head and glance quickly over the shoulder in the direction of the move before changing lanes.
note: Mirrors do not show everything around your vehicle; each side has a blind spot. Before changing lanes, signal, check your mirrors, and then quickly look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move to be sure the blind spot is clear. Do not rely only on mirrors or on honking the horn.

question: If the roadway ahead is filled with heavy smoke, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your high beams and continue carefully.,b:Reduce speed and be prepared to pull completely off the road and stop if visibility is severely limited.,c:Turn on your four-way flashers and keep driving.
note: If you encounter heavy smoke that severely limits visibility, slow down immediately and be prepared to pull completely off the roadway, stop, and turn on your hazard lights. Driving into dense smoke at normal speed is extremely dangerous because you may not see stopped vehicles, obstacles, or changes in the road until it is too late.

question: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Switch your lights to high beams.,b:Turn your lights on and off rapidly.,c:Glance toward the right edge of the road.
note: If oncoming headlights blind you at night, do not stare into the lights or switch to high beams. Instead, briefly glance toward the right edge of your lane and use the road edge or lane line as a guide with your peripheral vision until the vehicle passes. This helps you maintain lane position while reducing glare.

question: Is it ever acceptable to drive around or under a lowering or raising railroad crossing gate?
options: a:No — never drive around or under a moving gate.,b:If your vehicle can do so without damaging the gate.,c:Only if an approaching train is not too close.
note: You must never drive around, under, or through a railroad crossing gate while it is lowering, raising, or down. Flashing lights, bells, and gates mean a train is approaching, and trains cannot stop quickly. Always stop and wait until the lights stop flashing and the gates are fully raised before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What does a double solid yellow centerline mean on a two-lane road?
options: a:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is not permitted for either direction.,b:Lanes move in opposite directions and passing is permitted when safe.,c:Lanes move in the same direction and passing is prohibited.
note: A double solid yellow centerline separates traffic moving in opposite directions and means passing is not allowed for vehicles traveling in either direction. You may cross these lines only to make a left turn or to enter/exit a driveway or side road when it is safe and legal, but not to pass another vehicle.

question: If you encounter a deep puddle ahead, you should:
options: a:Speed up to reduce splash.,b:Shift into neutral and continue.,c:Maintain posted speed to get through.,d:Avoid it if possible.
note: Deep puddles can cause hydroplaning, loss of steering control, and hidden hazards like potholes. If you can safely avoid a deep puddle, do so. If you must drive through water, slow down, proceed cautiously, and keep a steady speed to maintain traction and control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you treat traffic signs and pavement markings?
options: a:You must follow them only at night.,b:They are only suggestions.,c:They must always be obeyed.,d:You may ignore them when traffic is light.
note: Traffic signs, signals, and pavement markings are legal controls that regulate, warn, and guide drivers. You must obey them at all times, regardless of time of day or how light traffic is, unless directed otherwise by a police officer or authorized person.

question: When does your stopping distance increase?
options: a:On paved highways.,b:On wet or icy roads.,c:When driving at night only.
note: Stopping distance increases whenever traction is reduced, such as on wet, icy, snowy, or loose gravel roads. With less grip, your tires need more distance to slow and stop safely, so you must reduce speed and increase following distance.

question: When a traffic light turns yellow, what should drivers do?
options: a:Continue driving.,b:Slow to a stop.,c:Accelerate to avoid a red light.
note: A steady yellow light means the signal is about to turn red. You should slow down and stop if you can do so safely before entering the intersection. Only continue through if you are too close to stop safely when the light turns yellow; you should never speed up to beat the red light.

question: When must you obey instructions from school crossing guards?
options: a:Only if you see children present.,b:Only during school hours.,c:At all times.
note: You must always obey school crossing guards when they are on duty directing traffic or pedestrians. Their instructions have the same legal force as traffic control devices and help protect children and other pedestrians in the crossing area.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When parking uphill on a street that has a curb, how should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.,b:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.,c:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn your front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will touch the curb and stop the car from rolling into traffic.

question: As you near the top of a hill, what should you do?
options: a:Prepare to stop if necessary and reduce speed.,b:Speed up slightly to crest the hill.,c:Maintain the exact same speed without scanning ahead.
note: As you approach the top of a hill, slow down, cover the brake, and be prepared to stop. Your view of oncoming traffic, stopped vehicles, pedestrians, or obstacles beyond the crest is limited, so reducing speed gives you more time and space to react safely.

question: An orange and red triangular emblem on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,b:A wide load.,c:A slow-moving vehicle.,d:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange and red triangular emblem is the standard slow-moving vehicle symbol. It warns that the vehicle usually travels at 25 mph or less, such as farm equipment or animal-drawn carts, so you should be prepared to slow down.

question: If a traffic signal shows a green arrow and a red light, you may:
options: a:Wait for a steady green light before moving.,b:Drive straight ahead only.,c:Proceed in any direction you choose.,d:Only proceed in the direction indicated by the green arrow.
note: A green arrow means you have a protected movement only in the direction of the arrow, even if other signals are red. You may turn or proceed only where the arrow points, and only if the intersection is clear and it is safe.

question: Why should you avoid following other cars too closely?
options: a:You may not have time to stop if the vehicle in front of you slows or stops suddenly.,b:You may not see the vehicle's turn signals.,c:You may not see the road between the cars.
note: Following too closely, or tailgating, is dangerous because you may not have enough time or distance to react if the vehicle ahead slows or stops suddenly. Keeping a safe following distance gives you room to brake smoothly and avoid rear-end collisions.

question: What does a broken yellow line alongside a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Both directions may pass.,b:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,c:Traffic next to the broken line may pass; traffic next to the solid line may not.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means passing is allowed only for traffic on the side of the broken line and prohibited for traffic on the side of the solid line. Any passing must still be done only when it is safe and legal.

question: After stopping for a school bus unloading children, what should you do before moving on?
options: a:Watch for children walking along the side of the road and proceed cautiously.,b:Do not proceed until the children wave to you.,c:Accelerate quickly to get past the bus.
note: After stopping for a school bus with red lights flashing and stop arm extended, you must remain stopped until the signals are turned off. When you are allowed to proceed, move slowly and watch carefully for children who may be walking near or crossing the road.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a narrow road when meeting oncoming traffic, what should you provide?
options: a:Allow the oncoming vehicle at least one-half of the main-traveled portion of the road.,b:Demand the other vehicle pull over.,c:Pull completely off the road and stop.
note: On narrow two‑way roads, each driver must share the roadway so that both vehicles can pass safely. You are required to allow the oncoming vehicle at least one‑half of the main‑traveled portion of the road; you do not have the right to demand the other driver pull over. Only pull completely off the road if needed for safety and if it can be done safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If stopped by a police officer, how should you behave?
options: a:Stay in your vehicle with hands visible on the steering wheel and wait for the officer to approach.,b:Unbuckle and roll down the window immediately.,c:Get out of the vehicle and meet the officer on the road.
note: Remain in your vehicle with hands visible and wait until the officer asks for documents or further action.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to turn left on red?
options: a:Only when you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street after stopping.,b:When you are on a two-way street turning onto another two-way street.,c:Whenever no other traffic is present.,d:Only when a sign permits it without stopping.
note: After a full stop, left turns on red are allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs prohibit it.

question: What does a solid yellow traffic arrow indicate when displayed steadily?
options: a:It is never used as a traffic signal.,b:It has the same meaning as a circular yellow light — prepare to stop.,c:Drivers may turn in the direction indicated by the arrow.
note: A solid yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending; treat it like a yellow light and prepare to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
