question: On a two-lane, two-way street, what must be true before you attempt to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Your vehicle must be capable of the speed necessary to pass.,b:You must be able to return to your lane before meeting oncoming traffic only.,c:You must be able to clearly see the road ahead and complete the pass before meeting oncoming traffic.
note: You can only pass when you can clearly see far enough ahead to complete the maneuver safely and return to your lane before encountering oncoming traffic.

question: When is highway pavement especially treacherous and slippery?
options: a:If it has been raining several hours.,b:If it has just begun to rain.,c:If it has been raining for one to two hours.
note: Highway pavement is most slippery right after rain begins. Oil, grease, and dirt that have built up on the dry road mix with the first water and create a slick film. After it has rained for a while, much of this residue is washed away and traction generally improves, though you should still drive carefully in wet conditions.

question: What effect does alcohol have on driving ability?
options: a:It improves coordination.,b:It increases alertness.,c:It wakes you up.,d:It slows reflexes and reaction time.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that slows brain and nervous system activity. It reduces your ability to judge situations, slows your reflexes and reaction time, and harms coordination and vision. Even small amounts can make you less able to respond quickly and safely to traffic conditions.

question: In what ways can alcohol affect you?
options: a:It only affects balance.,b:It improves judgment and reaction time.,c:It slows reaction time.
note: Alcohol affects many parts of your driving ability. It slows reaction time, dulls judgment, reduces coordination, and can blur or distort vision. Because your brain processes information more slowly, you are less able to respond quickly to hazards or make safe decisions in traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is unlawful when passing another vehicle?
options: a:Passing when the vehicle ahead is turning left if it can be done safely and legally.,b:Passing in marked no-passing zones or over railroad crossings.,c:Passing on the right only when it is permitted, safe, and you stay on the paved roadway.
note: Passing is illegal and unsafe in marked no‑passing zones and at or near railroad crossings because your view and escape paths are limited and unexpected hazards can appear. You may pass a vehicle turning left if you can do so safely and legally, and passing on the right is allowed only when conditions and markings clearly permit it and you do not leave the paved roadway.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, cough syrups, and some cold medications.,b:Only illegal drugs.,c:Only alcohol.,d:Caffeine in coffee.
note: Many substances can make you an unsafe driver, including tranquilizers, marijuana, sedatives, some prescription drugs, and even certain cough syrups and cold medicines. These can cause drowsiness, slow reactions, and affect judgment. Always read labels and talk to your doctor or pharmacist before driving after taking any medication.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a hill or curve.,b:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: You may pass another vehicle only when the centerline next to your lane is a broken line and you can complete the pass safely. You must not pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view is blocked, and you must not cross a solid line next to your lane to pass.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When making a right turn on a green light, what is required of you?
options: a:You must yield to pedestrians and other traffic in the intersection before turning.,b:Maintain your normal speed and complete the turn quickly.,c:Stop and wait for a flashing pedestrian signal before turning.
note: When turning right on a green light, you may proceed if a right turn is allowed, but you must first yield to pedestrians in the crosswalk and to any traffic already in or approaching the intersection closely enough to be a hazard.

question: If stopped and an officer suspects you have been drinking, are you allowed to refuse a chemical BAC test in Wisconsin?
options: a:Yes — you may refuse, but refusal will result in penalties such as license revocation.,b:Yes — you may refuse only if you have a valid medical reason documented by a doctor.,c:No — under Wisconsin's implied consent law you are legally required to submit to testing, and refusal carries its own penalties.
note: Under Wisconsin’s implied consent law, by driving you have already agreed to chemical testing if lawfully arrested for OWI. You can physically refuse the test, but that refusal is itself a violation and leads to penalties such as license revocation and other consequences. Legally, you are required to submit to the test when properly requested.

question: How is a driver's license classified under the law?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Right,c:Privilege
note: A driver’s license is considered a privilege, not a guaranteed right. The state can set requirements for getting and keeping a license, and it can suspend or revoke that privilege if you violate traffic laws or drive unsafely.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Only coordination.,c:Only alertness.,d:Only vision.
note: Alcohol and many drugs affect several driving abilities at once. They reduce alertness, slow reaction time, and harm coordination, judgment, and concentration, which makes it much harder to control the vehicle and respond to hazards.

question: Before backing out of a driveway near children playing, what should you do?
options: a:Walk to the rear of the vehicle to be sure the way is clear.,b:Sound your horn to warn the children.,c:Rev the engine to alert them.
note: Before backing where children may be present, walk to the rear and check the area so you can see any child, toy, or obstacle that may be too low to appear in mirrors or cameras. Only back up after you are sure the path is completely clear.

question: Why is it important to be especially alert for motorcycles?
options: a:Motorcyclists are less skilled than other drivers.,b:They rarely use headlights.,c:They are more difficult to see than cars.
note: Motorcycles are smaller and narrower than cars, so they are easier to overlook in mirrors, blind spots, and at intersections. Because they are harder to see and their speed and distance can be difficult to judge, drivers must look carefully for motorcycles and check blind spots before changing lanes or turning.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Stay in the same lane and pass quickly.,b:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,c:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move over.
note: When passing a motorcycle, treat it like any other vehicle and give it a full lane. Move completely into the left lane before and during the pass, and do not try to share a lane side‑by‑side with a motorcycle.

question: Which of the following can impair a person's ability to drive?
options: a:Alcohol.,b:A lack of sleep.,c:All of the above.,d:Any medication.
note: Driving can be impaired by alcohol, many prescription or over‑the‑counter medications, illegal drugs, and even fatigue or lack of sleep. Any of these can slow your reactions, affect judgment, and reduce coordination, so you must be cautious about driving when using substances or when you are very tired.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do regarding the brakes?
options: a:Brake lightly.,b:Brake abruptly.,c:Stay off the brakes.
note: If your vehicle begins to skid and you do not have ABS, ease off the accelerator and brake gently if you need to slow down; hard or abrupt braking can lock the wheels and make the skid worse. With ABS, press the brake pedal firmly and steer where you want to go while the system pulses the brakes for you.

question: Which of the following does NOT occur after drinking alcohol?
options: a:Your judgment of speed and distance is distorted.,b:You have reduced ability to recover from glare.,c:You become less alert.,d:Your reflexes and reaction time speed up.
note: Alcohol slows your reflexes and reaction time, makes you less alert, and distorts your judgment of speed and distance. It also reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare. It never speeds up your reactions, so the statement that your reflexes and reaction time speed up is the one that does NOT occur after drinking.

question: What is the best steering and braking approach when driving in bad weather?
options: a:Drive in a low gear at all times.,b:Brake and steer smoothly to maintain control.,c:Steer off the road immediately.
note: In bad weather, traction is reduced, so you should brake and steer smoothly and gradually. Sudden braking, acceleration, or sharp steering can cause skids and loss of control. Use gentle inputs and increase following distance to stay safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who proceeds first?
options: a:The driver who sounds their horn first.,b:The driver who arrives first.,c:The driver who arrives last.
note: At a four‑way stop, the vehicle that comes to a complete stop first has the right‑of‑way and should proceed first when safe. If two or more vehicles stop at the same time, the driver on the right goes first. Using the horn or arriving last does not give you the right‑of‑way.

question: Which of the following describes a work zone?
options: a:Is marked with black and white signs.,b:May be moving or stationary.,c:Does not require a driver to slow down and pay extra attention.
note: Work zones can be stationary, like a fixed construction site, or moving, such as line‑painting or mowing operations. They are typically marked with orange signs and devices, and drivers must slow down, be prepared for sudden stops, and pay extra attention to workers and equipment.

question: If the rear of your vehicle begins to skid to the left, which steering action corrects it?
options: a:Turn the steering wheel to the left (steer into the skid).,b:Do not turn the steering wheel at all.,c:Turn the steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: If the rear of your vehicle skids left, you should steer left—into the direction of the skid—while easing off the accelerator. This helps realign the vehicle with your intended path. Avoid slamming on the brakes; if you have ABS, apply firm, steady pressure while continuing to steer in the direction you want the front of the car to go.

question: When approaching a railroad crossing and you do not see or hear a train, in which of these situations must you stop?
options: a:If a crossing gate is lowered.,b:Any of the above,c:If a stop sign is posted.,d:If the crossing lights are flashing.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing any time a crossing gate is lowered, the red lights are flashing, or a stop sign requires you to stop, even if you do not see or hear a train. These controls mean a train may be approaching or is nearby, and you must obey them for safety.

question: When must you stop at a railroad crossing?
options: a:When directed by a flagger or stop sign, or when flashing red signals and gates are operating.,b:Only when you see a train.,c:Only at crossings with no signs.,d:Only if you are in a large vehicle.
note: You must stop at a railroad crossing when a flagger or stop sign directs you to stop, or when flashing red lights and/or gates indicate a train is approaching. Never proceed until you are sure it is safe and legal to cross.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You must not drive faster than:
options: a:A speed that feels comfortable to you.,b:The maximum speed limit only.,c:A speed that is reasonable and prudent for existing conditions.
note: You must always adjust your speed to be reasonable and prudent for current conditions, even if that means driving slower than the posted speed limit. Factors like rain, fog, heavy traffic, or poor road surfaces may require you to reduce speed to stay safe.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what should be your first reaction?
options: a:Swerve into the next lane immediately.,b:Take your foot off the gas to create space.,c:Honk and brake hard.
note: If another vehicle suddenly pulls in front of you, the safest first response is to ease off the accelerator to increase your following distance. This creates more space and time to react without making sudden swerves or hard braking that could cause a collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: On a short entrance ramp without an acceleration lane, you must look for a safe gap in interstate traffic and then accelerate on the ramp so you can merge at or near the speed of traffic. Do not drive on the shoulder to gain speed, and do not merge immediately if there is no safe gap.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on a multilane highway, what should you do first?
options: a:Be sure the passing lane is clear.,b:Always pass only on the right.,c:Ignore turn signals from other vehicles.
note: On a multilane highway, you must first make sure the lane you want to move into is clear before you pass. Check mirrors and blind spots, confirm there is enough space, then signal and change lanes to pass safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If your vehicle's turn signals stop working, what should you use to show a turn?
options: a:Your headlights.,b:Your horn.,c:Hand signals.
note: If your electrical turn signals fail, you are still required to signal turns and lane changes. Use standard hand and arm signals so other drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians can anticipate your movements.

question: How should you respond to a flashing red traffic signal at an intersection?
options: a:Slow down and yield the right-of-way.,b:Come to a complete stop, yield, and go when safe.,c:Slow down and proceed without stopping.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for cross traffic and pedestrians, yield the right-of-way as needed, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: If a fire engine is following you but not using its emergency signals, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to clear the way.,b:Continue driving in a normal manner.,c:Stop as quickly as you can.
note: You are required to yield and pull over only when an emergency vehicle is using its lights and/or siren. If a fire engine is behind you without emergency signals, simply continue driving normally and obey all traffic laws.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what should you expect?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as drivers. To make a left turn, a bicyclist may move into the appropriate left-turn lane or left side of the lane, just like a motor vehicle, when it is safe to do so.

question: If you feel fatigued while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Find a safe place to park and take a short nap.,b:Open all windows and drive faster.,c:Increase radio volume and keep driving.,d:Keep driving but reduce speed.
note: Signs of fatigue include drifting lanes and struggling to keep eyes open; stop in a safe area and rest rather than continuing to drive.

question: How should you drive through a construction zone to avoid causing congestion by slowing to look?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Decrease your following distance to get through faster.,c:Pass the construction area carefully and avoid “rubbernecking.”
note: In construction zones, your job is to move through safely and steadily, not to watch the work. Slowing down just to look at workers or equipment (“rubbernecking”) creates congestion and increases crash risk. Follow posted work-zone speeds, maintain a safe following distance, and keep your attention on the road and traffic while passing carefully.

question: If you are involved in an accident, what should you do at or near the scene?
options: a:Stop your vehicle at or near the scene and avoid standing in traffic lanes.,b:Leave the scene if damage seems minor.,c:Keep the ignition on for wrecked vehicles.
note: After a collision, you are legally required to stop at or near the scene. If possible, move vehicles out of traffic, turn off ignitions to reduce fire risk, and stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit by passing cars. Never leave the scene, even if damage seems minor.

question: When parking uphill next to a curb, what should you do after setting the parking brake?
options: a:Keep the front tires straight ahead.,b:Turn your steering wheel away from the curb.,c:Keep the rear tires against the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the front wheels away from the curb and set the parking brake. If the vehicle rolls, the back of the front tire will move gently into the curb and stop the car, helping prevent it from rolling into traffic.

question: If dust or smoke reduces your ability to see other vehicles, what should you do?
options: a:Turn on your emergency flashers but keep driving at the same speed.,b:Turn on your parking lights only.,c:Slow down and turn on your headlights.
note: In dust, smoke, or any condition that reduces visibility, you should slow down and turn on your headlights (low beams) so you can see and be seen. Parking lights alone are not bright enough for driving, and keeping your speed while visibility is poor greatly increases the chance of a collision.

question: Why is night driving generally more difficult than daytime driving?
options: a:Visibility is reduced in the dark.,b:Cars are more likely to overheat.,c:It is always raining at night.,d:Headlights improve peripheral vision at night.
note: Visibility is reduced at night because headlights illuminate only a limited area and your peripheral vision is less effective in the dark. You must slow down so you can stop within the distance you can see ahead with your headlights.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line indicate?
options: a:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,b:Passing is permitted only from the direction next to the dashed line.,c:Passing is permitted from both directions.
note: A dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line means only the traffic on the side with the dashed line may pass when safe. The side next to the solid line must not cross it to pass.

question: At an intersection with a flashing red light, how should you proceed?
options: a:Stop only if vehicles are already in the intersection.,b:Stop only if other cars are approaching.,c:Come to a full stop and go when it is safe.
note: A flashing red light is treated the same as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, yield to any traffic or pedestrians with the right of way, and then proceed only when it is safe.

question: A solid white line between lanes moving in the same direction means:
options: a:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are permitted to pass when it is safe to do so.,b:Lanes are moving in opposite directions and drivers are not permitted to pass.,c:Lanes are moving in the same direction and drivers are not permitted to pass.
note: A solid white line between lanes going in the same direction means lane changes are discouraged and sometimes prohibited. You should stay in your lane unless you must change and it is clearly safe and legal to do so.

question: When may you legally cross double solid yellow lines?
options: a:To pass a slow-moving truck.,b:To turn into a driveway or make a permitted left turn.,c:To pass another car.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and generally may not be crossed to pass. You may cross them only to make a left turn into or out of a driveway or side road, to make a permitted U‑turn, or to enter or exit the roadway when allowed. You may not cross double solid yellow lines just to pass a slower vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You arrive at a 4-way stop at the same time as a driver on your left. Who has the right of way?
options: a:The driver on your left, because they were there first,b:You have the right of way — the driver to your left must yield to you,c:Whoever signals first proceeds first,d:The driver going straight always has priority
note: At a 4-way stop when two vehicles arrive simultaneously, the driver to the RIGHT has the right of way. Since the other driver is to your LEFT, you are to their right — meaning you have the right of way and should proceed first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to pass on a two-lane road, what should be your primary check?
options: a:Judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles.,b:Flash your headlights as you pass.,c:Sound your horn as you pass.,d:Assume oncoming traffic will slow down.
note: Before passing on a two-lane road, your main concern is whether there is enough clear space ahead in the oncoming lane. Carefully judge the distance and speed of oncoming vehicles and only begin passing if you are sure you can complete the maneuver and return to your lane without forcing any other driver to slow or swerve.

question: On which road marking may you legally pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken center line next to your lane means you may pass when it is safe. A solid line next to your lane means you must not pass, and you should never pass on hills, curves, or anywhere your view of oncoming traffic is limited.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, you should move back into your original lane when:
options: a:You have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,b:You can see the passed vehicle’s headlights in your rearview mirror.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.,d:The passing vehicle signals you to move over.
note: After passing, do not move back into your original lane until you can see the front of the vehicle you passed (its headlights in the daytime or at night) in your rearview mirror. This ensures you have enough space ahead and do not cut off the other driver.

question: What do blue traffic signs generally indicate?
options: a:Regulatory requirements like speed limits.,b:Mileage distances to locations.,c:Construction and maintenance warnings.,d:Information on motorist services (rest areas, hospitals, food).
note: Blue traffic signs are service signs. They give information about motorist services such as rest areas, gas stations, food, lodging, and hospitals along the roadway.

question: When entering a freeway, how should you check traffic to merge safely?
options: a:Using your side mirror and looking over your shoulder.,b:Using only your rearview mirror.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors without looking over your shoulder.
note: Before merging onto a freeway, use your mirrors and then look over your shoulder to check your blind spot. This helps you see vehicles that are not visible in your mirrors so you can choose a safe gap and merge smoothly.

question: If a child is about to run into the street, what should you do?
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn while being prepared to stop.,b:Flash your headlights.,c:Continue at the same speed.
note: If a child appears ready to run into the street, immediately cover the brake and be prepared to stop while giving a sharp blast of your horn to warn the child and others nearby. Use the horn to alert, but your primary responsibility is to slow or stop to avoid a collision.

question: What must you do when approaching a pedestrian who uses a guide dog or white cane?
options: a:Honk so they know to clear the way.,b:Swerve quickly around them.,c:Yield the right-of-way.
note: Stop and give the blind pedestrian the right-of-way; do not honk or attempt to steer around them abruptly.

question: Alcohol is classified as which type of substance?
options: a:A depressant.,b:A stimulant.,c:An antihistamine.
note: Alcohol is a central nervous system depressant. It slows brain activity and impairs judgment, coordination, and reaction time, making it dangerous to drive after drinking.

question: Any amount of alcohol in your blood may affect which abilities?
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge.
note: Any amount of alcohol can affect your judgment and physical coordination, even if you do not feel drunk. Because driving requires quick decisions and precise control, even small amounts of alcohol can make driving unsafe.

question: When is using your horn appropriate?
options: a:When it may help prevent a collision.,b:When another driver makes a mistake.,c:When another vehicle is in your way and you want them to move.
note: Use your horn only to alert others to a potential collision or to warn of immediate danger. Do not use it to show anger, impatience, or to punish other drivers for mistakes.

question: At a crosswalk, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Construction workers must yield to you.,b:You must yield to pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must yield to you.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks, whether marked or unmarked, when pedestrians are in or approaching your lane. Always be prepared to stop for people crossing the street.

question: What does a green arrow signal require you to do?
options: a:Proceed immediately without yielding.,b:Ignore any pedestrians in the intersection.,c:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,d:Yield to vehicles, bicyclists, and pedestrians in the intersection, then complete the turn.
note: A green arrow gives you a protected movement in the direction of the arrow, but you must still yield to any vehicles, bicyclists, or pedestrians already in the intersection before you complete your turn.

question: Why is winter driving more hazardous than other seasons?
options: a:There are increased hours of darkness.,b:Road conditions can be affected by freezing temperatures, ice, snow, and fog.,c:Both of the above.
note: Winter driving is more dangerous because there are more hours of darkness and road surfaces can become slippery or obscured by ice, snow, and fog. These conditions reduce traction and visibility, requiring slower speeds and greater following distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What general attitude should a driver have about right-of-way rules?
options: a:Assume most drivers obey the right-of-way rules.,b:Always be prepared to yield the right-of-way.,c:Assume all drivers automatically obey the right-of-way rules.
note: Right-of-way laws say who should go first, but they do not guarantee that others will follow them. Safe drivers always stay ready to yield, even when they legally have the right-of-way, if yielding will prevent a collision.

question: When you see a school crossing sign, what should you do?
options: a:Always sound your horn when you see children.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always stop, whether there is a stop sign or not.
note: A school crossing sign warns that children may be crossing the road. You should slow down, scan carefully for children, and be prepared to stop if they are in or near the crosswalk. You do not automatically stop unless required by a stop sign, signal, or pedestrians in the crosswalk.

question: If a tire blows out suddenly while you're driving, what steps should you take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and exit the traffic lane slowly.,b:Pump the brakes rapidly to stop quickly.,c:Brake hard and steer immediately to the right edge.,d:Turn on your hazards and speed up to reach the shoulder faster.
note: When a tire blows out, the car may pull to one side. Hold the steering wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, and let the vehicle slow down. Once it is under control and speed has dropped, steer gradually off the road and brake gently if needed. Sudden hard braking or sharp steering can cause loss of control.

question: When ridden on public roadways, bicycles are legally classified as:
options: a:Pedestrians.,b:Vehicles.,c:Hazards.,d:Motor vehicles.
note: Bicycles ridden on public roads are treated as vehicles. Cyclists must obey traffic signals, signs, lane markings, and right‑of‑way rules just like drivers of cars, including stopping at red lights and stop signs and riding in the same direction as traffic.
